###### Findings verified in the code, not assumed

- **The dump is never written.** Every write the launcher performs goes to `LocalState`: `bbport.ini`,
  `Prepared\boot-linked.bin` / `content.bin` / `eboot.elf` / `app_ver.txt` / `format.txt` /
  `patches.bin` / `overlay\*` / `overlay.json`, the crash quarantine file and `dozen.log`. There is no
  `bb_uwp_mkdir`/`CreateFile2FromAppW` call against the game or update folder anywhere in
  `xbox/platform/main.cpp`, which is what makes the "USB dump byte-identical" acceptance testable
  with a SHA-256 of both folders before and after.
- **The update is not copied.** `BuildOverlayedImage` copies only the boot container (`eboot.bin`,
  `sce_sys\param.sfo`, `sce_module\*.prx` and other root/`sce_*` files) — a handful of megabytes — and
  writes every other path the update provides into `Prepared\overlay\files.txt`, which
  `bb_uwp_overlay_configure()` turns into a redirect in the platform file layer. A 10 GB
  `dvdroot_ps4` never lands in `LocalState`.
- **01.09 is written down once.** `kPatchTargetVersion` in `xbox/platform/sfo_version.h` is the only
  definition (8 uses in non-test code); the string `"01.09"` appears elsewhere only in two comments in
  `prepare_game.h`. A future 01.10 update changes one line.
- **The launcher text has one source.** Every sentence in a dialog and every summary line in
  `loader.log.txt` comes from `xbox/platform/dump_panel.h`; `main.cpp` only wraps it in
  `MessageDialog`/`printf`. That is why the three states can be pinned in CI at all.
- **No new capabilities.** The patch folder is remembered through the same
  `StorageApplicationPermissions::FutureAccessList` token mechanism as the game folder (token `patch`,
  redeemed into `g_patch_folder_lease`), so `runFullTrust`/`broadFileSystemAccess` stay absent and
  `check-imports.ps1` still passes.

##### Crash after character creation — what the PC-port reports translate to

The same crash is a well-documented PC problem. Screened against this codebase, one of the community's
reported causes is a **verbatim match**, one is **already implemented here**, and the rest are N/A.

| PC cause / community fix | Status in this port |
| --- | --- |
| `avplayer_source.h:48 Assertion Failed! Could not allocate frame buffer` — crash on the first movie after creation; people work around it with a post-creation save or by lowering effects | **Was a real defect here.** `GuestBuffer` called `ASSERT_MSG(m_data, ...)`, so a failed guest allocation aborted the process (dashboard crash) instead of failing the stream. **Fixed.** |
| Enable GPU readbacks, or disable FaceGen (vertex explosions / stale vertices) | **Already implemented**: `EmulatorSettings.GetReadbacksMode()` defaults to `Relaxed` (`gpu/shim/core/emulator_settings.h`), honoured by `RegionManager::InvalidateRegion` / `ForEachModifiedRange`. No FaceGen patch needed. |
| Out of device memory (`ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory`), 4 GB VRAM, RAM spikes | Still the dominant risk for us: Test #11 died at `4135/5120 MiB`. The `AppMemoryUsage` work (GC at frame boundaries, dense-arena retirement, `/STACK:8388608,65536`) is the equivalent of their "RAM spike workaround" mods. |
| `SDL_audiocvt.c ConvertAudio` buffer overrun / LibAtrac9 overflow on the cutscene audio | **N/A**: audio is FFmpeg + `XAudio2`; there is no SDL and no `LibAtrac9` call site in `gpu/` or `src/`. |
| Toggling patches (`Skip Intro`, 60 FPS, resolution) changes whether it crashes | Maps to our `patches/redzone.json` / `Bloodborne.xml` state: a `01.00` dump runs with `patches=skipped`, which is the configuration Test #11 crashed in. Split-dump support addresses this. |
| VBlank divider / frame-rate cap causing the load to hang | Exposed as `BB_VBLANK_HZ` / `BB_FPS_LIMIT`, not a defect. |

###### The fix (`gpu/shadps4/core/libraries/avplayer/`)

- `GuestBuffer::GuestBuffer` no longer aborts. It logs the size/align and exposes `IsValid()`.
- `AvPlayerSource::Init` allocates video and audio frame buffers one at a time, stops on the first
  refusal, and **fails the stream** (`return false`) when fewer than two are available — the count
  below which the decoder and presentation callback cannot run. The guest receives an AvPlayer error
  and keeps running, instead of the app dying on the cutscene after character creation.
- Partial allocation still plays: `N of M frame buffers allocated, playing with N`.

What to look for in `dozen.log` / `errors.log` on the next hardware run:
`Could not allocate frame buffer (… bytes, align …, texture=…)` followed by
`Video '<path>': only N of M frame buffers … could be allocated` — that is the memory-exhaustion
pressure the PC reports describe, now visible instead of fatal.

---

##### The crash after character creation, second round (`1.0.26299.2359` logs)

Test #13 ran the split dump correctly — `DumpLayout: kind=split; base_ver=01.00; patch_ver=01.09;
effective=01.09; patches=required`, `Compiled startup patches: FPS=60, ... writes=196`, then died.
The reported symptom ("exact same crash") is correct, but it is **not** the AvPlayer path fixed in
`a416e62`:

```
Texture cache: memory pressure, 4493 of 4352 MiB (critical 4672): 1 images evicted ...
GPU [Debug] <Critical> slot_vector.h:225 ValidateIndex: Assertion Failed!
SlotVector invalid or freed slot index=132 capacity=2978      (previous run: 257)
STOP: GPU library assertion failed
```

###### Cause

`Common::SlotId` is a bare `u32` index with **no generation counter**. The rasterizer resolves every
texture binding in two passes: pass 1 collects `(image_id, desc)`, pass 2 calls `GetImage(image_id)`
and `FindTexture(image_id, ...)`. Under memory pressure `InsertImage` -> `ReclaimMemoryFor` ->
`DeleteImage` frees images *between* those passes (the log line above is that eviction), so a
collected `image_id` can already be dead in pass 2. Indexing with it either trips `ValidateIndex`
(the crash seen) or, if the slot is reused first, silently binds the **wrong image**.

Two more places hold ids across an erase: `TextureCache::FindTexture`'s `ViewMemo` (kept in the
rasterizer's binding entry, which outlives the image) and `Image::last_view` / `image_view_infos`,
which keep indexes into `slot_image_views` after `DeleteImage` reset and erased those views.

###### Fix

- `TextureCache::IsImageAlive(ImageId)` — `slot_images.is_allocated`, next to the existing `TryGetImage`.
- `vk_rasterizer.cpp`, binding pass 2: re-resolve a dead id with `FindImage(desc)` (same guest
  address, so the draw stays correct and the texture is simply uploaded again) and fall back to
  `NullView()` if even that fails; the `needs_rebind` path is re-checked after it re-resolves, since
  `FindImage` can evict while resolving.
- `FindTexture`: the memoised view is only used while `slot_image_views.is_allocated(memo->view_id)`.
- `Image::FindView`: `last_view` and the `image_view_infos` search only return a view whose slot is
  still allocated; a stale list entry is overwritten with the freshly created view so the list does
  not grow without bound.

Logs to look for next run: `GPU: image binding N was evicted before it was bound; re-resolving
addr=... size=...` (at most 8 times). Those lines replacing the assertion mean the eviction race was
the cause; if `slot_vector.h:225` still fires, the id in the message tells us which container and
path, since neither `FindTexture` nor `FindView` can reach it any more.

###### Second cause: the collector freed images that were still held (this round)

The `1.0.26300.x` run stops in the same assertion, but the free that caused it is a *different* path
than the two-pass binding race above:

```
Texture cache: memory pressure, 4493 of 4352 MiB (critical 4672): 1 images evicted
slot_vector.h:225 ValidateIndex: Assertion Failed!
SlotVector invalid or freed slot index=132 capacity=2978
STOP: GPU library assertion failed
```

`GarbageCollectImages`' `clean_up` lambda decided purely on `SafeToDownload()`, `IsTiled()` and the
LRU age. It never asked whether the image was still in use, while `ReclaimMemoryFor` has always
skipped `info.scene_proxy`, `usage.vo_surface`, `binding.is_bound` and `binding.is_target`. Under
pressure (4 GB console memory) a bound render target or the video-out surface the presenter reads
could therefore be evicted, and the rasterizer / presenter / upscaler then indexed the freed slot.

The second half is that `Common::SlotId` has no generation, so even a *correctly* pinned image can be
freed later (UnmapMemory) behind a stored id: `GetImage` on it either asserts or silently returns
whichever image reused the slot.

Fix:

- `video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache_policy.h` (new, no Vulkan): `BbGpu::ImagePinState`,
  `ImagePinned`, `GcMayFreeImage`. `clean_up` now returns `false` for a pinned candidate without
  spending a deletion, and touches its LRU entry so the next pass is not stuck on the same entry.
  A `pinned` count is added to the 5-second pressure line, `gc_pinned`.
- Stale ids now carry their `image_uid`: the upscaler's `scene_color` / `ldr_target` / `ui_color` /
  `ui_depth` are stored through `Track(slot, uid, id)` and read through `Lookup(slot, uid)`
  (`TryGetImage(id, uid)`) or `LookupLive(id)` for ids owned by another component; every read site
  bails out instead of indexing. `OnDraw` also drops `color`/`depth` parameters that are already
  dead. `CameraMotion::Overlay` and `Rasterizer::ResetBindings` do the same with
  `TryGetImage(id, 0)` / `IsImageAlive`.
- `BB_GC_LOG_FREES=1` (UWP builds) traces every free with `id uid guest size bound target proxy vo
  tiled gpu_modified now`, to match a next-run assertion against the image that was freed.

Not changed: `TextureCache::UnmapMemory` still frees every image in the unmapped guest range, since
the guest really did unmap them; the holders now tolerate that instead.

How to verify: `xbox/tests/texture_cache_policy_test.cpp` (CI test, plain C++20, compiles with
`g++ -std=c++20 -I gpu/shadps4/video_core/texture_cache`) pins the policy and the uid rule. On the
console, a next log should show `pinned` in the pressure line and, with `BB_GC_LOG_FREES=1`, which
image was freed right before any remaining assertion. **This is not confirmed until it runs on a
Series S / X through character creation and into Central Yharnam.**

##### Failed attempts — original list, verbatim

This is §5 of the old handoff, kept so nothing is lost. §11 above summarises it and adds
two entries from the latest round.

Do **not** reintroduce any of the following approaches:

1. **Linking with `/STACK:16777216,16777216` (`xbox/CMakeLists.txt`)**:
   - Setting `SizeOfStackCommit = 16 MiB` in the PE header forces Windows `CreateThread` / `_beginthreadex` to commit `16 MiB` of physical RAM per OS thread (`82 × 16 MiB ≈ 1,312 MiB`), overriding `pthread_attr_setstacksize` and starving the `5,120 MiB` Series S budget. Keep `/STACK:8388608,65536`.
2. **Returning `{}` from `DrawPreparation::Build()` without gap-aware lookup/rebase (`vk_draw_prep.cpp`)**:
   - `Liverpool::SubmitGfx()` unconditionally increments `gfx_submit_seq++`. Any skipped `Build()` creates non-contiguous `seq` numbers in `submissions`, causing `submissions[next_seq - submissions.front()->seq]` in `ScannerLoop`/`WorkerLoop`/`BeginSubmission` to index out of bounds (`bloodborne.exe+0x270628`) and desynchronizing `tail_regs` deltas.
3. **Unguarded speculative guest-shader reads on `bb:DrawPrep0` (`vk_pipeline_cache.cpp` / `regs_shader.h`)**:
   - Calling `AmdGpu::GetParams(*pgm)` when `sel.worker != nullptr` dereferences guest shader memory without `runtime_fault_recover` and aborts via `UNREACHABLE_MSG` if the guest reused that page ahead of the GPU thread. Always use `runtime_fault_recover` + `AmdGpu::TryGetParams(*pgm)`.
4. **Default-constructing `Shader::ShaderParams params{}` or block-scope `extern "C"`**:
   - `Shader::ShaderParams::user_data` is `std::span<const u32, NumShaderUserData>` (fixed extent != `std::dynamic_extent`), which has no default constructor in C++20/23 (`clang-cl` error); always wrap deferred initialization in `std::optional<Shader::ShaderParams>`. Likewise, `clang-cl` rejects `extern "C"` declarations inside function bodies (`[dcl.link]/4`); keep them at namespace scope.
5. **Calling `scheduler.Finish()` inside `BufferCache::GetDenseArena()` (`xbox/graphics/dense_buffers.cpp`)**:
   - `GetDenseArena` runs inside `ObtainBuffer` -> `ResolveVertexBuffers` *after* `BeginRendering`. Calling `scheduler.Finish()` there splits and submits an active render pass mid-draw. Only call `scheduler.PopPendingOperations()` inside `GetDenseArena`, and run `scheduler.Finish(); scheduler.PopPendingOperations();` at frame boundaries inside `TextureCache::RunGarbageCollector()`.
6. **Serializing `getPipelineCacheData(*pipeline_cache)` every 32 runtime PSOs or when `num_flushed_pipelines == 0`**:
   - Allocates a temporary `~174 MiB` `std::vector<u8>` and queues a `174 MiB` SSD write mid-gameplay, pushing `AppMemoryUsage` across thresholds.
7. **Syncing `.vkcache` solely by file size (`src_size > dst_size`)**:
   - Overwrites valid local caches across Mesa Dozen rebuilds or skips valid exports when `pipelineCacheUUID` changes; always validate the 32-byte `VkPipelineCacheHeaderVersionOne` + `pipelineCacheUUID`.
8. **Keeping `if_body.pop_front()` in `GotoPass::MoveOutwardIf` or emitting `OpUnreachable` on `BB_UWP`**:
   - `if_body.splice(if_body.begin(), body, std::next(goto_stmt), body.end())` already excludes `goto_stmt`; calling `if_body.pop_front()` unlinks the empty `boost::intrusive::list` sentinel when `std::next(goto_stmt) == body.end()` (crashing shader `i = 1024`) and drops statements otherwise. Also emit `OpReturn` instead of `OpUnreachable` on `BB_UWP` because Mesa Dozen's `nir_to_dxil.c` (`emit_jump`) only handles `break`/`continue`.
9. **Single-pass `num_predecessors == 0` erasure in `CFG::RemoveUnreachableBlocks()`**:
   - Leaves unreachable loops/diamonds intact (`num_predecessors >= 1`), crashing Mesa's `vtn_cfg.c`. Always compute DFS reachability from the entry block and recompute `num_predecessors` over reachable edges only.
10. **Offline Dozen `GraphicsPipeline` pitfalls (`bb_precompile.cpp`)**:
    - Never compile color-pass `VS` standalone at `binding = 0` (`dzn_pipeline.c` `adjust_var_bindings` asserts `b < binding_count`); never leave depth-only `z_format` as `0` (`ZFormat::Invalid` skips shader compilation—use `ZFormat::Z32Float`); force `rasterizationSamples = e1` when `preloading == true`; cap VS attributes to `<= 28` (`semantic < 32`); ensure passthrough VS writes `gl_Position`; and cap `rt.hw.vs.num_outputs` to `0..3`.
11. **Relying on VEH / `signal(SIGABRT)` for static UCRT `abort()` or using `bb_longjmp` across C++ frames**:
    - Static `libucrt.lib` `abort()` executes `__fastfail` (`int 0x29`), bypassing Win32 VEH handlers. Crash-resilient precompilation must flush `LocalState\precompile_inflight.txt` before compiling and consume it on startup.
12. **Swapping `ONION`/`guest_code` memory, calling `TextureCache` GC inside VMA `createImage`, or committing after container refresh without checking `HEAD`**:
    - Restrict swap strictly to `WC_GARLIC` with fault-time guest pinning; run `TextureCache` GC only at frame boundaries outside `TextureCache::mutex`/VMA callbacks; build Mesa Dozen with MSVC `14.44` (never `19.51`, which ICEs on Mesa); never use `gh release download` in sandbox (`release-assets.githubusercontent.com` is outside the proxy allowlist); and after any container refresh, verify `git log -n 2` against `origin/arena/c39edde2-test-project` (`git fetch` + `git reset --soft origin/arena/c39edde2-test-project && git reset`) before committing.

### Appendix D — Community research and graphics-toggle audit


_Source: `docs/MEMORY_CRASH_RESEARCH.md`; historical snapshot where applicable._

#### The crash at high GiB — what the community found

Research round, 2026-10-27. Question: Bloodborne (bbport family) dies once memory use climbs into the
high-GiB range — "Texture cache: memory pressure, N of M MiB", then the GPU stops — and other people
have hit it, so what did they find?

##### 1. Somebody hit exactly this, with our log lines

`Mrsuss60/bloodborne_pc_windows_port` is a sibling of this project (same shadPS4 texture cache, same
bbport collector, same log format). Its **#75 "game crash due to vram leak (1650 super)"**, now closed,
contains this:

```
Texture cache: memory pressure, 3866 of 3729 MiB (critical 3936): 115 images evicted, 0 written back since the last report
Texture cache: memory pressure, 3878 of 3729 MiB (critical 3936): 146 images evicted, 0 written back since the last report
Texture cache: memory pressure, 3889 of 3729 MiB (critical 3936): 118 images evicted, 0 written back since the last report
GPU [Debug] <Critical> vk_platform.h:66 Check: Assertion Failed!
vk::Result=ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory
STOP: GPU library assertion failed (see GPU log above)
Process finished with code: 23
```

That is our failure: usage parked just under the critical mark, the collector evicting images every
report and freeing nothing that matters, then `ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory`. Reporters: 4 GB VRAM laptops
(RTX 3050 4 GB, GTX 1650 SUPER), RX 6600M 8 GB, all "smooth 60 FPS for 15–30 minutes, then this".

Companion issue **#69 "Unbounded VRAM/RAM accumulation during map transitions"**: "host process
footprint steadily expands by 200 MB–500 MB per zone load… VRAM increases continuously until
saturating hardware limits… eventually causing a crash with VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY".

Both were closed by **PR #89 — "gpu/texture_cache: Reclaim transient depth targets and mitigate VRAM
pressure leak"**, which changes 13 lines in `gpu/shadps4/video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache.cpp`
and states the cause precisely:

> 1. **Depth/Stencil & Shadow Maps**: GPU-modified depth attachments have `SafeToDownload() == true`
>    and `IsTiled() == true`. Because tiled downloads cannot be written back, they are **touched and
>    kept alive forever (lru_cache.Touch), locking gigabytes of VRAM**.
> 2. **Permanent Tiled Retention**: When tiled && download textures are encountered, they are never
>    freed even under active memory pressure (`pressured == true`), causing VRAM to stay pinned at the
>    pressure mark.

and the fix:

> 1. **Direct Depth Reclaim**: if `image.info.props.is_depth`, the image is a GPU-only depth/stencil or
>    shadow map. Guest CPU code never reads depth maps back into host RAM. We directly reclaim it via
>    `FreeImage(image_id)`.
> 2. **Pressure-Aware Eviction**: under memory pressure, stale tiled images that have aged past the
>    horizon are evicted instead of continuously being moved to the back of the queue.

Verified there on Bloodborne CUSA03173 (AMD RX 6600 8 GB): "Long play sessions (30m+) maintain stable
VRAM usage without running out of memory", and the 13,000-image mass-eviction stalls stopped.

Other reports of the same shape, all still open, all in that family:
`deadinside28/bloodborne_pc` #200 "VRAM grows steadily across area loads until
vk::Result=ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory (RX 6750 XT, 12 GB)" — its log shows `10138 of 5535 MiB (critical
8811): 30 images evicted … 0 old GPU-written tiled images kept (0 MiB)`, i.e. eviction running and
usage not moving: a *different* dominant holder; #32 "Crash every ~20 minutes (memory pressure)";
#377 "Crashing after 1 hour of gameplay"; #105 "rx 570 stop working after 15 minutes".

Upstream context: `shadps4-emu/shadPS4` #888 — `Failed allocating buffer … ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory` is
GPU OOM; the community workaround list for Bloodborne is the usual "lower resolution, no 60 FPS patch,
RAM-spike fix, 4 GB VRAM minimum" (r/shadps4 `1h8fsus`).

##### 2. What our tree was missing

`TextureCache::GarbageCollectImages()` in this repo had the *identical* keep rule the PR describes:

```cpp
const bool download = image.SafeToDownload();
const bool tiled = image.info.IsTiled();
const bool drop = drop_old && tiled && download && aggresive && image.lru_touched_tick < minute_tick;
if (!drop) {
    if (tiled && download) {
        return keep(/*tiled_written_back=*/true);   // ← every depth target, forever
    }
    if (download && !pressured) {
        return keep(/*tiled_written_back=*/false);
    }
}
```

with no notion of depth at all, so every depth/stencil target and shadow map in `slot_images` was
touched and kept, exactly as the PR describes. Under pressure our collector therefore freed "1 image"
(Test #13) while sitting at 4504 of 4352 MiB.

##### 3. What was changed (this round)

`gpu/shadps4/video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache.cpp`, inside the collector's `clean_up`, after the
pin gate and before the keep rules:

```cpp
if (depth_reclaim && image.info.props.is_depth && (pressured || aggresive)) {
    --num_deletions;
    ++gc_depth;
    evicted_any = true;
    FreeImage(image_id, "depth-reclaim");
    return false;
}
```

- `BB_GC_DEPTH_RECLAIM=0` switches it off for an A/B run.
- It is **pressure-gated** (`pressured || aggresive`), unlike the PR which reclaims depth
  unconditionally: a session with memory to spare keeps its depth buffers and its behaviour is
  unchanged, and the leak only matters once the collector has decided it needs room.
- Pinned images never reach it: `BbGpu::GcMayFreeImage` has already rejected bound/target/scene-proxy/
  video-out/collected ids, so a depth target the current draw or the upscaler holds is untouched.
- The pressure report gained a field: `… N pinned, M depth reclaimed`, and the counter resets with the
  others every 5 s.

Deliberately **not** taken from the PR: making *colour* render targets evictable under pressure. That
is what `BB_GC_DROP_OLD` already does when someone opts in, and the reason it is off by default here is
a measurement from this port — a dropped colour target the game still read produced a black screen with
sound on entering the Hunter's Dream on 6 GB cards (`handoff.md` §4.5, §11).

##### 4. What this does not explain yet

`deadinside28` #200 shows usage stuck at 10138 MiB with eviction running and **nothing kept by the tiled
rule**, so there is a second holder that our numbers would have to name: buffers/heaps rather than
images, the pinned set, or the collector's own budget (`num_deletions`, `visited > 256`). Our next
`loader.log` separates those: the pressure line now reports evicted / written back / kept / dropped /
pinned / depth reclaimed, and the once-a-minute `Memory:` line reports VRAM, texture bytes, arena-backed
bytes, unused-for-a-minute images and of those the GPU-written tiled ones.

If `depth reclaimed` climbs and VRAM still parks on the mark, the culprit is not images and the next
suspect is the buffer/heap side (the dense arenas, the stream reserve, or the texture cache's own
budget) — that is the number the next log will carry.

Unverified on hardware, as always: CI says it compiles; a Series S/X run says it works.


_Source: `docs/PRECOMPILE_CRASH_RESEARCH.md`; historical snapshot where applicable._

#### The precompile crash at item 1025 — what the community says

Research round, 2026-10-27. Question: the "Precompile shaders" step in the Xbox UWP port dies on the
item after 1024 of 10256 (last line `control_flow_graph.cpp:407 RemoveUnreachableBlocks: Removing
unreachable block begin=0x27c`), and has to be relaunched. Has anyone else hit this, and how did they
get past it?

Sources are public: shadPS4 issues/PRs, the sibling Bloodborne "bbport" repositories, and
r/BloodbornePC. Everything below is quoted or paraphrased from those; nothing here is a guess about
what our own code does (that is in `handoff.md` §2c).

##### 1. Nobody reports this exact crash

Searched (GitHub issue/PR search API + web):

| Query | Hits about this crash |
|---|---|
| `"DXIL cached"`, `"Precompiling Bloodborne shaders"`, `"driver.vkcache"` | none |
| `"Shader precompile"`, `"pipelines preloaded"` (fingerprints of our own log lines) | only `visy/bloodborne_pc_windows_port` #20, which is a Linux launch issue, no precompile failure |
| `precompile` in `visy/…`, `Mrsuss60/…`, `Jgamrot/…`, `deadinside28/…`, `ayozetr/…`, `bmy/bbport-mac`, `StanTheMackiar/bloodborne-android-port` | no crash reports for the precompile step |
| `"RemoveUnreachableBlocks"`, `"kMaxGotoTransforms"`, `GotoPass` in shadPS4 issues/PRs | none |
| `repo:shadps4-emu/shadPS4 Bloodborne precompile` | none — upstream shadPS4 has no precompile feature at all |

So this is ours: the bulk sweep over every shader extracted from the game's `.shf` archives is a
feature of this port family, and the other ports that have it (`Jgamrot`, `visy`, `Mrsuss60`) run it
to completion on the same game. That is the most useful signal in the whole search: **the sibling
ports precompile Bloodborne without dying**, so the failure is specific to how we do it, not to
Bloodborne's shaders being uncompilable.

##### 2. How the sibling ports do the same job differently

###### `Jgamrot/bloodborne_pc` — a *catalog* of shaders the game is known to use

> "Shader pre-build: shaders the game is known to use are built while it starts (*Preparing shaders*
> in the window title) instead of stuttering the first time an area or effect appears. The included
> catalog covers the game up to the Blood-starved Beast so far; it lists shaders, not game code, and
> each install builds them from its own files. Off with `BB_SHADER_PREBUILD=0`."

It does **not** compile everything in the archives. It compiles a list of shaders that were observed
being used, and the list is incomplete on purpose ("Areas and effects beyond the shader catalog still
stutter briefly the first time").

Reddit, r/BloodbornePC, `1x2qx0g` (the launcher announcement):

> "Less shader stutter: shaders the game uses are now built while the game starts ("Preparing
> shaders" in the title bar) instead of mid-fight. On a fresh install, Central Yharnam went from 479
> shaders compiled while playing to 2."

###### `visy/bloodborne_pc_windows_port` — compile the *recorded* cache, not the archives

`docs/SHADERS.md`:

> "The port records each pipeline the game uses in `user\cache\CUSA03173\` and: **Precompiles the
> cache before the intro** (`BB_SHADER_PRECOMPILE`, default on): all cores build every cached pipeline
> before the logos… Later launches reuse the driver's own disk cache and are quick."

and, the sentence that matters most here:

> "**Shaders the game has never used on any machine cannot be prepared up front: a pipeline depends on
> draw state the game only sets while running.** A shared cache from a player who visited more areas
> covers them."

The same document describes the shader sources being kept next to the compiled shaders:

> "Next to the compiled shaders it keeps each shader's source (`.src` files: the game's shader code
> and the inputs of its translation). When the cache was made for another GPU (or by a build with a
> changed shader translator), the first launch translates every shader again from these sources…
> `BB_SHADER_CACHE_SELFTEST=1` translates each newly compiled shader a second time from its stored
> source and logs any difference."

###### `Awakenchan/LanternEngine` (another port, same game) — a catalog plus a save bug

Release notes:

> "the shader catalog that ships with the engine was being ignored on every PC since 0.9.34 beta
> 9.9, so every shader was built during play. It is fixed and rebuilt: on an NVIDIA GPU about 510
> pipelines are now built before the game starts."

> "A bug in how shader records were saved made most of them unreadable."

~510 pipelines, not 8,207 archive programs. The numbers are the point: what the game actually uses is
one to two orders of magnitude smaller than what the archives contain.

###### What this implies for us

Our sweep compiles **8,207 extracted CS/PS/VS programs + 2,048 linked VS+PS pairs = 10,256 items**
with synthetic register state, on the theory that any of them might be needed. The sibling ports
converged on the opposite theory: compile only what the game has been observed to use, and let
everything else compile lazily at draw time with the real draw state.

If the sibling model is right, item 1025 is a shader **variant the game never asks for** — a
combination our synthetic arena can produce that the game does not. A crash there costs the whole
precompile run but would never have cost a stutter in play, because the variant never runs.

##### 3. Related crashes in shadPS4 that *were* root-caused (the general shape)

| Where | What it was | How it was settled |
|---|---|---|
| shadPS4 #4292 Uncharted: AV in `GpuComm` right after `CompileModule: Compiling cs shader 0x43b8ee5e` | a per-game setting (`directMemoryAccess`), not the compiler | maintainer: "given the shader that's failing to compile, that's likely your issue"; enabling it stopped the crash |
| shadPS4 #321 "Crash in `Shader::Gcn::CFG::EmitBlocks()`, out of bounds list access" | frontend bug in block splitting | fixed by an unrelated earlier fix (#497); the loop was fine |
| `axylpup/shadPS4` #5 (Radeon RX 5500 XT) | one generated shader contained a zero-length list; AMD's driver divided by it and crashed | find and fix the emission — "NVIDIA's driver ignores that, and yours divides by it" |
| `axylpup/shadPS4` #25 (RX 570) | the driver refused one generated pipeline and the emulator closed | **fail open**: "The next version no longer closes when the driver refuses one of the faster shader versions: that object is drawn the normal way instead, and the log names the shader so I can look at it." |
| `axylpup/shadPS4` #17 "Shader compilation stuck at 56%, 17441 completed" (same stuck % on every boot) | not the compiler — Windows thread data read under Wine | bisected with one-setting-at-a-time flags (`SPINLOCK_PARK`, `WRITE_FAULT_OFFLOAD`, `A2`) |
| `boykopovar/AnyPS5` #9702 | structurization of one 4,750-block graph took 177 s and tripped a watchdog | algorithmic fix in the structurizer (bitsets/binary search, dominator trees), verified by dumping the graph and **replaying it offline** (`agc_shader_replay`) |

Two habits run through all of them:

1. **Name the shader, then fail open.** No project in this space lets one pipeline take the process
   down if it can be avoided. (This is what §2c added to our build.)
2. **Replay one shader offline.** Every real root-cause above needed the offending shader in
   isolation — dumped source/registers, or a CFG dump replayed through the structurizer alone.

##### 4. Options that follow from the research

Ordered by how well the evidence supports them.

###### Route A — precompile only what the game uses (the sibling ports' model)

Stop sweeping all 10,256 archive items by default. Keep the startup "warm the recorded pipeline
cache" step (the 65/65 pipelines we already warm), and make the archive sweep a separate, explicitly
chosen "deep precompile", with a **catalog**: the set of shader hashes the game has actually drawn,
recorded during play (we already log `Compiling cs/fs/vs shader 0x…` at draw time, so the data
exists), stored next to the cache and shipped/pickable like `visy`'s exportable cache.

*Evidence:* `Jgamrot` catalog (works, ships), `visy` "cannot be prepared up front… a pipeline depends
on draw state the game only sets while running" (works, documented), `LanternEngine` ~510 pipelines.
*Effect on the crash:* a fabricated variant is never compiled, so item 1025 cannot stall the run.
*Cost:* a shader the game uses but the catalog never saw compiles lazily once — the stutter the
feature exists to avoid, for that one shader.

###### Route B — keep the sweep, but make one bad shader cost nothing

What §2c started, pushed to its conclusion: per-shader time budget, dump each item's source before
compiling it (journal), resume from the last completed item instead of recompiling from 0, and a
visible "N skipped, quarantined" list with a button to re-try them. The sweep stays complete-by-design
and a poisoned shader costs seconds, not a relaunch.

*Evidence:* `axylpup` #25 fail-open + "the log names the shader"; `visy`'s `.src` dump + self-test;
`AnyPS5`'s replay tool.
*Effect on the crash:* the crash still happens, but only once, and the victim is identified.
*Cost:* more code in the precompile path; a shader that dies the process still costs one relaunch if
it is not an access violation.

###### Route C — replay the shader offline first (diagnosis, no behaviour change)

Journal every item's code + synthetic registers during the sweep, then build a tiny host tool that
feeds one record through `TranslateProgram`/`EmitSPIRV` and, on a debug build, dumps the CFG dot
(`CFG::Dot()` already exists). This is how `AnyPS5` found the 177-second structurization.

*Effect on the crash:* none directly; it turns item 1025 into a reproducible input, so the real fix
can be written and tested without the console.
*Cost:* small, and it is the prerequisite for fixing the underlying frontend bug rather than routing
around it.

A and C are complementary; A is the one that makes the crash stop happening on the console, C is the
one that finds out whether the port has a genuine recompiler bug worth reporting upstream.

##### 5. What the search rules out

- **Not a known shadPS4 bug we can cherry-pick.** Upstream `control_flow_graph.cpp` still has the
  same `RemoveUnreachableBlocks` shape (our version is *more* thorough: reachability from the entry
  rather than a single-pass predecessor count), and no upstream issue or PR reports this failure. The
  frontend in this tree also carries our own hardening (goto-transform cap, tree guards, `VisitExpr`
  depth limit) that upstream does not have — so "update from upstream to fix it" is not available.
- **Not a driver-version problem in the usual sense.** Every "crashes after compiling shaders" report
  in the wild is either a missing VC++ redistributable, a wrong dump/update layout, or a per-game
  setting; none of them match a deterministic stop at a fixed item number.
- **Not evidence of a broken dump.** 65/65 recorded pipelines warm successfully and the executable's
  own shaders are not involved; the run dies inside the recompiler on archive content, before any
  game code runs.


_Source: `docs/graphics-toggles.md`; historical snapshot where applicable._

#### Graphics toggles: what the build actually does

Every item on the community guide's list, checked against the code in this repository. "Wired" means
there is a path from the ini key to the thing that runs; "takes effect" means that path is complete
with nothing stubbed in the middle. Line numbers are for this commit.

The guide's list is not the same thing as the port's list. Two items on it did not exist when this
audit started (Bloom, AO Strength) and one was named differently (Less Ghosting).

##### The table

| Guide item | Exists | Wired (ini → consumer) | Takes effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Disable Chromatic Aberration | yes | `bbport_effects.h:50` → `bbport_settings.cpp:152` (ini) → `prepare_game.cpp:2137` (patch) → `patches/Bloodborne.xml:261` | yes, after restart |
| Disable Motion Blur | yes | `bbport_effects.h:53` → `prepare_game.cpp:2137` → `patches/Bloodborne.xml:251` | yes, after restart |
| Disable DoF | yes | `bbport_effects.h:52` → `prepare_game.cpp:2137` → `patches/Bloodborne.xml:271` | yes, after restart |
| Screen-space reflections (SSR) | yes, off by default | `bbport_effects.h:62` → `prepare_game.cpp:2137` → `patches/Bloodborne.xml:281` | yes, after restart |
| Dynamic shadows | yes | `bbport_effects.h:60` → `prepare_game.cpp:2137` → `patches/Bloodborne.xml:256` | yes, after restart |
| Ambient occlusion (SSAO) | yes, on/off only | `bbport_effects.h:58` → `prepare_game.cpp:2137` → `patches/Bloodborne.xml:276` | yes, after restart |
| AO Strength slider | **no** | — | **no.** The game takes an AO constructor, not an AO strength. The patch removes the pass; there is no scalar to scale. The console menu now says so (`bbport_overlay.cpp:379`) instead of showing a slider that would move nothing. |
| Model detail (LOD) | yes | `bbport_settings.cpp:137` (`model_lod`, −2..2) → startup patch selection `prepare_game.cpp:2159` | yes, after restart |
| Bloom | **added in this change** | `bbport_settings.h:174` → `bbport_settings.cpp:84` (parse) / `:400` (save) → `vk_presenter.cpp:692` → `pp_pass.h:30` push constant → `post_process.frag:17` | yes, live. See "Bloom" below for what it does and does not do. |
| AA / Sharpening | yes | `sharpen`/`sharpness` (`bbport_settings.cpp:99-102`) → RCAS in `vk_temporal_upscaler.cpp:740`, `vk_fsr4.cpp:403`, `fsr411.cpp:636`; values >1 add a second pass (`vk_temporal_upscaler.cpp:858`) | yes, live |
| "Less Ghosting" | yes, under another name | the guide's term is the object-motion pass: `object_motion` (`bbport_settings.cpp:107`, which now also accepts the port's `less_ghosting=` spelling) → `vk_camera_motion.cpp:238` | yes; **off** by default on the console, ~5–10% frame cost. The console menu label is now "Less ghosting (object motion vectors)" (`bbport_overlay.cpp:308`) so the two names are the same control. |
| Live Resolution Changes | PC only | `live_resolution` (`bbport_settings.cpp:139`) → `run.py:460` | **not on the console.** `xbox/platform/main.cpp:1399` sets `BB_RENDER_RES`, which fixes the 3D scene at startup; the console menu used to claim the scene resolution "applies immediately on the next frame" anyway. It now says the truth (`bbport_overlay.cpp:243`). |

##### What changed in this pass

1. **Bloom exists now.** It is a host post-process step, not the game's bloom (which is already
   composited into the frame before this port sees it, and cannot be removed without a patch to the
   game). It compresses highlights above a knee of 0.72 in linear light before the transfer curve, so
   a lantern lights its surroundings instead of turning its core into a white disc. Cost: one branch
   and a `exp()` on values that already exceed the knee, in a pass that already runs — no extra
   render target, no extra bandwidth, nothing allocated. `bloom=0` is the default and is bit-exact:
   the branch is not taken. It is skipped when HDR output is on, because that image is graded by the
   TV.
2. **One table instead of three.** `gpu/shim/bbport_effects.h` is now the only list of effects: the
   ini reader/writer (`bbport_settings.h:43-45`), the console's patch compiler
   (`prepare_game.cpp:2086`) and the test read the same array. `scripts/patches.py` keeps its Python
   table (it is a separate process and a separate language) and the test checks it against this one.
3. **Ambient occlusion says what it is.** The console menu no longer implies an AO strength control
   exists.
4. **The scene-resolution hint stopped lying** when the session is startup-patched.
5. **The post-process push constant is asserted**, not documented: `static_assert` on all four
   offsets in `pp_pass.h:35-39`, and `xbox/tests/graphics_toggles_test.cpp` checks the shader's block
   matches it. A mismatch there is a picture that ignores the menu.

##### New test

`xbox/tests/graphics_toggles_test.cpp`, registered in `.github/workflows/xbox.yml`. It reads the files
that ship and checks that they agree with the table:

* every `patch_off`/`patch_on` name exists as a `Metadata Name="…"` in `patches/Bloodborne.xml`;
* `scripts/patches.py` maps the same key to the same patch names;
* every runtime toggle is parsed, stored and saved by `bbport_settings.cpp` and shown by the menu;
* bloom reaches the shader (the push constant carries it, the presenter fills it every frame, the
  shader reads it), which is what distinguishes a working toggle from a checkbox.

It cannot check that the picture looks right. That needs the console.

##### Still needs a console run

Nothing here has been run on hardware yet. Specifically unverified on a Series S/X: that the bloom
rolloff looks the way the description says at 25/50/75, that it costs nothing measurable, and that
`bloom=0` really is bit-identical (it should be — the branch is not taken — but "should be" is not a
measurement). Everything else in the table was already shipping before this change; the audit found
the wiring intact and added the checks that would notice if it stopped being intact.

#### Hardware Test #11 logs (build `xbox-alpha-1.0.26299.1047`)

Text logs uploaded from the Series S test of `xbox-alpha-1.0.26299.1047` (`a3d39fd`), kept verbatim
so the evidence behind the Test #12 fixes stays with the repository (the photos of the console are
not included).

| File | What it contains |
|---|---|
| `loader.log.txt` | Relaunch after the crash: stuck at `presents=0`, `1003/5120 MiB`, no fault. |
| `loader.prev.log.txt` | The crashing session (468 lines): prepare, patches, precompile, arenas, the fault. |
| `errors.prev.log.txt` | The fault report, five `SanitizeCopyLayers` coercions, the `precompile_inflight.txt` ENOENT. |
| `errors.log.txt` | Post-crash relaunch: only Vulkan extension/format warnings. |
| `dozen.log.txt`, `dozen.prev.log.txt` | Dozen startup lines for both runs. |

Key lines (verbatim):

```
Prepared boot image cached: ...\LocalState\Prepared (app_ver=01.00)
Compiled startup patches: game version 01.00 != 01.09; running unpatched 30 FPS (24 bytes)
Patches: 0 writes, 0 bytes applied
GPU: discarding stale driver.vkcache (172154 KiB, UUID/device mismatch)
UWP memory telemetry: 4135/5120 MiB (level=1, presents=1376)
Fault: read access to 0000020500987170 at bloodborne.exe+0x3003f0
UWP swap: out=248 in=20 disk=240 views=20 MiB; checks=1739 corrupt=0 window evictions=0
Runtime: save data 'SPRJ0005' mounted at /savedata0   (lines 229, 417, 419)
vk_runtime.cpp:60 SanitizeCopyLayers: Coercing copy source layers N and destination layers N+1
```

How each observation maps to a Test #12 step (see `handoff.md`, `## Hardware Test #12`):

- `app_ver=01.00` + `running unpatched 30 FPS` -> the missing patch set in this run (the 01.09
  prepare-time gate that briefly refused such dumps was rolled back; see `handoff.md`).
- `+0x3003f0` with `rcx-rdx = 0x2878A160` -> step 3, host page-table/`cached_pages` index fed by a
  guest address outside the 40-bit space (step 2 adds the linker map that resolves such frames).
- Two dense arenas live (`448 MiB` + `464 MiB`) right before the fault -> step 4, arena refcount.
- `driver.vkcache` discarded without the two identities -> step 6.
- `SPRJ0005` mounted three times -> step 7.
- Five layer coercions -> step 8.

#### Console log — the run that confirmed skip-intro, and the crash it ended in

Build on the console: `1.0.26300.345` (release `xbox-alpha-1.0.26300.0345`, target `c63f0b7`).
Sent 2026-10-27, right after the crash and before relaunching, so these are the files of that run.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `loader.log.txt` | launcher + `stdout` of the run: the skip-intro answer, the texture-cache frees, the memory-pressure report |
| `errors.log.txt` | the GPU/`stderr` side: ends with the `slot_vector.h:225` assertion and the STOP line |

`dozen.log.txt` was sent too and held only the two `dzn is not a conformant Vulkan implementation`
warnings — nothing about this run, so it is not kept here.

##### What the run proved

- The skip-intro question works end to end (§2f): the launcher asked, wrote `skip_intro=1` into
  `LocalState\bbport.ini`, printed `Launcher panel: intro skipped`, and the intro did not play.
- The crash after name entry is unchanged, and this log pins its mechanism for the first time:

```
Texture cache: memory pressure, 4726 of 4096 MiB (critical 4352): 9 images evicted ...
Texture cache: free id=58 uid=58 by=eviction guest=0x1066ffe000 size=1048576 ... deferred=1
Texture cache: erase id=58 (freed by=eviction)
Runtime: ImeDialog text: Hunter
Runtime: save data 'SPRJ0005' mounted at /savedata0 (existing)
slot_vector.h:225 ValidateIndex: Assertion Failed!
SlotVector invalid or freed slot index=58 capacity=2978
```

  `capacity=2978` is one 2 MiB chunk of `slot_images` (`sizeof(Image)` ≈ 704 B), so the stale id is
  an `ImageId`, and `58` is exactly the image the collector had just erased. `grep -c "DEAD IMAGE"`
  is **0** in both files: the id was not used through `GetImage`/`GetImageView` but through a direct
  `slot_images[...]`, which is what §2g instruments and fixes.

##### Numbers worth keeping

| Measurement | Value |
|---|---|
| Frame rate before the crash | 27.3 FPS, slowest frame 96.0 ms |
| Memory high-water | `4333/5120 MiB (level=1, presents=870)`, back to `3237` after the GC |
| Images evicted by that pressure pass | 9 (512 B – 1 MiB, all `tiled=1`), `0 written back`, `0 pinned`, `0 dropped`, `0 depth reclaimed` |
| UWP swap at the end | `unpinned private=187 pinned=266 MiB` |


_Source: `docs/hardware-test-15/README.md`; historical snapshot where applicable._

#### Console log — build `.424`: the slot_vector stop is gone, the 5,120 MiB app limit is the wall

Console build `1.0.26300.424` (release `xbox-alpha-1.0.26300.0424`, target `9b09565`). Sent
2026-10-27, right after the crash and before relaunching.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `loader.log.txt` | 814 lines: the whole session, the memory telemetry, the buffer headroom passes |
| `errors.log.txt` | the GPU/`stderr` side, ending in the `buffer.cpp:184` assertion |

##### What it proves

- **The `slot_vector.h:225` stop is gone.** `grep -c "DEAD IMAGE"` = 0 and no `ValidateIndex` line in
  either file, and the run went through character creation into gameplay — §2g held.
- The new stop is an out-of-memory at the platform's app limit:

```
UWP buffer headroom pass 1..6: swap paged out 0 MiB (usage 5087/5120 MiB)
[uwp-vk] FATAL vmaCreateBuffer(16384 KiB, type=DeviceLocal) -> -2; Xbox AppMemory 5116/5120 MiB;
    VMA heap[0] block=1958 MiB alloc=1952 MiB usage=1958 MiB budget=4096 MiB
GPU [Debug] <Critical> buffer.cpp:184 Create: Assertion Failed! Failed allocating buffer with
    error ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory
```

##### The numbers that matter

| Measurement | Value |
|---|---|
| App budget (`AppMemoryUsageLimit`) | 5,120 MiB — the same pool the GPU uses (`integrated, 5120 MiB VRAM`) |
| GC marks in this build | pressure 4,096 / critical 4,352 MiB (`limit-1024` / `limit-768`) |
| Previous build `.0345` marks, same console | pressure 4,352 / critical 4,672 — it hit the wall sooner |
| VMA device-local at the stop | 1,958 MiB of 5,120 — so ~3 GiB was guest-side |
| Guest **pinned** memory | 253 → 657 → 1,168 → 1,331 → 1,337 MiB (unpinned flat at 402–407) |
| Page-out before the failed 16 MiB buffer | 0 MiB in six passes |
| Dense GPU arenas at the stop | 832 MiB live, 52/176 DMA views |
| Frame rate | 55–58 FPS in the open areas, 28–40 FPS at the transitions |

Also seen once, four lines before the end: `UNHANDLED NATIVE FAULT: code=0xc0000005 … addr=0x0
rip=0x7ffd74acf5a0 module=unknown`. The run continued for several frames afterwards, so it is not
the reported crash — but it does not appear in any earlier log.

#### Console log — build `.534`: the pinned-growth ramp, and the area load that tipped it

Console build `1.0.26300.534` (release `xbox-alpha-1.0.26300.0534`, target `b7fff3c`). Sent
2026-10-27, right after the crash and before relaunching. First build whose telemetry keeps printing
near the limit and shows the delta since the last sample.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `loader.log.txt` | 820 lines: 20 telemetry samples with deltas, the arena burst, the headroom passes |
| `errors.log.txt` | GPU/`stderr` side, ending in the `buffer.cpp:189` assertion |

##### The ramp (the part earlier builds hid)

| presents | usage | guest pinned | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 250 | 2,286 | 235 | +279 |
| 564 | 4,401 | 1,079 | +555 |
| 652 | 4,566 | 1,265 | +108 |
| 770 | 4,634 | 1,341 | +11 |
| 793 | 4,687 | 1,354 | +53 |
| 793 | 4,607 | 1,355 | −80 (GC) |
| — | 4,995 | 1,355 | +388 (one area load) |
| — | 5,104 | 1,355 | FATAL |

Headroom passes: 4948 → 4936 → 4958 (64 MiB each), then 4977 → 5028 → 5045 → 5077 → 5110 (0 MiB
each). Same failure as `.504`, same 16 MiB `HostUncached` allocation:

```
[uwp-vk] FATAL vmaCreateBuffer(16384 KiB, type=HostUncached) -> -2; Xbox AppMemory 5104/5120 MiB
    (guest pinned=1355 MiB); VMA heap[0] block=2140 MiB alloc=2134 MiB usage=2140 MiB budget=4096 MiB
GPU [Debug] <Critical> buffer.cpp:189 Create: Assertion Failed!
```

##### What it proves

`guest pinned` climbed 0 → 1,355 MiB while `pageable private` (the pager's only source) stayed near
400 MiB, so five emergency page-out passes in a row returned nothing. The pin rule pinned every page
a guest thread first touched, not just the shared/WC_GARLIC windows — §2j has the cause, the fix and
the `BB_UWP_PIN_PRIVATE=1` A/B switch.


_Source: `docs/hardware-test-18/README.md`; historical snapshot where applicable._

#### Console log — build `.559`: the pin fix works, the pager fills the device and stops on disk-full

Console build `1.0.26300.559` (release `xbox-alpha-1.0.26300.0559`, target `817f291`). Sent
2026-10-27, right after the crash and before relaunching. First build with the new pin rule.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `loader.log.txt` | 1,008 lines: the session, 20+ telemetry samples, the pager reports, a 10 s stall dump |
| `errors.log.txt` | GPU/`stderr` side, ending in `STOP: UWP swap private write …, error 112` |

##### The pin fix did what it was meant to

| Measurement | `.534` (before) | `.559` (this run) |
|---|---|---|
| `guest pinned` | 0 → 1,355 MiB | **0 MiB the whole session** |
| pager's pageable set | ~400 MiB, flat | **989 MiB**, reported openly |
| page-out passes / with nothing to give | 6 emergency passes, all 0 MiB | **237 / 0** |
| swapped out | 0 MiB | **908 → 1,016 MiB** (checks 274 → 660, `corrupt=0`) |
| session | died at `presents=829` on a 16 MiB allocation | **same presents, different reason** (below) |

`UWP memory telemetry` shows `guest pinned=0 MiB` on every sample and `UWP swap: out=908 in=3
disk=907 … checks=274 corrupt=0` — the pager was doing its job for the first time.

##### The new stop: the device ran out of disk

```
UWP swap: out=1016 in=9 disk=1015 views=9 MiB; checks=660 corrupt=0 window evictions=0
STOP: UWP swap private write at 00000010ACD30000, error 112        <- ERROR_DISK_FULL
```

The sparse swap file in `LocalState` reached ~1 GiB and the volume had no more room, and the pager
treated a failed write as fatal. Notes:

- There was a `UWP STALL DETECTED (presents stuck at 829 for 10 s)` right before it, and during the
  stall the pager still paged 108 MiB out — the allocation-retry path pages out synchronously while
  the GPU thread waits, which is where the second of silence came from.
- `presents` never advanced past 829, the same point `.534` died at. So the area load needs more
  than 5,120 MiB, and every mechanism is now doing its best: memory that could be handed back was
  handed back (1 GiB to disk), and there is nothing else to give.
- New warning also seen once: `ProcessGraphics: PM4 header 0x00000002 (type 0) at +0x3a20: rest of
  the buffer dropped` — unrelated to memory, worth remembering.

##### What this run proves

1. The pin rule was the reason the pager had no work (§2j). That part is now measured, not assumed.
2. LocalState is not free space: ~1 GiB is what the volume had, and saves live there too. A pager
   that fills it is worse than one that does not page, so it now keeps a budget and fails soft (§2k).
3. The remaining gap is real capacity: the scene at `presents=829` needs more than 5,120 MiB.


_Source: `docs/hardware-test-19/README.md`; historical snapshot where applicable._

#### Console log — build `.649`: disk-full fixed, the ladder reports "0 MiB paged out"

Console build `1.0.26300.649` (release `xbox-alpha-1.0.26300.0649`, target `8219ff7`). Start line
carries `disk budget=768 MiB`, so this is the build with the fail-soft page-out **and** the ladder.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `loader.log.txt` | 837 lines |
| `errors.log.txt` | ends in `buffer.cpp:235 Create: Assertion Failed!` |

##### What is fixed

- **No `ERROR_DISK_FULL`.** `disk pages=185 MiB of a 768 MiB budget; write failures=0` on every
  report: the budget held and no write ever failed.
- **No 10 s stall** (`grep -c STALL` = 0). Starting the pager at 640 MiB of headroom moved the work
  ahead of the spike: the pre-allocation passes cost 7 / 19 / 109 ms.
- The session ran 6 presents longer (861 vs 815) and `guest pinned` stayed 0 MiB.
- The ladder ran and printed itself rather than stopping silently.

##### The new numbers

```
UWP swap: pageable private=1757 pinned=0 MiB; page-out passes=93 with nothing to give=0
UWP memory emergency (allocation failed): need 141 MiB; paged out 0 MiB in 3 ms,
    freed 0 MiB of images in 0 ms (usage now 5101/5120 MiB)
[uwp-vk] FATAL vmaCreateBuffer(65536 KiB, type=DeviceLocal) -> -2; Xbox AppMemory 5101/5120 MiB
```

`pageable private` was **1,757 MiB** and a 141 MiB request still returned **0 MiB in 3 ms**. That is
the second-chance bit: the clock sweep sets `recent` on every page it passes and only clears it on
the *next* pass, and during an area load every eligible page had been touched since the last sweep.
The background pager's 93 passes produced exactly 2 MiB each - the same limit, at 2 MiB a pass.

Meanwhile the texture cache's emergency reclaim also returned 0 MiB, with no way to tell which keep
rule was responsible (`.649` only had the total).

Both are addressed in the next build: urgent sweeps that ignore the second-chance bit when an
allocation has already failed, and a one-line breakdown of the image reclaim.


_Source: `docs/hardware-test-21/README.md`; historical snapshot where applicable._

#### Console run 7 — `.717` (2026-10-27, scene load)

Logs: `loader.log.txt` (857 lines), `errors.log.txt` (79 lines). Build identity: the pager line reads
`app budget=5120 MiB, pressure headroom=640 MiB; private pages pageable; disk budget=768 MiB` and the
report ends `urgent sweeps=…` — so this is `.717` (`3fe9da1`), the first run with the urgent sweep.

##### What the ladder did

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Disk backing | `disk pages=367 MiB of a 768 MiB budget; write failures=0` — **no disk-full**, half the budget still free |
| Stalls | `grep -c STALL` = **0**; slowest frame 575.5 ms once at start-up, then ≤ 52.4 ms |
| Pinned guest memory | `pinned=0 MiB` in every report and every telemetry line |
| Page-out on request | 9, 9, 14, 6, 9 MiB for 16 MiB asks (25–105 ms), then **ten requests in a row that took 0 MiB in 7 ms** |
| Urgent sweeps | `urgent sweeps=0 (0 MiB)` in every report — the second-chance bit was never what stopped it here |
| Image reclaim | `emergency reclaim freed 0 MiB of the 132 MiB asked for; seen=0 …` |

Then the same wall as `.649`:

```
UWP memory emergency (allocation failed): need 131 MiB; paged out 0 MiB in 7 ms,
    freed 0 MiB of images in 0 ms (usage now 5060/5120 MiB)
[uwp-vk] FATAL vmaCreateBuffer(98304 KiB, type=DeviceLocal) -> -2; Xbox AppMemory 5060/5120 MiB
    (guest pinned=0 MiB); VMA heap[0] block=2313 MiB alloc=2307 MiB usage=2313 MiB budget=4096 MiB
buffer.cpp:235 Create: Assertion Failed! / Failed allocating buffer with error ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory
```

##### What this run proved, and what it left open

- **The disk half is not the problem any more** (367 of 768 MiB, zero write failures, zero stalls).
- **The second-chance bit is not the problem either**: the urgent sweep never had to fire, so the
  pages it was written for were not what the sweep was rejecting.
- **`seen=0` in the texture line is a bug in the reclaim call, not a full cache.** `ForEachItemBelow`
  stops at the first item newer than the gate, and `EmergencyReclaim` asked for `unused_seconds = 0`,
  i.e. the tick recorded at the start of this second. During an area load every image is created or
  touched after that tick, so the walk never entered its loop. Fixed in `.733` (no age gate for the
  emergency path).
- **The guest pager still reported 1,534 MiB of `pageable private`** with `section=0 shared=0
  pinned=0 exec/unreadable=0` while ten consecutive requests took nothing. The report and the sweep
  used the same rules, so one of them is looking at stale state; the next build prints the sweep's own
  per-reason counters and re-counts the page-table buckets at the moment the request fails.

##### Memory growth in this run

`4367 … 4402 (presents 791) → 4572 → 5020 MiB (presents 792, level=2, +447 MiB in one sample)`,
while `UWP dense GPU arena` climbed 16–64 MiB per chunk to `live 960 MiB, 60/176 DMA views`. The
jump happens across two presents — an area load, not a leak per frame.


_Source: `docs/hardware-test-22/README.md`; historical snapshot where applicable._

#### Console run 8 — `.736` (2026-10-27): the crash is gone, the wall is the disk budget

Logs: `loader.log.txt` (1,506 lines), `errors.log.txt` (77). Build identity: the pager line reads
`disk budget=768 MiB` with no `ceiling` field and the report carries `urgent sweeps=0 (0 MiB)`, so this
is `.736` (`3dec03a`) — the first run with the emergency reclaim that ignores the age gate.

##### The run did not stop

No `FATAL`, no assertion, no `STOP` this time. The previous two runs both died on
`vmaCreateBuffer(…) -> -2`; this one reached the wall and **kept going**:

```
Texture cache: emergency reclaim freed 117 MiB of the 116 MiB asked for;
    seen=610 too recent=0 gpu-written=149 bound/target=1 no backing=3 (gc_tick=1251)
UWP memory emergency (allocation failed): need 116 MiB; paged out 0 MiB in 7 ms,
    freed 117 MiB of images in 214 ms (usage now 5025/5120 MiB)
```

The age-gate fix worked: `seen=610` (was `seen=0`) and it freed more than it was asked for.

##### What it then hit: the swap budget, not the device

```
UWP swap: disk pages=768 MiB of a 768 MiB budget; write failures=0; urgent sweeps=0 (0 MiB)
UWP swap: pageable private=1209 pinned=0 MiB; page-out passes=689 with nothing to give=275
UWP swap: not paged - pinned policy=0 section=0 shared=0 exec/unreadable=0 MiB
UWP swap: request 64 MiB got nothing; scanned=1257248 unmapped=0 unpageable=444960
    kind=196724 uncommitted=306024 views-off=0 pinned=0 shared=0 section=0 at-budget=0
    unreadable=0 view-guard=0 recent=0 write-failed=0; disk=768/768 MiB full=0
    write failures=0; page table: resident=1209 pinned=0 section=0 shared=0 unreadable=0 MiB
```

Read together, the three lines are unambiguous:

- the sweep took **nothing** for a reason the old report could not name: the pages were skipped by
  `uwp_swap_disk_pages * PAGE >= uwp_swap_disk_budget`, i.e. the self-imposed 768 MiB ceiling;
- `at-budget=0` in that line is a **missing counter** in `.736` (the increment was not inserted when
  the sweep was split into buckets) — it is the only bucket the 309,540 unaccounted pages fit;
- everything else is zero: 1,209 MiB of pages passed every structural test and could not be written
  because the budget was full. `full=0` means **the device never refused a write** — 768 MiB is a
  number this port chose, not a limit the console imposed.

End of life: `UWP STALL DETECTED (presents stuck at 1291 for 10 s)`, then
`UWP lifecycle: suspending; memory=5116/5120 MiB` (the user suspended it). Usage sat at 5,116/5,120 MiB
with 1,209 MiB of pages it was not allowed to write out.

##### Fixes in the next build

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| The disk budget grows on demand: only while an allocation is waiting (`runtime_memory_page_out`), 256 MiB a step, 768 MiB → **1 GiB ceiling**, `BB_UWP_SWAP_DISK_MB` still a hard cap. Past the ceiling, or on `ERROR_DISK_FULL`, the page stays resident exactly as before | `guest_swap.inc:24-46, 537-558, 831-841` |
| `at-budget` counter added (the missing bucket) | `guest_swap.inc:545` |
| No repeated full-table scan while the disk is the blocker: if the previous request was refused by the disk and less than 500 ms has passed, answer at once instead of walking 2× the page table under the commit lock | `guest_swap.inc:666-675, 706-712` |
| Report and pager line print `ceiling` and `raised` | `guest_swap.inc:786-792, 859-864` |

The 10 s stall is what an allocation storm through that lock looks like: `paged out 0 MiB on request`
fourteen times, 7–8 ms each, all under `uwp_commit_lock`, then `presents stuck`.

##### Still open

- `gpu-written=149` images were refused by the emergency reclaim. They hold GPU output and cannot be
  written back from a tiled layout (upstream PR #89 documents the same thing). Not touched yet.
- Whether 1 GiB of swap is enough for this area load: unknown until the next run.


_Source: `docs/hardware-test-23/README.md`; historical snapshot where applicable._

#### Console run 9 — `.823` (2026-10-27): the budget raise worked, the ceiling is next

Logs: `loader.log.txt` (1,032 lines), `errors.log.txt` (77). Build identity: the pager line ends
`disk budget=768 MiB (ceiling 1024 MiB)` — the first run with the growing budget.

##### The raise did exactly what it was for

```
UWP swap: disk budget raised to 1024 MiB (ceiling 1024 MiB) for a waiting allocation
UWP swap: paged out 62 MiB on request (0 MiB of it urgent)
UWP buffer headroom: swap paged out 62 MiB for a 65536 KiB allocation in 220 ms (usage 4958/5120 MiB)
```

One step, taken during the area load, and the pager filled it. No `FATAL`, no assertion, no `STOP` —
third run in a row that reached the wall without stopping.

##### Where it ended: the 1 GiB ceiling, with the device still willing

```
UWP swap: request 43 MiB got nothing; scanned=1257248 ... at-budget=234572 ...;
    disk=1024/1024 MiB full=0 write failures=0;
    page table: resident=916 pinned=0 section=0 shared=0 unreadable=0 MiB
UWP swap: disk pages=1024 MiB of a 1024 MiB budget (ceiling 1024 MiB, raised 1); write failures=0
UWP STALL DETECTED (presents stuck at 832 for 10 s)
UWP lifecycle: suspending; memory=5111/5120 MiB
```

`at-budget=234572` pages = 916 MiB refused by the ceiling **alone**, with `full=0` and
`write failures=0`: the device never refused a byte. Total paged out in the run: 1,033 MiB.

The stall is the same shape as `.736`: it appeared at 4,972 MiB (before the ceiling was reached) and
`presents` never moved again (832 for the rest of the run) — the log has no way to say whether the
pager's exclusive lock was involved, which is what `.9xx` adds.

##### Fixes in the next build

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Ceiling 1 GiB → **1.5 GiB** (start 768, step 256), so `.823`'s own step repeats twice. `.559` had writes refused at 1,252 MiB, so the second step should fit and the third finds the edge — and a refusal is fail-soft (`full=1`, growth stops, page stays resident) | `guest_swap.inc:24-46, 878-889` |
| Growth stops if the sweep saw a write failure for any other reason (no point raising a limit writes are not reaching) | `guest_swap.inc:545-566` |
| **Images are reclaimed before an allocation fails**, when the pager under-delivers (`paged < want`): the ladder's second rung on the GPU thread, bounded to 128 MiB, at most once a second, same structural rules as the emergency path | `buffer.cpp:180-225` |
| `runtime_memory_pager_state()` — printed into the stall dump: whether a sweep holds the commit lock and for how long, the last page-out request and when it finished, out/in/disk/budget | `guest_swap.inc:677-701`, `main.cpp:58, 1895` |

##### Memory in this run

`4456 → 4776 (+320) → 4972 (+196)` MiB in three samples while `UWP dense GPU arena` climbed to
`live 928 MiB, 58/176 DMA views`. `Runtime: direct memory ... live=4812046336, budget=5301600256` —
the guest's own direct memory is 4.48 GiB of the 5 GiB app budget and the pager cannot touch it;
what is pageable is the ~1.2 GiB below it, and that is what the swap budget bounds.

#### Console run 10 — `.908` (2026-10-27): the device itself refuses at 1,171 MiB

Logs: `loader.log.txt` (1,117 lines), `errors.log.txt` (83). Build identity: pager line ends
`disk budget=768 MiB (ceiling 1536 MiB)`.

##### The growth worked, twice — then the device said no

```
UWP swap: disk budget raised to 1024 MiB (ceiling 1536 MiB) for a waiting allocation
UWP swap: disk budget raised to 1280 MiB (ceiling 1536 MiB) for a waiting allocation
UWP swap: paged out 90 MiB on request … for a 98304 KiB allocation in 295 ms (usage 4928/5120 MiB)
UWP swap: disk pages=1171 MiB of a 1280 MiB budget (ceiling 1536 MiB, raised 2);
    write failures=1; urgent sweeps=0 (0 MiB) (device full: private pages stay resident)
```

`raised 2` and 1,171 MiB stored. Then **one** failed write: `write failures=1`, `full=1`. That is
the real edge — `.559` was refused at 1,252 MiB, this run at 1,171. The room on that console is
about 1.2 GiB, whatever number the port asks for.

##### What the one refusal cost, and it was everything

After it, the pager was dead for the rest of the run:

```
UWP swap: request 64 MiB got nothing; scanned=0 unmapped=0 unpageable=0 … at-budget=0 …
    disk=1171/1280 MiB full=1 write failures=1;
    page table: resident=767 pinned=0 section=0 shared=0 unreadable=0 MiB
```

`scanned=0` — the sweep broke out before examining a single page, because
`if (uwp_swap_disk_full) break;` sat at the top of the loop. 767 MiB of guest memory was still
pageable and the app was 780 MiB from its limit; it climbed to 5,111/5,120, the frame rate fell to
5.2 FPS, and the session ended with `Fault: exception 0xc00000fd` (host stack overflow, thread 3728,
in the present path) — a failure mode this port had not produced before.

##### What this decides

The room is fixed. The pages have to get smaller. Both available levers are in the next build:

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| **Pages are stored compressed** (LZ4 block per page, `xbox/platform/swap_codec.h`), in a 4 KiB-aligned packed arena with one 32-bit record per physical page; all-zero pages are not written at all | `guest_swap.inc:70-100, 240-430` |
| A rewarded write re-uses its record when the new payload fits (a view saved twice does not grow the file) | `guest_swap.inc:385-400` |
| The budget and every report now count **bytes the file actually occupies**, not `pages × 16 KiB` | `guest_swap.inc:974-1000` |
| `full` is no longer permanent: a refused write is retried after 10 s | `guest_swap.inc:52-59, 655-670` |
| A full device **no longer stops the walk**: view pages (`kind == 3`) free RAM without needing disk, so `scanned=0` cannot happen again | `guest_swap.inc:700-712` |
| A record that would exceed our own budget reports `ERROR_DISK_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, never `ERROR_DISK_FULL` — a full budget must not look like a full device | `guest_swap.inc:395-408` |
| The store's page buffers take their own innermost lock (`uwp_promote` reaches a transfer without `uwp_commit_lock`) | `guest_swap.inc:336-342, 420-428` |
| `xbox/tests/swap_codec_test.cpp` round-trips zero, random, heap-like, text-like and boundary-length pages and rejects malformed input; added to CI | `.github/workflows/xbox.yml`, `xbox/tests/swap_codec_test.cpp` |

Measured on the host (16 KiB pages, `-O2`): heap-like data 3.4 KiB/page (21%), zeros 0.15 KiB, at
~10 µs per page. A page-out of 16 MiB is ~1,000 pages, so ~10 ms of coding on top of the ~7 ms of
I/O the sweep already spends.

Expected: the same 1.17 GiB of device room holds roughly 2–4× the guest memory, i.e. the ~780 MiB
that was missing at the crash with room to spare. **Unproven until the console prints the ratio**
(`… pages stored (N raw, N blank, N MiB of payload, N% of raw)`).

##### Open

- `Fault: exception 0xc00000fd` on the host stack in the present path, at the memory limit — not
  investigated. If it recurs in the next build, the thread and RVA are in `errors.log.txt`.


_Source: `docs/hardware-test-25/README.md`; historical snapshot where applicable._

#### Console run 11 — `.1119` (2026-10-27): compression works, and the swap took the game's disk

Logs: `loader.log.txt` (1,283 lines), `errors.log.txt` (80), `dozen.log.txt` (2). Build identity:
`UWP swap: compressed sparse backing ready; 64 MiB mapped-window limit, 389120 page records`.

##### The codec does what it was written for

Progression through the run, from the report line:

| stored | raw | blank | payload | % of raw |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15,755 | 36 | 2,887 | 1 MiB | 0% (early, mostly untouched pages) |
| 47,390 | 85 | 19,683 | 85 MiB | 11% |
| 61,261 | 260 | 19,820 | 233 MiB | 24% |
| 90,799 | 676 | 19,820 | 522 MiB | 36% |
| **125,940** | **1,492** | **20,604** | **890 MiB** | **45%** |

99% of non-blank pages compressed; **1,125 MiB of device held ~2,500 MiB of guest pages**, and
20,604 pages needed no bytes at all. `pageable private=0` at the end: everything pageable had been
paged out. **Present 941**, against 832 in `.908` and 792 in `.823` — the furthest this port has
reached in this area.

No `FATAL`, no `ERROR_DISK_FULL` from the pager: `write failures=0` for the whole run, budget raised
twice (768 → 1,024 → 1,280 MiB).

##### The pager was not the stall — the diagnostic says so

```
UWP STALL DETECTED (presents stuck at 939 for 10 s):
UWP swap: state at the stall: lock=sweep held=0 ms sweeps=397 request=64 MiB finished 16 ms ago
UWP STALL DETECTED (presents stuck at 941 for 10 s):
UWP swap: state at the stall: lock=sweep held=0 ms sweeps=637 request=32 MiB finished 609 ms ago
```

`held=0 ms` twice: no sweep was holding `uwp_commit_lock`. The 10 s freeze is upstream of the pager —
an area load with the working set over RAM (0.6 FPS at the end, `Frame rate: 0.6 FPS`).

##### What ended it: the game's own write, out of space

```
GPU [Debug] <Critical> io_file.h:187 WriteSpan: Assertion Failed!
Failed to write to file, error = No space left on device
STOP: GPU library assertion failed (see GPU log above)
```

The swap file had grown to 1,125 MiB on a device with ~1.2 GiB to spare, and the pipeline-cache
flush lost the race. The pager did not fail — it did its job and the *game's* next write could not.

##### Fixes in the next build

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| **A reserve for the game's own files**: before a new record is taken, the store asks the device how much space is left (`GetDiskFreeSpaceExW` on the swap file's directory, cached for 1 s) and refuses to come closer than **384 MiB** (`BB_UWP_SWAP_RESERVE_MB`). A refused record is `ERROR_DISK_FULL`, handled like any other: the page stays resident | `guest_swap.inc:76-125, 445-455` |
| The report prints `device free=… MiB (reserve … MiB kept for the game's own writes, N record(s) refused by it)`, so the next log answers "could we have taken more?" | `guest_swap.inc:1100-1112` |
| A cache write that hits `ENOSPC` no longer asserts: the short write is reported to the caller (which already removes the partial file and recompiles next time), and the assertion stays for every other error | `gpu/shadps4/common/io_file.h:186-208` |

Nothing else about the ladder changed: paging, image reclaim and the ceiling work as before.

##### Still open

- The 10 s stall and the 0.6 FPS at the end are **not** the pager's lock. It is an area load whose
  working set does not fit in 5 GiB. The approved ladder has one rung left that has not been pulled:
  a lower output resolution / frame-generation setting. That is a settings default, so it needs a
  decision before it ships.
- `disk pages=1125 MiB` was reached with `free` never measured; the next run prints it.
