+/// bbport: last-resort reclaim for a failed allocation (handoff §10). The buffer path asks for it
+/// after the guest pages have been paged out; it returns what the texture cache could still free.
+/// bbport: the last rung of the memory ladder, taken automatically at memory level 2 (the console's
+/// own "critical" mark) and released when the pressure is gone for a while.
+///
+/// What it lowers is the *internal* render resolution, and only through a mechanism that already
+/// exists and is reversible: the upscaler's preset, one step at a time (1080p -> 1.5x -> 1.7x of
+/// the output). With no upscaler active the scene is the guest's own surfaces, so there is nothing
+/// here to scale - `.1119` ran with the upscaler off, which is why this logs that fact once per
+/// excursion instead of pretending to act.
+///
+/// Deliberately not done here: writing the setting to bbport.ini (the user's choice survives a
+/// restart; this one does not) and touching the output resolution (a restart-level change).
+/* bbport: the breadcrumb ring (xbox/platform/main.cpp). A resolution change is exactly the kind of
+ * event a crash report cannot reconstruct afterwards. */
+extern "C" void bb_uwp_breadcrumb(const char *text);
+
+extern "C" void bbgpu_uwp_pressure_level(int level) {
+    auto& s = BbSettings::Get();
+    /* One line when the level changes, not one per sample: this is called every heartbeat. */
+    {
+        static int last_level = -1;
+        if (level != last_level) {
+            last_level = level;
+            char line[96];
+            std::snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "memory pressure level -> %d", level);
+            bb_uwp_breadcrumb(line);
+        }
+    }
+    static int saved_preset = -1;
+    static int saved_output = -1;
+    static std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point calm_since{};
+    const int upscaler = s.upscaler.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
+    if (upscaler == BbSettings::UpscalerOff) {
+        // No upscaler: the host renders the guest's surfaces at the output size, so the internal
+        // resolution is the *output* one. 1280x720 there is a real saving in host targets (and the
+        // text the GPU already prints recommends it) and it is a live change, unlike the startup
+        // patch. Restored by the same ten-calm-seconds rule below.
+        if (level >= 2) {
+            calm_since = {};
+            const int current = s.output_res.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
+            if (saved_output < 0 && current != 0) {
+                saved_output = current;
+                s.output_res.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+                std::printf("UWP memory pressure: level %d, no upscaler - output %dx%d -> %dx%d "
+                            "(live, restored when the pressure is gone)\n",
+                            level, BbSettings::OutputWidths[saved_output],
+                            BbSettings::OutputHeights[saved_output], BbSettings::OutputWidths[0],
+                            BbSettings::OutputHeights[0]);
+                std::fflush(stdout);
+            }
+            return;
+        }
+        if (saved_output < 0) return;
+        const auto calm = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
+        if (calm_since.time_since_epoch().count() == 0) {
+            calm_since = calm;
+            return;
+        }
+        if (calm - calm_since < std::chrono::seconds(10)) return;
+        std::printf("UWP memory pressure: level %d again, output restored to %dx%d\n", level,
+                    BbSettings::OutputWidths[saved_output], BbSettings::OutputHeights[saved_output]);
+        s.output_res.store(saved_output, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        saved_output = -1;
+        calm_since = {};
+        std::fflush(stdout);
+        return;
+    }
+    if (level >= 2) {
+        calm_since = {};
+        if (saved_preset < 0) saved_preset = s.preset.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        const int preset = s.preset.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        // One step per sample, and no further than Performance (1.7x): past that the guest is
+        // rendering 720p-class pixels and the saving is small next to the picture.
+        if (preset < BbSettings::Performance) {
+            const int next = preset + 1;
+            s.preset.store(next, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+            std::printf("UWP memory pressure: level %d, internal render resolution %s -> %s "
+                        "(upscaler %s)\n",
+                        level, BbSettings::PresetName(preset), BbSettings::PresetName(next),
+                        BbSettings::UpscalerName(upscaler));
+            std::fflush(stdout);
+        }
+        return;
+    }
+    if (saved_preset < 0 || saved_preset == s.preset.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
+        saved_preset = -1;
+        return;
+    }
+    // Restore only after ten calm seconds: paging out of an area load dips the level for a moment,
+    // and flipping the resolution back mid-load costs more than it saves.
+    const auto now = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
+    if (calm_since.time_since_epoch().count() == 0) {
+        calm_since = now;
+        return;
+    }
+    if (now - calm_since < std::chrono::seconds(10)) return;
+    std::printf("UWP memory pressure: level %d again, internal render resolution restored to %s\n",
+                level, BbSettings::PresetName(saved_preset));
+    s.preset.store(saved_preset, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+    saved_preset = -1;
+    calm_since = {};
+    std::fflush(stdout);
+}
+
+extern "C" uint64_t bbgpu_uwp_emergency_reclaim(uint64_t need) {
+    auto* r = Core::Memory::Instance()->GetRasterizer();
+    if (!r) {
+        return 0;
+    }
+    // bbport: B9's "retired-arena release" half, which until now only ever happened from
+    // Rasterizer::OnSubmit. `.819` sat at `arena: live=912 retired=448 MiB` while the app was at its
+    // ceiling and the texture cache was being emptied - 448 MiB of replaced arenas waiting for a
+    // release that the submit path defers whenever a draw-prep producer is in flight (which, at
+    // world load, is always).
+    //
+    // ReleaseRetiredArenas only frees an arena whose replacement tick the GPU has already signalled
+    // and which no DMA view still hands to a descriptor set, so this cannot free memory that is in
+    // use; it just asks again, now, because an allocation is waiting.
+    uint64_t freed = 0;
+    auto& buffers = r->GetBufferCache();
+    const uint64_t retired_before = buffers.RetiredArenaBytes();
+    if (retired_before != 0 && need != 0) {
+        buffers.ReleaseRetiredArenas();
+        const uint64_t retired_after = buffers.RetiredArenaBytes();
+        if (retired_after < retired_before) {
+            freed = retired_before - retired_after;
+            std::printf("UWP emergency reclaim: released %llu MiB of retired dense arenas "
+                        "(%llu MiB still retired)\n",
+                        static_cast<unsigned long long>(freed >> 20),
+                        static_cast<unsigned long long>(retired_after >> 20));
+            std::fflush(stdout);
+            bb_uwp_breadcrumb("emergency reclaim: retired arenas released");
+        }
+    }
+    // `need - freed`, never 0: EmergencyReclaim's argument is a byte budget, and asking it for zero
+    // bytes is not a way of asking for nothing.
+    if (need > freed) {
+        freed += r->GetTextureCache().EmergencyReclaim(need - freed);
+    }
+    return freed;
+}
+
+/// bbport (BUILD 3, item 14): the fail-soft ladder's waiting rung.
+///
+/// `bbgpu_uwp_emergency_reclaim` asks once. Both `.736` and `.819` show why once is not always
+/// enough: a merge or an area load is retiring arenas and freeing images on other threads while the
+/// allocation that failed is waiting, and the submit path defers a retired-arena release whenever a
+/// draw-prep producer is in flight - which, at world load, is always. So the release happens, just
+/// after the allocation has already failed.
+///
+/// This waits for those in-flight frees, up to `timeout_ms`, asking again every 20 ms, and reports
+/// what the waiting bought. It is bounded: the plan's rule is "never block forever", and the caller
+/// (`buffer.cpp`) still has its own attempts and the unmodified assertion after this.
+extern "C" uint64_t bbgpu_uwp_present_count(void);
+extern "C" uint64_t bbgpu_uwp_wait_for_release(uint64_t need, uint32_t timeout_ms) {
+    if (need == 0 || timeout_ms == 0) {
+        return 0;
+    }
+    auto* r = Core::Memory::Instance()->GetRasterizer();
+    if (!r) {
+        return 0;
+    }
+    const auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
+    const auto deadline = start + std::chrono::milliseconds(timeout_ms);
+    uint64_t freed = 0;
+    uint32_t asks = 0;
+    uint64_t retired_at_start = r->GetBufferCache().RetiredArenaBytes();
+    while (true) {
+        const uint64_t remaining = freed >= need ? 0 : need - freed;
+        freed += bbgpu_uwp_emergency_reclaim(remaining);
+        ++asks;
+        if (freed >= need) {
+            break;
+        }
+        const auto now = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
+        if (now >= deadline) {
+            break;
+        }
+        // 20 ms: long enough for a draw-prep producer to finish its share and for the fence the
+        // release is waiting on to be signalled, short enough that the whole wait stays a fraction
+        // of a frame budget when it is triggered from the GPU thread at world load.
+        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(20));
+    }
+    const auto waited = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(
+                            std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - start)
+                            .count();
+    const uint64_t retired_now = r->GetBufferCache().RetiredArenaBytes();
+    std::printf("UWP memory: waited %lld ms for in-flight frees (%u ask(s)): released %llu MiB of "
+                "the %llu MiB wanted; retired arenas %llu -> %llu MiB\n",
+                static_cast<long long>(waited), asks,
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(freed >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(need >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(retired_at_start >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(retired_now >> 20));
+    std::fflush(stdout);
+    if (freed != 0) {
+        bb_uwp_breadcrumb("memory: waited for in-flight frees");
+    }
+    return freed;
+}
+
+/// bbport (BUILD 3, item 15): one recovery step, run by the watchdog thread in main.cpp.
+///
+/// The watchdog decides *which* step to run (xbox/platform/watchdog_policy.h, tested in
+/// xbox/tests/watchdog_policy_test.cpp) and this runs it, returning the bytes it released so the
+/// log line carries a number rather than an intention. Every step is bounded work: none of them
+/// waits on a fence without a deadline, and none of them is allowed to fail the run - a step that
+/// finds nothing returns 0 and the next one is considered on the following check.
+///
+///  1 = release: retired arenas, idle staging, then any image the collector may take
+///  2 = pager:   a forced sweep, including the compressed pool (the pager's own urgent path)
+///  3 = degrade: optional features off at run time, then the internal resolution one notch down
+///  4 = exit:    nothing here; main.cpp dumps state, flushes saves and closes the app
+extern "C" uint64_t bbgpu_uwp_recovery_step(int32_t step, uint64_t need) {
+    auto* r = Core::Memory::Instance()->GetRasterizer();
+    if (!r) {
+        return 0;
+    }
+    if (step == 1) {
+        uint64_t freed = 0;
+        // Retired arenas first: they are whole copies of ranges the page table no longer points at,
+        // so releasing them returns the most memory for the least work, and the release is already
+        // gated on the replacement tick having been signalled and no DMA view holding the arena.
+        const uint64_t retired_before = r->GetBufferCache().RetiredArenaBytes();
+        r->GetBufferCache().ReleaseRetiredArenas();
+        const uint64_t retired_after = r->GetBufferCache().RetiredArenaBytes();
+        const uint64_t arena_freed = retired_before > retired_after ? retired_before - retired_after : 0;
+        freed += arena_freed;
+        // Then staging: the same idle rule as the per-frame trim, run now because a stalled
+        // presenter means the per-frame trim is not running at all.
+        // Staging's vectors are renderer-owned. Request its normal idle trim there rather than
+        // mutating them from the watchdog worker while a producer holds a StagingBufferRef.
+        r->GetRuntime().GetStagingPool().RequestIdleTrim();
+        const uint64_t staging_freed = 0; // actual bytes are logged on the next renderer TickFrame
+        // Then images. `need` is what the caller wants back; when it is 0 the texture cache is asked
+        // for whatever it can take, which is the cheap end of the same walk.
+        // A step the watchdog runs with no specific need still has to ask the walk for a budget:
+        // EmergencyReclaim(0) is a request for zero bytes, not "as much as you can".
+        const uint64_t ask = need > freed ? need - freed : (uint64_t{32} << 20);
+        const uint64_t images_freed = r->GetTextureCache().EmergencyReclaim(ask);
+        freed += images_freed;
+        std::printf("UWP recovery: released %llu MiB (arenas %llu, staging %llu, images %llu MiB) "
+                    "of the %llu MiB wanted\n",
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(freed >> 20),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(arena_freed >> 20),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(staging_freed >> 20),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(images_freed >> 20),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(need >> 20));
+        std::fflush(stdout);
+        return freed;
+    }
+    if (step == 2) {
+        // The pager's forced sweep: the same entry point a failed allocation uses, with the pages'
+        // second-chance bit overridable. It returns what it paged out, which is memory the app
+        // budget gets back as soon as the pages are resident again in the compressed pool.
+        const uint64_t paged = runtime_memory_page_out(static_cast<size_t>(need ? need : (128ull << 20)));
+        std::printf("UWP recovery: paged out %llu MiB (of the %llu MiB wanted)\n",
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(paged >> 20),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(need >> 20));
+        std::fflush(stdout);
+        return paged;
+    }
+    if (step == 3) {
+        // Visible, so it is the last thing before giving up, and each change is logged with the
+        // target it costs (item 16: the byte cost of every optional feature).
+        auto& s = BbSettings::Get();
+        const int upscaler = s.upscaler.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        const int frame_gen = s.frame_gen.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        const int output = s.output_res.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        const int preset = s.preset.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        if (upscaler != BbSettings::UpscalerOff) {
+            s.upscaler.store(BbSettings::UpscalerOff, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        }
+        if (frame_gen != BbSettings::FrameGenOff) {
+            s.frame_gen.store(BbSettings::FrameGenOff, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        }
+        // The two optional buffers the upscaler feeds: with no upscaler they are pure cost.
+        s.reactive.store(false, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        s.object_motion.store(false, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        if (output != 0) {
+            s.output_res.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        }
+        if (preset < BbSettings::Performance) {
+            s.preset.store(preset + 1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        }
+        std::printf("UWP recovery: degraded - upscaler %s -> off, frame generation %s -> off, "
+                    "output %dx%d -> %dx%d, preset %s -> %s; optional buffers (reactive mask, "
+                    "object motion) off\n",
+                    BbSettings::UpscalerName(upscaler), BbSettings::FrameGenName(frame_gen),
+                    BbSettings::OutputWidths[std::clamp(output, 0, BbSettings::OutputCount - 1)],
+                    BbSettings::OutputHeights[std::clamp(output, 0, BbSettings::OutputCount - 1)],
+                    BbSettings::OutputWidths[0], BbSettings::OutputHeights[0],
+                    BbSettings::PresetName(preset),
+                    BbSettings::PresetName(std::clamp(preset + 1, 0, BbSettings::PresetCount - 1)));
+        std::fflush(stdout);
+        bb_uwp_breadcrumb("recovery: degraded");
+        return 0;
+    }
+    if (step == 4) {
+        // Request a lower proxy resolution. Native guest render targets are retained by
+        // SceneTargets and the change is applied at a frame boundary; do NOT claim hypothetical
+        // byte savings until actual allocations/usage are observed on the console.
+        auto& settings = BbSettings::Get();
+        const int before = std::clamp(settings.xbox_scene_res.load(std::memory_order_relaxed), 0,
+                                      BbSettings::XboxSceneCount - 1);
+        const int old_output = std::clamp(settings.output_res.load(std::memory_order_relaxed), 0,
+                                          BbSettings::OutputCount - 1);
+        settings.xbox_scene_res.store(BbSettings::XboxScene360p, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        settings.output_res.store(BbSettings::OutputDefault, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        const char* fixed = std::getenv("BB_RENDER_RES");
+        std::printf("UWP recovery: requested scene %dx%d -> %dx%d, output %dx%d -> %dx%d; "
+                    "actual target release pending a rendered frame%s\n",
+                    BbSettings::XboxSceneWidths[before], BbSettings::XboxSceneHeights[before],
+                    BbSettings::XboxSceneWidths[BbSettings::XboxScene360p],
+                    BbSettings::XboxSceneHeights[BbSettings::XboxScene360p],
+                    BbSettings::OutputWidths[old_output], BbSettings::OutputHeights[old_output],
+                    BbSettings::OutputWidths[BbSettings::OutputDefault],
+                    BbSettings::OutputHeights[BbSettings::OutputDefault],
+                    fixed && *fixed ? "; startup-patched BB_RENDER_RES overrides live scene setting" : "");
+        std::fflush(stdout);
+        bb_uwp_breadcrumb("recovery: lower scene resolution requested");
+        return 0;
+    }
+    return 0;
+}
+
+/// bbport: the memory categories and the fence position, for the UWP heartbeat (main.cpp).
+///
+/// The `.524` run showed why one number is not enough: `pageable private` fell to 508 MiB while the
+/// app was still at 5,032/5,120 MiB, and the log could not say where the other 4.5 GiB was. Each
+/// category here is a counter that already existed inside the renderer; this is the arithmetic that
+/// puts them next to each other, and `unaccounted` in main.cpp is what is left.
+extern "C" int32_t bbgpu_uwp_memory_cats(BbGpuMemoryCats *out) {
+    if (!out) {
+        return 0;
+    }
+    *out = BbGpuMemoryCats{};
+    auto *r = Core::Memory::Instance()->GetRasterizer();
+    if (!r) {
+        return 0;
+    }
+    const auto &instance = r->GetInstance();
+    if (instance.CanReportMemoryUsage()) {
+        out->device_used = instance.GetDeviceMemoryUsage();
+    }
+    const auto &textures = r->GetTextureCache();
+    out->texture_bytes = textures.ImageBytes();
+    out->texture_count = textures.ImageCount();
+    const auto &buffers = r->GetBufferCache();
+    out->dense_live = buffers.ArenaBackedBytes();
+    out->dense_retired = buffers.RetiredArenaBytes();
+    out->arena_reserve_used = buffers.ArenaReserveUsedBytes();
+    auto &scheduler = r->GetScheduler();
+    out->fence_submitted = scheduler.CurrentTick();
+    out->fence_completed = scheduler.GetWorkSemaphore()->KnownGpuTick();
+    // bbport (B5): a fence age, without asking the scheduler for tick timestamps it does not keep.
+    // "Completed has not moved while submitted is ahead of it" is the stall this is for; the clock
+    // is the same one the heartbeat runs on, so the two lines can be read together.
+    {
+        static uint64_t last_completed = 0, last_change_ms = 0;
+        const uint64_t now_ms = static_cast<uint64_t>(
+            std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(
+                std::chrono::steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch())
+                .count());
+        if (out->fence_completed != last_completed || last_change_ms == 0) {
+            last_completed = out->fence_completed;
+            last_change_ms = now_ms;
+        }
+        out->fence_stalled_ms = out->fence_submitted > out->fence_completed && now_ms > last_change_ms
+                                    ? now_ms - last_change_ms
+                                    : 0;
+    }
+    out->available = 1;
+    return 1;
+}
+
+/// bbport: B8 - the big allocations and the slow ones, in one line each.
+///
+/// Two things go wrong at world load and neither used to leave a trace: a single allocation of
+/// hundreds of MiB (which is what turns a run that was fine into the run that died), and an
+/// allocation or a fence wait that takes a quarter of a second (the stall that looks like a hang in
+/// the log but is really one call). Everything below this size is left alone - a log that prints
+/// every 4 KiB page is not cheap enough for a release build.
+///
+/// `caller` is a static string literal; `elapsed_ms` is what the caller measured (0 when it does not
+/// care). The usage numbers are the console's own, so the line says where the budget went.
+extern "C" uint64_t bb_uwp_app_memory_usage();
+
+namespace {
+constexpr uint64_t kBigAllocBytes = UINT64_C(32) << 20;
+constexpr double kSlowAllocMs = 250.0;
+} // namespace
+
+extern "C" void bbgpu_note_alloc(uint64_t size, const char *kind, const char *caller,
+                                 uint64_t usage_before, double elapsed_ms) {
+    const bool big = size >= kBigAllocBytes;
+    const bool slow = elapsed_ms >= kSlowAllocMs;
+    if (!big && !slow) {
+        return;
+    }
+    std::printf("UWP alloc%s: %llu MiB %s (%s), usage %llu -> %llu MiB, %.1f ms%s\n",
+                big ? "" : " (small but slow)", static_cast<unsigned long long>(size >> 20),
+                kind ? kind : "unknown", caller ? caller : "unknown",
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(usage_before >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(bb_uwp_app_memory_usage() >> 20), elapsed_ms,
+                slow ? " [SLOW >250 ms]" : "");
+    std::fflush(stdout);
+}
+
+/// bbport: per-thread "current operation", so a stall report says what each GPU thread was doing
+/// rather than only where its stack was. `tag` is a string literal kept as a pointer, which is what
+/// makes this safe to read from another thread: no buffer is ever rewritten, only swapped.
+namespace {
+struct ThreadOp {
+    std::atomic<uint32_t> tid{0};
+    std::atomic<const char *> tag{nullptr};
+    std::atomic<uint64_t> arg0{0};
+    std::atomic<uint64_t> arg1{0};
+    std::atomic<uint64_t> since{0};
+};
+constexpr size_t kThreadOpSlots = 16;
+ThreadOp g_thread_ops[kThreadOpSlots];
+} // namespace
+
+/* bbport: the slot is found once per thread and then cached, because `Scheduler::Wait` tags on
+ * every fence wait - a 16-slot scan there would be paid thousands of times a second. Slots live in
+ * a static array, so a cached pointer never dangles. */
+static thread_local ThreadOp *t_slot = nullptr;
+
+extern "C" void bbgpu_thread_op(const char *tag, uint64_t arg0, uint64_t arg1) {
+    ThreadOp *slot = t_slot;
+    if (!slot) {
+        const uint32_t tid = static_cast<uint32_t>(::GetCurrentThreadId());
+        ThreadOp *empty = nullptr;
+        for (auto &op : g_thread_ops) {
+            const uint32_t owner = op.tid.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
+            if (owner == tid) {
+                slot = &op;
+                break;
+            }
+            if (owner == 0 && !empty) {
+                empty = &op;
+            }
+        }
+        if (!slot) {
+            slot = empty;
+            if (!slot) {
+                return; // more than 16 tagged threads: keep the ones already there
+            }
+            slot->tid.store(tid, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        }
+        t_slot = slot;
+    }
+    slot->arg0.store(arg0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+    slot->arg1.store(arg1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+    slot->since.store(static_cast<uint64_t>(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(
+                                                std::chrono::steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch())
+                                                .count()),
+                      std::memory_order_relaxed);
+    slot->tag.store(tag, std::memory_order_release);
+}
+
+extern "C" void bbgpu_thread_op_done(void) {
+    const uint32_t tid = static_cast<uint32_t>(::GetCurrentThreadId());
+    for (auto &op : g_thread_ops) {
+        if (op.tid.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) == tid) {
+            op.tag.store(nullptr, std::memory_order_release);
+            return;
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+extern "C" void bbgpu_thread_op_dump(void) {
+    const uint64_t now = static_cast<uint64_t>(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(
+                                                   std::chrono::steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch())
+                                                   .count());
+    for (auto &op : g_thread_ops) {
+        const char *tag = op.tag.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
+        if (!tag) {
+            continue;
+        }
+        std::printf("UWP thread op: tid %u in '%s' (0x%llx, 0x%llx) for %llu ms\n",
+                    op.tid.load(std::memory_order_relaxed), tag,
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(op.arg0.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(op.arg1.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(now - op.since.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)));
+    }
+    std::fflush(stdout);
+}
+
diff --git a/gpu/shim/bbport_effects.h b/gpu/shim/bbport_effects.h
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..00e5bb7
--- /dev/null
+++ b/gpu/shim/bbport_effects.h
@@ -0,0 +1,137 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+// bbport: one table for every user-facing graphics/gameplay toggle.
+//
+// There used to be three lists of the same toggles: `BbSettings::Effects` (the ini key, the menu
+// label and the default), `kEffects` inside xbox/platform/prepare_game.cpp (the console's mapping
+// from key to patch name) and `EFFECTS` in scripts/patches.py (the PC launcher's mapping). Three
+// copies of one fact is three chances for a toggle to be "in the build" and do nothing: the ini key
+// is written, the menu shows it, and one of the two patch compilers does not know it.
+//
+// This header is the single source of truth for the first two, and `xbox/tests/graphics_toggles_test`
+// checks the third against it - every patch name here must exist in patches/Bloodborne.xml and must
+// be mapped to the same key in scripts/patches.py.
+//
+// Conventions:
+//   * `key`         the bbport.ini key, also the launcher's key. Never reused.
+//   * `label`       the in-game menu text (menu shows the effect, the ini stores the opposite).
+//   * `default_on`  the game's own behaviour. "Disable X" toggles default on (X enabled).
+//   * `patch_off`   patch applied when the key is 0 (nullptr: nothing to apply).
+//   * `patch_on`    patch applied when the key is 1 (nullptr: nothing to apply).
+//     A toggle with neither is a runtime feature (a menu item the code acts on directly).
+//   * `xbox`        whether the console's menu offers it. Three are desktop-only and stay ini-only
+//     there; the reason is in the comment on the row, not in a string comparison somewhere else.
+//
+// Header-only and dependency-free: the GPU side (gpu/shim/bbport_settings.h), the console's patch
+// compiler (xbox/platform/prepare_game.cpp) and the test all include this file.
+
+#pragma once
+
+namespace BbPortEffects {
+
+struct Effect {
+    const char* key;
+    const char* label;
+    bool default_on;
+    /// Applied when the ini key is 0 / 1. Null means "no patch for this direction".
+    const char* patch_off;
+    const char* patch_on;
+    /// True for a toggle the code acts on at run time rather than a startup patch.
+    bool runtime;
+    /// False: keep it out of the console's menu (it still parses from bbport.ini).
+    bool xbox;
+};
+
+/// Disabling a game effect is a patch at start ("Disable X"); enabling a PC-only effect is a patch
+/// too ("Enable SSR"). Cheats and tweaks are always "on" patches: they do not exist in the game.
+inline constexpr Effect Effects[] = {
+    // --- post-processing ---------------------------------------------------
+    // The four the guide calls "core post-processing": a startup patch that removes the game's own
+    // pass, so the saving is real and needs a restart.
+    {"effect_chromatic_aberration", "Chromatic aberration", true,
+     "Disable Chromatic Aberration", nullptr, false, true},
+    {"effect_dof", "Depth of field (DoF)", true, "Disable DoF", nullptr, false, true},
+    {"effect_motion_blur", "Motion blur", true, "Disable Motion Blur (perf increase)", nullptr, false,
+     true},
+    // PC-exclusive quality: SSAO and dynamic shadows off by default in the patch set (checked = on),
+    // SSR is off in the game and this turns it on. AO strength is not here: the game exposes no
+    // scalar for it, only the constructor choice this patch removes.
+    {"effect_ssao", "Ambient occlusion (SSAO)", true, "Disable SSAO", nullptr, false, true},
+    {"effect_game_aa", "Game anti-aliasing", true, "Disable AA", nullptr, false, true},
+    {"effect_dynamic_shadows", "Dynamic shadows", true,
+     "Disable Dynamic Light Shadows (perf increase)", nullptr, false, true},
+    {"effect_ssr", "Screen-space reflections (SSR)", false, nullptr,
+     "Enable Screen Space Reflections (READ NOTE)", false, true},
+    // --- intro / debug -----------------------------------------------------
+    {"skip_intro", "Skip intro logos and movie", false, nullptr, "Skip Intro", false, true},
+    {"debug_camera", "Free camera (Cross + L3)", false, nullptr, "Restore Debug Camera", false, true},
+    // The debug menu patch rewrites the game's font paths to files from nexusmods: without them the
+    // game crashes on the title screen. It stays ini-only (never applied by the console compiler,
+    // never shown in the console menu) exactly as before this table existed.
+    {"debug_menu", "Debug menu (requires font files)", false, nullptr, "Restore Debug Menu (READ NOTES)",
+     false, false},
+    // --- cheats ------------------------------------------------------------
+    {"cheat_no_death", "Cheat: never die (minimum 1 HP)", false, nullptr, "Player No Dead (Read note)",
+     false, true},
+    {"cheat_stealth", "Cheat: enemies cannot see you", false, nullptr, "Player Stealth (Read note)",
+     false, true},
+    {"cheat_silent", "Cheat: enemies cannot hear you", false, nullptr, "Player Silent (Read note)",
+     false, true},
+    {"cheat_rally_no_decay", "Cheat: Rally never decays", false, nullptr, "No Rally Decay", false,
+     true},
+    {"cheat_enemy_control", "Cheat: control targeted enemy (R3 / L3)", false, nullptr,
+     "Enemy Control", false, true},
+    // --- tweaks ------------------------------------------------------------
+    {"tweak_no_rally", "Disable Rally (health recovery)", false, nullptr, "Disable Rally (HP Regain)",
+     false, true},
+    {"tweak_camera_distance", "Increase camera distance", false, nullptr, "Increased camera distance",
+     false, true},
+    {"tweak_no_camera_rotation", "Disable automatic camera rotation", false, nullptr,
+     "Disable Camera Auto Rotation via Movement", false, true},
+    {"tweak_easy_run", "Run with less stick tilt", false, nullptr,
+     "Sensitive Analog Input (easier to run)", false, true},
+    {"tweak_ragdoll", "Dark Souls-style ragdoll physics", false, nullptr, "DS1-like physics", false,
+     true},
+    {"tweak_circle_confirm", "Japanese/Asian buttons (Circle confirms)", false, nullptr,
+     "Circle Confirm (Japanese/Asian button layout)", false, true},
+    // --- runtime features (no patch; the code implements them) ------------
+    {"quit_to_desktop", "Quit to Desktop in the title and System menus", true, nullptr, nullptr, true,
+     false}, // no desktop on the console
+    {"rebirth", "Rebirth at the Doll (5 Insight)", true, nullptr, nullptr, true, false},
+};
+
+inline constexpr int EffectCount = int(sizeof(Effects) / sizeof(Effects[0]));
+
+/// Toggles that are not in `Effects[]` because they are neither a patch nor a checkbox: they are
+/// numbers the renderer reads every frame. Listed here so the same test can check that each one is
+/// still parsed by the ini, saved back, and shown in the menu - the "in the build but not wired"
+/// failure mode that a table of checkboxes cannot catch.
+struct RuntimeToggle {
+    const char* key;      ///< bbport.ini key
+    const char* label;    ///< menu text
+    const char* field;    ///< the `BbSettings::Values` member that holds it (checked textually)
+    const char* note;     ///< what it does, for the menu hint and the log header
+};
+
+inline constexpr RuntimeToggle RuntimeToggles[] = {
+    {"model_lod", "Model detail (LOD)", "model_lod", "startup patch: -2 highest, 0 the game's, +2 lowest"},
+    {"output_res", "Display output", "output_res", "the host's output and UI size"},
+    {"preset", "Preset", "preset", "scene resolution relative to the output"},
+    {"upscaler", "Upscaler", "upscaler", "off, FSR 3, FSR 4, FSR 4.1.1, TAA or DLSS"},
+    {"sharpen", "Sharpening (RCAS)", "sharpen", "the upscaler's sharpening pass"},
+    {"sharpness", "Sharpness", "sharpness", "0 silent .. 1 single RCAS pass .. 2 two passes"},
+    {"bloom", "Bloom (highlight rolloff)", "bloom",
+     "0 off (bit-exact) .. 100: compresses highlights above the knee so lanterns and fires stop "
+     "blooming into a white halo; a host post-process step, no extra memory"},
+    {"object_motion", "Less ghosting (object motion vectors)", "object_motion",
+     "on: characters, cloth and weapons get motion vectors, less ghosting, about 5-10% slower"},
+    {"live_resolution", "Live resolution changes", "live_resolution",
+     "0 off (startup patch), -1 auto, 1 on: change output and preset without restarting"},
+};
+
+inline constexpr int RuntimeToggleCount = int(sizeof(RuntimeToggles) / sizeof(RuntimeToggles[0]));
+
+/// The community port's ini name for the motion-vector toggle is `less_ghosting`; both spellings
+/// are accepted so a bbport.ini carried over from a PC install keeps working.
+inline constexpr const char* LessGhostingAlias = "less_ghosting";
+
+} // namespace BbPortEffects

+    int v = value;

+        ImGui::SliderInt(label, &v, lo, hi, (v == 0 && zero_text) ? zero_text : "%d");

+}

+         "graded by the TV and is left alone.");
+    // The community port calls this toggle "Less ghosting"; it is the object-motion pass, and on

+    Checkbox("Less ghosting (object motion vectors)", s.object_motion);
+    Hint("Accurate motion vectors for characters, cloth and weapons, so the upscaler does not leave "

+    if (s.object_motion != s.startup_object_motion) {
+        ImGui::TextColored(ImVec4(1.0f, 0.75f, 0.3f, 1.0f),
+                           "Less ghosting applies after restarting the game");
+    }
+

@@ -566,2 +609,3 @@ void Menu() {
-    Checkbox("Object motion vectors", s.object_motion);
-    Hint("Accurate vectors for animated objects reduce breakup on clothing and weapons during movement. Static geometry receives no extra pass. Changes require a restart.");
+    // The community port sells this as "less ghosting"; it is the same object-motion pass.
+    Checkbox("Object motion vectors (less ghosting)", s.object_motion);
+    Hint("Accurate vectors for animated objects reduce breakup on clothing and weapons during movement. Static geometry receives no extra pass. Changes require a restart. About 5-10% of the frame rate.");
@@ -711,0 +756,5 @@ void Menu() {
+    ImGui::SeparatorText("Post-processing");

+    } else if (key == "bloom") {

+        // (`bloom=0.5` and `bloom=50` mean the same thing) because both spellings exist in the wild.

-    } else if (key == "object_motion") {

@@ -352,0 +360,27 @@ bool FsrSettingsNeedRestart() {
+/// Everything from the first `[section]` line to the end of the file. The Xbox launcher owns those
+/// sections in this same file (`[dump] patch_path=` / `use_patch=`, see xbox/platform/ini_file.h),
+/// and Save() rebuilds the file from scratch: without carrying them over, changing any option in
+/// the menu dropped the player's patch folder, and the next start fell back to auto-detection.
+static std::string OtherSections() {
+    std::string out;
+    bool in_sections = false;
+    if (FILE* file = std::fopen(Path(), "r")) {
+        char line[256];
+        while (std::fgets(line, sizeof(line), file)) {
+            const std::string text{line};
+            const size_t begin = text.find_first_not_of(" \t");
+            if (!in_sections && begin != std::string::npos && text[begin] == '[') {
+                in_sections = true;
+            }
+            if (in_sections) {
+                out += text;
+            }
+        }
+        std::fclose(file);
+    }
+    if (!out.empty() && out.back() != '\n') {
+        out += '\n';
+    }
+    return out;
+}
+

+                 "bloom=%d\n",
@@ -370 +406,2 @@ void Save() {

+                 int(v.fsr4_auto_exposure.load()), int(v.fsr4_invert_jitter.load()),
+                 v.bloom.load());

diff --git a/src/runtime_file.c b/src/runtime_file.c
index af03d3a..78cdcb9 100644
--- a/src/runtime_file.c
+++ b/src/runtime_file.c
@@ -865,0 +866,24 @@ int runtime_file_translate(const char *guest,char *out,size_t size) { return tra
+/* bbport (BUILD 3, item 15d): flush the open save files before the watchdog exits the app.
+ *
+ * A save is written to a temporary copy and renamed over the old file when it is closed
+ * (deadinside28#64), so nothing is half-written while a file is open - but the bytes of an *open*
+ * save can still be in the kernel's cache, and the console killing the app a moment later would lose
+ * them. This fsyncs every save the guest has dirty and leaves it open, which is what "flush saves"
+ * means here: it does not commit (a commit is a rename the guest asked for), and it does not touch
+ * anything outside /savedataN. Returns how many files it flushed. */
+int runtime_files_flush(void) {
+    int flushed=0;
+    pthread_mutex_lock(&lock);
+    for (int i=3;i<MAX_FILES;++i) {
+        File *f=&files[i];
+        if (!f->used || f->host<0 || !save_path(f->path) || !f->dirty) continue;
+        if (fsync(f->host)) {
+            printf("Runtime: save flush failed for %s: %s\n",f->path,strerror(errno));
+        } else {
+            ++flushed;
+        }
+    }
+    pthread_mutex_unlock(&lock);
+    return flushed;
+}
+
diff --git a/src/runtime_thread.c b/src/runtime_thread.c

+/* bbport: the guest thread name for the fault handler. A stack overflow prints the thread it
+ * happened on (docs/hardware-test-27: the report only had a host tid, and the thread that overflowed
+ * was a 64 KiB guest thread whose fault handler wanted 64 KiB of its own). Returns "" when the
+ * current host thread is not a guest thread. */
+const char *runtime_thread_current_name(void) {
+    static _Thread_local char name[32];
+    GuestThread *t = current;
+    if (!t || !t->name[0]) return "";
+    snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "%s", t->name);
+    return name;
+}
+

diff --git a/xbox/graphics/arena_admission_policy.h b/xbox/graphics/arena_admission_policy.h
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..78358c8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/xbox/graphics/arena_admission_policy.h
@@ -0,0 +1,32 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+// Overflow-safe admission arithmetic. Used for diagnostics only until callers can safely abandon
+// a DeviceLocal buffer request without handing the renderer a null/dangling buffer.
+#pragma once
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <limits>
+
+namespace BbArenaAdmission {
+inline constexpr std::uint64_t kMinimum = std::uint64_t{16} << 20;
+inline constexpr std::uint64_t kHeadroom = std::uint64_t{250} << 20;
+inline constexpr std::uint64_t kLiveCap = std::uint64_t{768} << 20;
+
+inline bool BudgetFits(std::uint64_t usage, std::uint64_t limit, std::uint64_t bytes,
+                       std::uint64_t headroom = kHeadroom) {
+    if (!limit) return true; // unknown: report separately, do not invent a ceiling
+    if (usage > limit || headroom > limit - usage) return false;
+    return bytes <= limit - usage - headroom;
+}
+
+inline std::uint64_t ProjectedLive(std::uint64_t live, std::uint64_t replaced,
+                                   std::uint64_t incoming) {
+    const std::uint64_t remaining = live > replaced ? live - replaced : 0;
+    if (incoming > std::numeric_limits<std::uint64_t>::max() - remaining)
+        return std::numeric_limits<std::uint64_t>::max();
+    return remaining + incoming;
+}
+
+inline bool CapFits(std::uint64_t live, std::uint64_t replaced, std::uint64_t incoming,
+                    std::uint64_t cap = kLiveCap) {
+    return cap == 0 || ProjectedLive(live, replaced, incoming) <= cap;
+}
+} // namespace BbArenaAdmission

@@ -86,0 +124,39 @@ const Buffer* BufferCache::GetDenseArena(u64 first_block, u64 last_block) {

+                    "MiB, for a buffer at %#llx-%#llx; copied %llu MiB, cumulative %llu MiB in %llu "
+                    "merge(s), largest %llu MiB\n",

+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(merge_largest >> 20));
+        // Item 13's evaluation, measured rather than argued: what merging past a cap would have

+        // would have produced, so the next decision is made on a number.
+        static const u64 merge_cap = [] {

@@ -135,0 +212,19 @@ void BufferCache::ReleaseRetiredArenas() {
+            // Fence retirement (CanRelease) is: the grace window has passed since the replacement,

+            // producer holds an arena. Called from Rasterizer::OnSubmit - after DrainDrawPipe and

diff --git a/xbox/platform/guest_memory.inc b/xbox/platform/guest_memory.inc
index 4883a45..a657be7 100644
--- a/xbox/platform/guest_memory.inc
+++ b/xbox/platform/guest_memory.inc
@@ -31,0 +32,25 @@ static int uwp_promote(UwpPhysical *physical, uint64_t offset);
+/* Should an ordinary private page stay pageable when a guest thread touches it?
+ *
+ * The commit-fault handler used to pin every page a guest thread first touched, because
+ * `guest_code` is true whenever the faulting instruction pointer is anywhere inside the loaded
+ * image (src/probe.c:370) - which is all of the game's code and all of the data it touches while
+ * running. The rule it was written for is in its comment: pin the pageable WC_GARLIC/alias windows
+ * the GPU reads directly. Pinning private pages as well removed the pager's entire workload.
+ *
+ * Measured on the console (docs/hardware-test-15, -16): `guest pinned` grew 0 -> 1,355 MiB over one
+ * session, `UWP swap: unpinned private` stayed flat at ~401 MiB, page-outs in the emergency passes
+ * returned 0 MiB, and the app died failing a 16 MiB `HostUncached` (guest-side) allocation at
+ * 5,104/5,120 MiB - guest memory it could not hand back.
+ *
+ * So: kinds 3 and 4 (shared/alias windows, the GPU reads them directly) and executable pages are
+ * pinned; a private page is not. Should this ever regress, BB_UWP_PIN_PRIVATE=1 restores the old
+ * rule for an A/B run without rebuilding. */
+static int uwp_pin_private_pages(void) {
+    static int cached = -1;
+    if (cached < 0) {
+        const char *env = getenv("BB_UWP_PIN_PRIVATE");
+        cached = env && *env && *env != '0';

+/* bbport (A3): both savings are switchable, because a number you cannot turn off is a number you
+ * cannot measure against. `BB_UWP_SWAP_BLANK=0` stores all-zero pages like any other page (which
+ * costs a record and a write each, and says exactly how many there were); `BB_UWP_SWAP_COMPRESS=0`
+ * stores every page raw. The default is on for both - the logs from `.524` measured 19,770 blank
+ * pages out of 92,196 and 37% of raw payload, so the saving is real - and the report prints what
+ * each one bought either way. */
+static int uwp_swap_flag_on(const char *name) {
+    char buffer[8];
+    const DWORD length = GetEnvironmentVariableA(name, buffer, sizeof(buffer));
+    return !(length == 1 && buffer[0] == '0');
+}
+
+static int uwp_swap_blank_enabled(void) {
+    static int cached = -1;
+    if (cached < 0) cached = uwp_swap_flag_on("BB_UWP_SWAP_BLANK");
+    return cached;
+}
+
+static int uwp_swap_compress_enabled(void) {
+    static int cached = -1;
+    if (cached < 0) cached = uwp_swap_flag_on("BB_UWP_SWAP_COMPRESS");
+    return cached;
+}
+
+/* bbport: all-zero pages are the cheapest saving available - a heap that was freed and zeroed is
+ * still pageable, and it needs no bytes on disk at all. */
+static int uwp_swap_blank(const void *data) {
+    const uint64_t *words = data;
+    for (size_t i = 0; i < PAGE / sizeof(*words); ++i) {
+        if (words[i] != 0) return 0;
+    }
+    return 1;
+}
+
+/* Compress `data` into uwp_swap_io (2-byte length header first). Returns the total bytes to write.
+ * A block is never stored at exactly the page size - that length is the raw marker - and
+ * `uwp_swap_encode_page` (swap_codec.h) is where that rule lives so the tests can hold it. */
+static size_t uwp_swap_encode(const void *data, int *raw) {
+    return uwp_swap_encode_page((const unsigned char *)data, PAGE, uwp_swap_io,
+                                sizeof(uwp_swap_io), uwp_swap_lz_table, raw);
+}
+
+/* bbport: verify a payload by decompressing it before it goes to the device. `.437` could only
+ * catch a bad payload on the way back in, when the page is already gone from RAM and the only
+ * option left is the integrity stop (docs/hardware-test-26). Decompressing 16 KiB and comparing it
+ * costs ~10 us against a page-out that already writes to the device, so it is on by default;
+ * BB_UWP_SWAP_VERIFY=0 turns it off for an A/B run. A page that fails is stored raw instead of
+ * compressed: the session keeps its memory, the report counts the fallback, and the codec bug is
+ * a statistic instead of a stop. */
+static int uwp_swap_verify_payloads(void) {
+    static int cached = -1;
+    if (cached < 0) {
+        const char *env = getenv("BB_UWP_SWAP_VERIFY");
+        cached = !(env && *env == '0');
+    }
+    return cached;
+}
+
+/* ============================ the in-memory page pool ============================
+ *
+ * `.819` is the case this exists for: the LocalState volume had 867 MiB free, so the swap budget was
+ * capped to 483 MiB, the volume filled, 6,828 writes were refused, and 1,171 MiB of guest memory
+ * that the pager *could* have been holding stayed resident until the app hit 5,116/5,120 MiB. The
+ * console has 30 GB free elsewhere, but a UWP app cannot be given another volume - so the second
+ * tier lives in the one resource the app is allowed to spend a little more of: its own RAM.
+ *
+ * A 16 KiB page compressed into this pool costs ~6 KiB of committed memory instead of 16. The net
+ * saving is therefore the difference, not the page: a 192 MiB pool holds roughly 512 MiB of guest
+ * pages, and the ~320 MiB difference is what the app budget gets back. Unlike the file, a blob can
+ * never be dropped to make room - it IS the page's only copy - so the pool is a fixed reservation,
+ * committed as blobs arrive and decommitted as they are read back, and once it is full the pager
+ * behaves exactly as before (pages stay resident).
+ *
+ * Layout: one contiguous reservation, first-fit extents with coalescing, both guarded by
+ * uwp_swap_io_lock (the same lock that already serialises the shared payload buffer, and the only
+ * path in is uwp_swap_transfer_locked). The descriptors are a flat array, so nothing allocates on
+ * the page-out or page-in path. */
+#define UWP_POOL_BLOB_MAX 32768u   /* 32768 blobs x ~6 KiB ~ 192 MiB of pages; 384 KiB of table */
+#define UWP_POOL_EXTENT_MAX 1024u
+#define UWP_POOL_ALIGN UINT64_C(4096)
+
+typedef struct {
+    uint64_t offset;
+    uint32_t length; /* 0 = descriptor free */
+} UwpPoolBlob;
+
+typedef struct {
+    uint64_t offset, length;
+} UwpPoolExtent;
+
+static unsigned char *uwp_pool_base;
+/* One bit per 4 KiB page: VirtualFree can fail, and reusing that committed page must not count it
+ * as new commit. Protected by uwp_swap_io_lock, just like the blobs and extents. */
+static unsigned char *uwp_pool_commit_map;
+static uint64_t uwp_pool_size, uwp_pool_commit;
+static UwpPoolBlob *uwp_pool_blobs;
+static size_t uwp_pool_blob_used;
+static UwpPoolExtent uwp_pool_free[UWP_POOL_EXTENT_MAX];
+static size_t uwp_pool_free_count;
+static uint64_t uwp_pool_pages, uwp_pool_bytes, uwp_pool_pages_in, uwp_pool_refused;
+static uint64_t uwp_pool_decommit_failures, uwp_pool_peak_commit, uwp_pool_decommitted;
+static DWORD uwp_pool_last_decommit_error;
+static int uwp_pool_off, uwp_pool_unavailable;
+
+static uint64_t uwp_pool_limit(void) {
+    static int cached = -1;
+    static uint64_t bytes;
+    if (cached < 0) {
+        bytes = UINT64_C(192) << 20;
+        const char *env = getenv("BB_UWP_SWAP_POOL_MB");
+        if (env && *env) {
+            const unsigned long long mb = strtoull(env, NULL, 10);
+            bytes = (mb <= 2048) ? (uint64_t)mb << 20 : UINT64_C(2048) << 20;
+        }
+        cached = 1;
+    }
+    return bytes;
+}
+
+static int uwp_pool_init(void) {
+    if (uwp_pool_blobs) return 1;
+    if (uwp_pool_unavailable) return 0;
+    const uint64_t limit = uwp_pool_limit();
+    if (limit < (UINT64_C(16) << 20)) {
+        uwp_pool_off = 1;
+        return 0;
+    }
+    uwp_pool_blobs = calloc(UWP_POOL_BLOB_MAX, sizeof(*uwp_pool_blobs));
+    if (!uwp_pool_blobs) {
+        uwp_pool_unavailable = 1;
+        return 0;
+    }
+    uwp_pool_base = VirtualAllocFromApp(NULL, (SIZE_T)limit, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_NOACCESS);
+    if (!uwp_pool_base) {
+        free(uwp_pool_blobs);
+        uwp_pool_blobs = NULL;
+        uwp_pool_unavailable = 1;
+        printf("UWP swap pool: reservation of %" PRIu64 " MiB failed (error %lu); disk only\n",
+               limit >> 20, GetLastError());
+        return 0;
+    }
+    uwp_pool_commit_map = calloc((size_t)((limit / UWP_POOL_ALIGN + 7) / 8), 1);
+    if (!uwp_pool_commit_map) {
+        VirtualFree(uwp_pool_base, 0, MEM_RELEASE);
+        uwp_pool_base = NULL;
+        free(uwp_pool_blobs);
+        uwp_pool_blobs = NULL;
+        uwp_pool_unavailable = 1;
+        puts("UWP swap pool: commit accounting unavailable; disk only");
+        return 0;
+    }
+    uwp_pool_size = limit;
+    uwp_pool_free_count = 1;
+    uwp_pool_free[0].offset = 0;
+    uwp_pool_free[0].length = limit;
+    printf("UWP swap pool: %" PRIu64 " MiB reserved for pages the disk cannot take "
+           "(BB_UWP_SWAP_POOL_MB, 0 disables)\n", limit >> 20);
+    return 1;
+}
+
+static void uwp_pool_insert_extent(uint64_t offset, uint64_t length);
+
+/* First fit. Splitting the tail is free; the extent table is small and only grows when a blob in the
+ * middle of the arena is freed, which is rare enough that 1024 extents is not a real bound. */
+static uint32_t uwp_pool_alloc(size_t need) {
+    if (need == 0) return UINT32_C(0);
+    const uint64_t want = (need + UWP_POOL_ALIGN - 1) / UWP_POOL_ALIGN * UWP_POOL_ALIGN;
+    if (want > uwp_pool_size) return UINT32_C(0);
+    /* Find a descriptor before committing: no rollback/free call is needed if the table is full. */
+    size_t index = 1;
+    while (index < UWP_POOL_BLOB_MAX && uwp_pool_blobs[index].length) ++index;
+    if (index >= UWP_POOL_BLOB_MAX) {
+        ++uwp_pool_refused;
+        return UINT32_C(0);
+    }
+    for (size_t i = 0; i < uwp_pool_free_count; ++i) {
+        if (uwp_pool_free[i].length < want) continue;
+        const uint64_t offset = uwp_pool_free[i].offset;
+        if (uwp_pool_free[i].length == want) {
+            memmove(&uwp_pool_free[i], &uwp_pool_free[i + 1],
+                    (uwp_pool_free_count - i - 1) * sizeof(*uwp_pool_free));
+            --uwp_pool_free_count;
+        } else {
+            uwp_pool_free[i].offset += want;
+            uwp_pool_free[i].length -= want;
+        }
+        /* Commit exactly the blob: commit-on-touch would work too, but the payload arrives as one
+         * memcpy and the saving is only real if the untouched tail stays uncommitted. */
+        if (!VirtualAllocFromApp(uwp_pool_base + offset, (SIZE_T)want, MEM_COMMIT,
+                                 PAGE_READWRITE)) {
+            // Put the carried-over extent back instead of rebuilding the map: rebuild would forget
+            // every blob still allocated and hand its space out twice.
+            uwp_pool_insert_extent(offset, want);
+            ++uwp_pool_refused;
+            return UINT32_C(0);
+        }
+        uwp_pool_commit += bb_pool_mark_pages(uwp_pool_commit_map, offset, want, 1);
+        if (uwp_pool_commit > uwp_pool_peak_commit) uwp_pool_peak_commit = uwp_pool_commit;
+        uwp_pool_blobs[index].offset = offset;
+        uwp_pool_blobs[index].length = (uint32_t)want;
+        if (index + 1 > uwp_pool_blob_used) uwp_pool_blob_used = index + 1;
+        return (uint32_t)index;
+    }
+    return UINT32_C(0);
+}
+
+static void uwp_pool_insert_extent(uint64_t offset, uint64_t length) {
+    size_t at = 0;
+    while (at < uwp_pool_free_count && uwp_pool_free[at].offset < offset) ++at;
+    /* Merge with neighbours before testing the descriptor limit. A full descriptor table must not
+     * lose a range that can be merged without allocating a new entry. */
+    if (at > 0 && uwp_pool_free[at - 1].offset + uwp_pool_free[at - 1].length == offset) {
+        uwp_pool_free[at - 1].length += length;
+        if (at < uwp_pool_free_count &&
+            uwp_pool_free[at - 1].offset + uwp_pool_free[at - 1].length == uwp_pool_free[at].offset) {
+            uwp_pool_free[at - 1].length += uwp_pool_free[at].length;
+            memmove(&uwp_pool_free[at], &uwp_pool_free[at + 1],
+                    (uwp_pool_free_count - at - 1) * sizeof(*uwp_pool_free));
+            --uwp_pool_free_count;
+        }
+        return;
+    }
+    if (at < uwp_pool_free_count && offset + length == uwp_pool_free[at].offset) {
+        uwp_pool_free[at].offset = offset;
+        uwp_pool_free[at].length += length;
+        return;
+    }
+    if (uwp_pool_free_count == UWP_POOL_EXTENT_MAX) {
+        static uint64_t lost_bytes;
+        lost_bytes += length;
+        if (lost_bytes == length) {
+            printf("UWP swap pool: free-extent table full; some reservation cannot be reused\n");
+        }
+        return;
+    }
+    memmove(&uwp_pool_free[at + 1], &uwp_pool_free[at],
+            (uwp_pool_free_count - at) * sizeof(*uwp_pool_free));
+    uwp_pool_free[at].offset = offset;
+    uwp_pool_free[at].length = length;
+    ++uwp_pool_free_count;
+}
+
+static void uwp_pool_free_blob(uint32_t index) {
+    if (index == 0 || index >= UWP_POOL_BLOB_MAX || !uwp_pool_blobs[index].length) return;
+    const uint64_t offset = uwp_pool_blobs[index].offset;
+    const uint64_t length = uwp_pool_blobs[index].length;
+    uwp_pool_blobs[index].offset = 0;
+    uwp_pool_blobs[index].length = 0;
+    /* Only after the guest page has been copied back (or a new disk record written): the blob is
+     * the only backing copy up to that point. MEM_DECOMMIT is a VirtualFree operation, not an
+     * allocation operation. If it fails, retain its committed bits so later reuse does not count
+     * the same pages twice. The switch allows a hardware A/B without risking the page contents. */
+    static int decommit_enabled = -1;
+    if (decommit_enabled < 0) {
+        const char *flag = getenv("BB_UWP_POOL_DECOMMIT");
+        decommit_enabled = !(flag && flag[0] == '0');
+    }
+    if (decommit_enabled) {
+        if (VirtualFree(uwp_pool_base + offset, (SIZE_T)length, MEM_DECOMMIT)) {
+            const uint64_t actual = bb_pool_mark_pages(uwp_pool_commit_map, offset, length, 0);
+            uwp_pool_commit -= actual;
+            uwp_pool_decommitted += actual;
+        } else {
+            uwp_pool_last_decommit_error = GetLastError();
+            ++uwp_pool_decommit_failures;
+            if (uwp_pool_decommit_failures <= 4) {
+                printf("UWP swap pool: decommit failed (error %lu, offset=%" PRIu64
+                       ", bytes=%" PRIu64 "); still committed and tracked\n",
+                       uwp_pool_last_decommit_error, offset, length);
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    if (uwp_pool_pages) --uwp_pool_pages;
+    uwp_pool_insert_extent(offset, length);
+    uwp_pool_bytes = uwp_pool_bytes > length ? uwp_pool_bytes - length : 0;
+}
+
+/* Store the record already encoded in uwp_swap_io - both its 2-byte length header and its payload,
+ * so the blob describes itself exactly as a file record does and the read path cannot disagree with
+ * the write path about where the payload starts. `total` is the encoded size including the header.
+ * Returns the tagged slot value, or 0 when the pool is off, full or refused. */
+static uint32_t uwp_pool_store(size_t total) {
+    if (uwp_pool_off || !uwp_pool_init()) return 0;
+    const uint32_t index = uwp_pool_alloc(total);
+    if (index == 0) {
+        ++uwp_pool_refused;
+        return 0;
+    }
+    memcpy(uwp_pool_base + uwp_pool_blobs[index].offset, uwp_swap_io, total);
+    uwp_pool_bytes += uwp_pool_blobs[index].length;
+    ++uwp_pool_pages;
+    return UWP_SWAP_SLOT_POOL | index;
+}
+
+/* Read a blob back into `data`. Returns 1 on success; a decode failure is a hard error for the
+ * caller (it never gets a half-decoded page). */
+static int uwp_pool_load(uint32_t index, void *data) {
+    if (index == 0 || index >= UWP_POOL_BLOB_MAX || !uwp_pool_blobs[index].length) {
+        uwp_swap_transfer_error = ERROR_NOT_FOUND;
+        return 0;
+    }
+    const unsigned char *blob = uwp_pool_base + uwp_pool_blobs[index].offset;
+    const size_t stored = uwp_pool_blobs[index].length;
+    /* The length header is inside the blob: 2-byte little-endian, == PAGE for a raw block. */
+    const size_t length = (size_t)blob[0] | ((size_t)blob[1] << 8);
+    if (length == 0 || length > stored - 2) {
+        uwp_swap_transfer_error = ERROR_INVALID_DATA;
+        return 0;
+    }
+    if (length == PAGE) {
+        memcpy(data, blob + 2, PAGE);
+    } else if (uwp_lz_decompress(blob + 2, length, data, PAGE) != PAGE) {
+        uwp_swap_transfer_error = ERROR_INVALID_DATA;
+        return 0;
+    }
+    ++uwp_pool_pages_in;
+    return 1;
+}
+
+static int uwp_pool_slot(uint32_t slot) {
+    return slot != UWP_SWAP_SLOT_ZERO && (slot & UWP_SWAP_SLOT_POOL) != 0;
+}
+
+/* Is the pool worth walking to? True when it is enabled and has room for at least one blob. The
+ * check is deliberately cheap: it runs per page in the sweep that is already under the commit lock,
+ * and the exact fit is decided by the transfer. */
+static int uwp_pool_available(void) {
+    if (uwp_pool_off) return 0;
+    if (!uwp_pool_blobs) return !uwp_pool_unavailable && uwp_pool_limit() >= (UINT64_C(16) << 20);
+    for (size_t i = 0; i < uwp_pool_free_count; ++i) {
+        if (uwp_pool_free[i].length >= UWP_POOL_ALIGN) return 1;
+    }
+    return 0;
+}
+
+/* Second tier: the payload in uwp_swap_io (+2, `length` bytes) goes into RAM instead of the file.
+ * Called from the write path, with uwp_swap_io_lock held, only after the disk refused the record. */
+static int uwp_swap_store_pool_locked(uint64_t physical, size_t total) {
+    const size_t key = (size_t)(physical / PAGE);
+    if (!uwp_swap_slot || key >= uwp_swap_slot_count) return 0;
+    const uint32_t pooled = uwp_pool_store(total);
+    if (!pooled) return 0;
+    const uint32_t previous = uwp_swap_slot[key];
+    if (uwp_pool_slot(previous)) uwp_pool_free_blob(previous & ~UWP_SWAP_SLOT_POOL);
+    uwp_swap_slot[key] = pooled;
+    ++uwp_swap_store_pages;
+    return 1;
+}
+
+/* bbport: the page buffers below (uwp_swap_io, uwp_swap_verify, the LZ table) are shared, and a
+ * transfer is reached from the pager, the GPU thread and any guest thread taking a commit fault.
+ * Most callers already hold uwp_commit_lock, but not all of them do (uwp_promote from a guest map),
+ * so the store keeps its own innermost lock: it is never held while taking uwp_commit_lock, so it
+ * cannot deadlock. */
+static SRWLOCK uwp_swap_io_lock = SRWLOCK_INIT;
+
+static int uwp_swap_transfer_locked(uint64_t physical, void *data, int write) {
+    const size_t key = (size_t)(physical / PAGE);
+    if (!uwp_swap_slot || key >= uwp_swap_slot_count) {
+        uwp_swap_transfer_error = ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER;
+        return 0;
+    }
+    if (!write) {
+        const uint32_t slot = uwp_swap_slot[key];
+        if (slot == 0) {
+            uwp_swap_transfer_error = ERROR_NOT_FOUND;
+            return 0;
+        }
+        if (slot == UWP_SWAP_SLOT_ZERO) {
+            memset(data, 0, PAGE);
+            return 1;
+        }
+        if (uwp_pool_slot(slot)) {
+            return uwp_pool_load(slot & ~UWP_SWAP_SLOT_POOL, data);
+        }
+        if (!uwp_swap_io_at((uint64_t)slot - 1, uwp_swap_io, 2, 0)) return 0;
+        const size_t length = (size_t)uwp_swap_io[0] | ((size_t)uwp_swap_io[1] << 8);
+        if (length == 0 || length > PAGE) {
+            uwp_swap_transfer_error = ERROR_INVALID_DATA;
+            return 0;
+        }
+        if (!uwp_swap_io_at((uint64_t)slot - 1 + 2, uwp_swap_io + 2, length, 0)) return 0;
+        if (length == PAGE) {
+            memcpy(data, uwp_swap_io + 2, PAGE);
+            return 1;
+        }
+        if (uwp_lz_decompress(uwp_swap_io + 2, length, data, PAGE) != PAGE) {
+            // Never hand a half-decoded page to the guest: the caller treats this as a failed read
+            // (and the hash check would catch it anyway).
+            uwp_swap_transfer_error = ERROR_INVALID_DATA;
+            return 0;
+        }
+        return 1;
+    }
+    if (uwp_swap_blank_enabled() && uwp_swap_blank(data)) {
+        if (uwp_swap_slot[key] != UWP_SWAP_SLOT_ZERO) ++uwp_swap_store_zero;
+        ++uwp_swap_store_pages;
+        uwp_swap_blank_bytes += PAGE;
+        uwp_swap_slot[key] = UWP_SWAP_SLOT_ZERO;
+        return 1;
+    }
+    int raw = 0;
+    size_t total;
+    if (!uwp_swap_compress_enabled()) {
+        // Raw on request: the length header is PAGE, which is the marker the reader already treats
+        // as "uncompressed", so nothing else in the record format changes.
+        memcpy(uwp_swap_io + 2, data, PAGE);
+        uwp_swap_io[0] = (unsigned char)(PAGE & 0xFF);
+        uwp_swap_io[1] = (unsigned char)((PAGE >> 8) & 0xFF);
+        total = PAGE + 2;
+        raw = 1;
+    } else {
+        total = uwp_swap_encode(data, &raw);
+    }
+    if (!raw && uwp_swap_verify_payloads()) {
+        if (uwp_lz_decompress(uwp_swap_io + 2, total - 2, uwp_swap_verify, PAGE) != PAGE ||
+            memcmp(uwp_swap_verify, data, PAGE) != 0) {
+            ++uwp_swap_codec_fallbacks;
+            memcpy(uwp_swap_io + 2, data, PAGE);
+            uwp_swap_io[0] = (unsigned char)(PAGE & 0xFF);
+            uwp_swap_io[1] = (unsigned char)((PAGE >> 8) & 0xFF);
+            total = PAGE + 2;
+            raw = 1;
+        }
+    }
+    if (raw) {
+        ++uwp_swap_store_raw;
+        uwp_swap_raw_bytes += PAGE;
+    } else {
+        uwp_swap_compressed_bytes += PAGE;
+    }
+    uwp_swap_store_payload += total - 2;
+    uint64_t offset = 0;
+    uint64_t new_space = 0;
+    const uint32_t slot = uwp_swap_slot[key];
+    if (slot != 0 && slot != UWP_SWAP_SLOT_ZERO && !uwp_pool_slot(slot)) {
+        // Rewriting a page that is already stored (a view saved twice): reuse its record when the
+        // new payload fits, which keeps a session from growing the file on every cycle.
+        unsigned char header[2];
+        if (uwp_swap_io_at((uint64_t)slot - 1, header, sizeof(header), 0)) {
+            const size_t stored = (size_t)header[0] | ((size_t)header[1] << 8);
+            if (stored + 2 >= total) {
+                offset = (uint64_t)slot - 1;
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    if (offset == 0) {
+        const uint64_t need =
+            (total + UWP_SWAP_RECORD_ALIGN - 1) / UWP_SWAP_RECORD_ALIGN * UWP_SWAP_RECORD_ALIGN;
+        const uint64_t free_bytes = uwp_swap_free_space();
+        if (uwp_swap_free_valid && free_bytes < need + uwp_swap_reserve) {
+            // The game's own writes come first: a cache blob or a save that cannot be written stops
+            // the process, a page that stays resident does not. The pool is tried below: it needs
+            // no device space at all.
+            ++uwp_swap_reserve_hits;
+            uwp_swap_transfer_error = ERROR_DISK_FULL;
+            if (uwp_swap_store_pool_locked(physical, total)) return 1;
+            return 0;
+        }
+        if (uwp_swap_store_next + need > uwp_swap_disk_budget) {
+            // Our own budget, not the device's answer: ERROR_DISK_QUOTA_EXCEEDED so a full *budget*
+            // is never mistaken for a full disk (the sweep checks it before getting here anyway).
+            // The pool still takes the page: the budget is about the device, not about RAM.
+            uwp_swap_transfer_error = ERROR_DISK_QUOTA_EXCEEDED;
+            if (uwp_swap_store_pool_locked(physical, total)) return 1;
+            return 0;
+        }
+        if (uwp_swap_store_next + need > UWP_SWAP_FILE_MAX_BYTES) {
+            // Past the pool tag: the store cannot address it, so it is a budget answer too.
+            uwp_swap_transfer_error = ERROR_DISK_QUOTA_EXCEEDED;
+            return 0;
+        }

+/// Rewrites a *top-level* `key` (a bare line above the first `[section]`, the layout
+/// scripts/patches.py and the Windows launcher write). `SetValue` cannot do this: it looks for a
+/// literal `[]` section, whereas a bare key belongs to no section at all. Replacements keep every
+/// other line (comments, order, `[dump]`) untouched; duplicates collapse to the one line so a stale

+inline std::string SetTopLevel(const std::string& text, const std::string& key,
+                               const std::string& value, bool* changed) {
+    std::vector<std::string> lines;
+    size_t pos = 0;

+        size_t end = text.find('\n', pos);
+        if (end == std::string::npos) {
+            end = text.size();
+        }
+        std::string line = text.substr(pos, end - pos);
+        pos = end + 1;

+            line.pop_back();
+        }

+            matches = eq != std::string::npos && Trim(lines[i].substr(0, eq)) == key;

+            if (!Trim(lines[i]).empty()) {
+                insert_at = i + 1;
+            }
+        }
+        lines.insert(lines.begin() + static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(insert_at), key + "=" + value);
+    } else {
+        modified = !unchanged;
+    }
+
+    std::string out;
+    for (const auto& line : lines) {
+        out += line;
+        out += '\n';
+    }
+    if (changed) {
+        *changed = modified;
+    }
+    return out;
+}

+/// a console that has been running since before A5 still says `output_res=1920x1080`. This rewrites

+static void migrate_ini_defaults(const std::string& ini_path) {
+    BbPrepare::Bytes data;
+    if (!read_file_bytes(ini_path, data)) {
+        return;
+    }
+    std::string text(data.begin(), data.end());
+    // BUILD 3: the file now carries the watchdog's thresholds (item 15) and the opt-in for a heavy
+    // optional feature (item 16), so the migration runs while the revision is below 3 instead of
+    // only when the marker is absent. Everything it adds is a comment or a default the code already
+    // uses, and no existing line is touched.
+    constexpr int kSettingsRev = 3;
+    int revision = 0;
+    if (const auto at = text.find("settings_rev="); at != std::string::npos) {
+        std::size_t end = at + std::strlen("settings_rev=");
+        while (end < text.size() && text[end] >= '0' && text[end] <= '9') {
+            revision = revision * 10 + (text[end] - '0');
+            ++end;
+        }
+    }
+    const std::string old_line = "output_res=1920x1080";
+    const auto at = text.find(old_line);
+    if (at != std::string::npos) {
+        text.replace(at, old_line.size(), "output_res=1280x720");
+        std::printf("UWP settings: output_res 1920x1080 -> 1280x720 (new default that keeps the "
+                    "app under the memory limit; set output_res=1920x1080 in bbport.ini to keep "
+                    "1080p)\n");
+    }
+    if (revision < 3 && text.find("watchdog=") == std::string::npos) {
+        if (!text.empty() && text.back() != '\n') {
+            text.push_back('\n');
+        }
+        text += "\n"
+                "# BUILD 3: the recovery watchdog. It checks once a second and acts when the app is\n"
+                "# within these distances of its memory limit; 0 disables every step. The stall times\n"
+                "# are what turns 'presents stopped' into a resolution drop, and then a clean exit.\n"
+                "watchdog=1\n"
+                "watchdog_ladder_mb=400\n"
+                "watchdog_pager_mb=250\n"
+                "watchdog_degrade_mb=150\n"
+                "watchdog_stuck_s=3\n"
+                "watchdog_exit_s=10\n"
+                "watchdog_cooldown_ms=2000\n"
+                "# heavy_features_optin=1 keeps an optional feature that costs more than 50 MiB.\n"
+                "heavy_features_optin=0\n";
+        std::printf("UWP settings: added the watchdog thresholds and heavy_features_optin to "
+                    "bbport.ini (settings_rev %d -> %d)\n", revision, kSettingsRev);
+    }
+    if (revision < 3) {
+        if (const auto marker = text.find("settings_rev="); marker != std::string::npos) {
+            std::size_t end = marker + std::strlen("settings_rev=");
+            while (end < text.size() && text[end] >= '0' && text[end] <= '9') {
+                ++end;
+            }
+            text.replace(marker, end - marker, "settings_rev=3");
+        } else {
+            if (!text.empty() && text.back() != '\n') {
+                text.push_back('\n');
+            }
+            text += "settings_rev=3\n";
+        }
+        BbPrepare::Bytes bytes(text.begin(), text.end());
+        write_file_bytes(ini_path, bytes);
+        std::fflush(stdout);
+    }
+}

+// B10: the breadcrumb ring. When the app dies, the last thing printed is usually minutes before the
+// fault (the pager printing "sweeping" then nothing), so the interesting question - what was it
+// doing in the final seconds - has no answer in any log so far. Every lifecycle event and every
+// limit change drops a line here; the fault handler dumps the last 200 before anything else.
+//
+// Static storage, no allocation, no lock in the fault path: a spinlock that the crashed thread may
+// already hold would hang the handler, so the fault dump reads the ring as-is. A torn line is
+// acceptable; a missing dump is not.
+#define BB_BREADCRUMB_LINES 200
+#define BB_BREADCRUMB_CHARS 160
+static char g_breadcrumb[BB_BREADCRUMB_LINES][BB_BREADCRUMB_CHARS];
+static std::atomic<unsigned> g_breadcrumb_at{0};
+
+static unsigned long long breadcrumb_ms() {
+    static const ULONGLONG base = GetTickCount64();
+    return GetTickCount64() - base;
+}

+extern "C" void bb_uwp_breadcrumb(const char* text) {
+    if (!text) {
+        return;
+    }
+    const unsigned slot = g_breadcrumb_at.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+    char* dst = g_breadcrumb[slot % BB_BREADCRUMB_LINES];
+    std::snprintf(dst, BB_BREADCRUMB_CHARS, "[%llu ms] %s",
+                  static_cast<unsigned long long>(breadcrumb_ms()), text);
+}
+
+extern "C" void bb_uwp_breadcrumb_dump(const char* why) {
+    const unsigned at = g_breadcrumb_at.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
+    const unsigned count = at < BB_BREADCRUMB_LINES ? at : BB_BREADCRUMB_LINES;
+    std::printf("UWP breadcrumbs (%s), last %u of %u entries:\n", why ? why : "dump", count, at);
+    for (unsigned i = at - count; i < at; ++i) {
+        std::printf("  %s\n", g_breadcrumb[i % BB_BREADCRUMB_LINES]);
+    }
+    std::fflush(stdout);
+}

+/// The device being lost (vk::Result -4) is the failure `.819` ended in, and the log said only

+extern "C" void bb_uwp_note_device_lost(const char* where) {
+    static std::atomic<int> logged{0};
+    if (logged.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed) > 0) {
+        return;
+    }
+    BbSwapStats swap{};
+    runtime_memory_swap_stats(&swap);
+    BbGpuMemoryCats gpu{};
+    const bool have_gpu = bbgpu_uwp_memory_cats(&gpu) != 0;
+    std::printf("UWP DEVICE LOST at %s: app=%llu/%llu MiB, guest resident=%llu MiB, "

+                "gpu device=%llu MiB, textures=%llu MiB in %llu images, "
+                "arena live=%llu retired=%llu MiB, fences %llu/%llu\n",

+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(bb_uwp_app_memory_limit() >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(runtime_memory_resident_bytes() >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.disk_used >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.disk_budget >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.pages),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.write_failures),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(have_gpu ? gpu.device_used >> 20 : 0),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(have_gpu ? gpu.texture_bytes >> 20 : 0),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(have_gpu ? gpu.texture_count : 0),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(have_gpu ? gpu.dense_live >> 20 : 0),

+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(have_gpu ? gpu.fence_submitted : 0),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(have_gpu ? gpu.fence_completed : 0));

+}
