+                "swap_reserve_mb=%s\n",
+                output, upscaler, frame_gen, setting("preset", "default"),
+                setting("swap_disk_mb", "default (2048, capped to the device)"),
+                setting("swap_reserve_mb", "384"));
+
+    // What each feature costs, so "turn it off" is a number and not an opinion. These are the host
+    // targets the feature needs, computed from its own resolution: 4 bytes per pixel for an RGBA8
+    // scene/history target, and frame generation keeps one extra interpolated frame plus its
+    // history pair. Printed whether or not the feature is on - the point is the comparison.
+    auto pixels_of = [](const char* text, int fallback_w, int fallback_h, int* out_w, int* out_h) {
+        int w = 0, h = 0;
+        if (text && std::sscanf(text, "%dx%d", &w, &h) == 2 && w > 0 && h > 0) {
+            *out_w = w;
+            *out_h = h;
+        } else {
+            *out_w = fallback_w;
+            *out_h = fallback_h;
+        }
+    };
+    int out_w = 1280, out_h = 720;
+    pixels_of(output, 1280, 720, &out_w, &out_h);
+    const double scene_mib = (double)out_w * out_h * 4.0 / (1024.0 * 1024.0);
+    std::printf("UWP feature cost: output %dx%d (scene target %.1f MiB, history pair %.1f MiB); "
+                "upscaler=%s (+%.1f MiB when on); frame_gen=%s (+%.1f MiB per extra frame when on)\n",
+                out_w, out_h, scene_mib, scene_mib * 2.0, upscaler,
+                (std::strcmp(upscaler, "off") == 0) ? 0.0 : scene_mib * 2.0, frame_gen,
+                (std::strcmp(frame_gen, "off") == 0) ? 0.0 : scene_mib);
+
+    // Record actual launch-time paths BEFORE creating Prepared or importing caches. An existing
+    // directory alone is not proof of cached shaders: report existence, file count and bytes.
+    if (BbIni::Flag(ini, "cache_run_diagnostics", true)) {
+        const std::filesystem::path root{winrt::to_hstring(local_dir).c_str()};
+        const auto prepared = root / L"Prepared";
+        const auto portable = root / L"shader_cache";
+        const auto driver = root / L"user" / L"cache";
+        std::error_code ec;
+        const bool prep_dir = std::filesystem::is_directory(prepared, ec); ec.clear();
+        const bool prep_boot = std::filesystem::is_regular_file(prepared / L"boot-linked.bin", ec); ec.clear();
+        const bool shader_dir = std::filesystem::is_directory(portable, ec); ec.clear();
+        const bool driver_dir = std::filesystem::is_directory(driver, ec); ec.clear();
+        BbStorage::FolderSize shader_total, driver_total;
+        (void)BbStorage::WalkFolders(portable, shader_total, 10000);
+        (void)BbStorage::WalkFolders(driver, driver_total, 10000);
+        const bool shaders_warm = shader_total.files != 0 || driver_total.files != 0;
+        const int run_class = prep_boot && shaders_warm ? 2 : (!prep_boot && !shaders_warm ? 1 : 3);
+        g_cache_run_class.store(run_class, std::memory_order_release);
+        g_cache_curve_enabled.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
+        std::printf("UWP cache launch: Prepared=%s boot-linked.bin=%s; shader_cache=%s "
+                    "(%llu files, %llu MiB%s); user/cache=%s (%llu files, %llu MiB%s); run=%s\n",
+                    prep_dir ? "exists" : "absent", prep_boot ? "exists" : "absent",
+                    shader_dir ? "exists" : "absent",
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(shader_total.files),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(shader_total.bytes >> 20),
+                    shader_total.truncated ? ", lower bound" : "",
+                    driver_dir ? "exists" : "absent",
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(driver_total.files),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(driver_total.bytes >> 20),
+                    driver_total.truncated ? ", lower bound" : "",
+                    run_class == 2 ? "warm" : run_class == 1 ? "cold" : "mixed");
+    } else {
+        std::puts("UWP cache launch: diagnostics off (cache_run_diagnostics=0)");
+    }
+
+    const auto effective = [](const char* name, const char* fallback) {
+        const char* value = std::getenv(name);
+        return value && *value ? value : fallback;
+    };
+    std::printf("UWP memory plan switches: swap_auto=%s swap_speed_test=%s swap_pool_decommit=%s "
+                "arena_admission=%s watchdog=%s watchdog_fast=%s watchdog_reduce=%s "
+                "texture_reclaim_experiment=%s resolution_diagnostics=%s cache_run_diagnostics=%s\n",
+                setting("swap_auto", "1"), setting("swap_speed_test", "1"),
+                effective("BB_UWP_POOL_DECOMMIT", "1"), effective("BB_ARENA_ADMISSION", "1"),
+                setting("watchdog", "1"), setting("watchdog_fast", "1"),
+                setting("watchdog_reduce", "1"), effective("BB_GC_EXPERIMENT", "0"),
+                effective("BB_RESOLUTION_DIAGNOSTICS", "1"), setting("cache_run_diagnostics", "1"));
+    std::printf("UWP texture switches: legacy BB_GC_DROP_OLD=%s, BB_GC_DEPTH_RECLAIM=%s\n",
+                effective("BB_GC_DROP_OLD", "0"), effective("BB_GC_DEPTH_RECLAIM", "1 (gated by experiment on UWP)"));
+    std::printf("UWP arena admission: %s; 250 MiB reserve and %s MiB live cap are OBSERVATION ONLY, "
+                "not enforced\n", std::strcmp(effective("BB_ARENA_ADMISSION", "1"), "0") == 0 ? "off" : "on",
+                effective("BB_ARENA_LIVE_CAP_MB", "768"));
+    if (std::strcmp(effective("BB_GC_EXPERIMENT", "0"), "1") == 0) {
+        std::puts("UWP texture experiment: ON; stale GPU-written contents are discarded without "
+                  "tiled write-back and may be needed later. Hardware verification required.");
+    }
+    std::printf("UWP swap selection: %c: free=%llu MiB path=%s source=%s "
+                "requested_budget=%s MiB reserve=%s MiB (actual cap after open)\n",
+                swap_choice.letter ? swap_choice.letter : '?',
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap_choice.free >> 20), swap_choice.path.c_str(),
+                swap_choice.source.c_str(), effective("BB_UWP_SWAP_DISK_MB", "2048"),
+                effective("BB_UWP_SWAP_RESERVE_MB", "384"));
+
+    // Flags that change behaviour at run time, printed even when unset, so a log reader does not
+    // have to guess which A/B switches were in play.
+    // BUILD 1's switches are in here too, so a console run says which of the new tiers was armed:
+    // the in-memory pool (item 3), the all-zero-page exemption (item 2) and the storage warning
+    // (item 1) can each be turned off without a rebuild, which is what makes an A/B measurement of
+    // them possible.
+    std::printf("UWP flags: swap=%s verify=%s blank=%s compress=%s pin_private=%s "
+                "timeout_ms=%s toggles=%s pool_mb=%s storage_dialog=%s\n",
+                std::getenv("BB_UWP_SWAP") ? std::getenv("BB_UWP_SWAP") : "1",
+                std::getenv("BB_UWP_SWAP_VERIFY") ? std::getenv("BB_UWP_SWAP_VERIFY") : "1",
+                std::getenv("BB_UWP_SWAP_BLANK") ? std::getenv("BB_UWP_SWAP_BLANK") : "1",
+                std::getenv("BB_UWP_SWAP_COMPRESS") ? std::getenv("BB_UWP_SWAP_COMPRESS") : "1",
+                std::getenv("BB_UWP_PIN_PRIVATE") ? std::getenv("BB_UWP_PIN_PRIVATE") : "0",
+                std::getenv("BB_UWP_SWAP_TIMEOUT_MS") ? std::getenv("BB_UWP_SWAP_TIMEOUT_MS")
+                                                      : "2000",
+                std::getenv("BB_TOGGLE_FILE") ? std::getenv("BB_TOGGLE_FILE") : "none",
+                std::getenv("BB_UWP_SWAP_POOL_MB") ? std::getenv("BB_UWP_SWAP_POOL_MB")
+                                                   : "192 (default)",
+                std::getenv("BB_UWP_STORAGE_DIALOG") ? std::getenv("BB_UWP_STORAGE_DIALOG") : "1");
+    std::fflush(stdout);
+}
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// BUILD 3, item 15: the recovery watchdog.
+//
+// The heartbeat (below) reports; this acts. It is a separate thread on purpose - the two runs that
+// ended at the wall both did it with the guest's threads blocked in an allocation, so anything that
+// has to notice "we have been at the limit for seconds" cannot be driven by a frame or a submission.
+//
+// Every check is 1 s, every step has a cooldown (watchdog_policy.h), and every step prints what it
+// released. The order is the plan's: cheap release, then the pager, then visible degradation, then a
+// clean exit that has flushed the saves - never a step that waits without a deadline.
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+static BbWatchdog::Thresholds g_watchdog{};
+static std::atomic<bool> g_watchdog_ready{false};
+static std::atomic<bool> g_watchdog_ran_exit{false};
+
+/// `[watchdog]`/top-level keys in bbport.ini, read once by the loader before the game starts.
+/// Whole megabytes for the thresholds, milliseconds for the two stall times and the cooldown; every
+/// value is clamped by watchdog_policy.h, and every value it used is printed so a log shows which
+/// numbers were in play.
+static void configure_watchdog_from_ini(const BbIni::Values& ini) {
+    const auto value = [&ini](const char* key) -> const char* {
+        const auto it = ini.find(key);
+        return it == ini.end() ? nullptr : it->second.c_str();
+    };
+    BbWatchdog::Thresholds t;
+    t.enabled = BbIni::Flag(ini, "watchdog", true);
+    t.fast_enabled = BbIni::Flag(ini, "watchdog_fast", true);
+    t.reduce_enabled = BbIni::Flag(ini, "watchdog_reduce", true);
+    t.ladder_bytes = BbWatchdog::ParseMiB(value("watchdog_ladder_mb"), t.ladder_bytes,
+                                          std::uint64_t{64} << 20, std::uint64_t{2048} << 20);
+    t.pager_bytes = BbWatchdog::ParseMiB(value("watchdog_pager_mb"), t.pager_bytes,
+                                         std::uint64_t{64} << 20, std::uint64_t{2048} << 20);
+    t.degrade_bytes = BbWatchdog::ParseMiB(value("watchdog_degrade_mb"), t.degrade_bytes,
+                                           std::uint64_t{32} << 20, std::uint64_t{1024} << 20);
+    t.reduce_bytes = BbWatchdog::ParseMiB(value("watchdog_reduce_mb"), t.reduce_bytes,
+                                          std::uint64_t{32} << 20, std::uint64_t{1024} << 20);
+    t.fast_tick_bytes = BbWatchdog::ParseMiB(value("watchdog_fast_tick_mb"), t.fast_tick_bytes,
+                                             std::uint64_t{64} << 20, std::uint64_t{2048} << 20);
+    t.stuck_degrade_ms = BbWatchdog::ParseMs(value("watchdog_stuck_s"), t.stuck_degrade_ms / 1000,
+                                            1, 60) * 1000;
+    t.stuck_exit_ms = BbWatchdog::ParseMs(value("watchdog_exit_s"), t.stuck_exit_ms / 1000, 2, 120) * 1000;
+    t.cooldown_ms = BbWatchdog::ParseMs(value("watchdog_cooldown_ms"), t.cooldown_ms, 200, 30000);
+    // Clamp from the largest threshold down: no inverted pair may make a rung unreachable.
+    constexpr std::uint64_t one_mib = std::uint64_t{1} << 20;
+    t.pager_bytes = std::min(t.pager_bytes, t.ladder_bytes - one_mib);
+    t.degrade_bytes = std::min(t.degrade_bytes, t.pager_bytes - one_mib);
+    t.reduce_bytes = std::min(t.reduce_bytes, t.degrade_bytes - one_mib);
+    if (t.stuck_degrade_ms >= t.stuck_exit_ms) {
+        t.stuck_degrade_ms = t.stuck_exit_ms / 2;
+    }
+    if (t.fast_tick_bytes < t.ladder_bytes) {
+        t.fast_tick_bytes = t.ladder_bytes;
+    }
+    g_watchdog = t;
+    g_watchdog_ready = true;
+    std::printf("UWP watchdog: %s; ladder %llu MiB, pager %llu MiB, degrade %llu MiB, reduce %llu "
+                "MiB (%s), fast tick %llu MiB (%s), stuck %llu s degrades / %llu s exits, "
+                "cooldown %llu ms\n",
+                t.enabled ? "on" : "off (watchdog=0)",
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(t.ladder_bytes >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(t.pager_bytes >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(t.degrade_bytes >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(t.reduce_bytes >> 20),
+                t.reduce_enabled ? "on" : "off",
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(t.fast_tick_bytes >> 20),
+                t.fast_enabled ? "on" : "off",
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(t.stuck_degrade_ms / 1000),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(t.stuck_exit_ms / 1000),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(t.cooldown_ms));
+    std::fflush(stdout);
+}
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// BUILD 3, item 16: the byte cost of each optional feature, and forcing off anything over 50 MiB.
+//
+// A5 already made 720p / upscaler off / frame generation off the console's defaults. What was still
+// missing is the rule the plan asks for on top of that: a feature that is *on* and costs more than
+// 50 MiB of host targets is turned off, and the line says what it would have cost. The number is
+// computed from the feature's own resolution (4 bytes per pixel per target), not guessed.
+//
+// The override goes through the environment because that is how BbSettings::Load applies a forced
+// value (it reads `BB_UPSCALER` / `BB_FRAME_GEN` after the file), so the player's bbport.ini is not
+// rewritten - the intent stays in the file, and `heavy_features_optin=1` in it restores it.
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+static void enforce_optional_feature_budget(const BbIni::Values& ini) {
+    const auto value = [&ini](const char* key) {
+        const auto it = ini.find(key);
+        return it == ini.end() ? nullptr : it->second.c_str();
+    };
+    const char* output = value("output_res");
+    int width = 1280, height = 720;
+    if (output == nullptr || std::sscanf(output, "%dx%d", &width, &height) != 2 || width <= 0 ||
+        height <= 0) {
+        width = 1280;
+        height = 720;
+        output = "1280x720 (default)";
+    }
+    const double scene_mib = double(width) * double(height) * 4.0 / (1024.0 * 1024.0);
+    const char* upscaler = value("upscaler");
+    const char* frame_gen = value("frame_gen");
+    const bool upscaler_on = upscaler != nullptr && std::strcmp(upscaler, "off") != 0;
+    const bool frame_gen_on = frame_gen != nullptr && std::strcmp(frame_gen, "off") != 0;
+    // What each feature holds: the upscaler needs a history pair and its output at the feature's own
+    // resolution (two more scene targets); frame generation keeps one interpolated frame plus its
+    // history pair per generated frame.
+    const double upscaler_mib = upscaler_on ? scene_mib * 2.0 : 0.0;
+    const double frame_gen_mib = frame_gen_on ? scene_mib * 3.0 : 0.0;
+    const bool opt_in = BbIni::Flag(ini, "heavy_features_optin", false);
+    std::printf("UWP feature budget: output %s -> scene target %.1f MiB; upscaler=%s costs %.1f MiB, "
+                "frame_gen=%s costs %.1f MiB; features over 50 MiB are %s\n",
+                output, scene_mib, upscaler ? upscaler : "off", upscaler_mib,
+                frame_gen ? frame_gen : "off", frame_gen_mib,
+                opt_in ? "kept (heavy_features_optin=1)" : "turned off");
+    if (upscaler_on && upscaler_mib > 50.0 && !opt_in) {
+        set_env_var("BB_UPSCALER", "off");
+        std::printf("UWP feature budget: upscaler %s turned off (%.1f MiB of host targets at %s, "
+                    "over the 50 MiB this port allows by default); heavy_features_optin=1 in "
+                    "bbport.ini keeps it\n",
+                    upscaler, upscaler_mib, output);
+    }
+    if (frame_gen_on && frame_gen_mib > 50.0 && !opt_in) {
+        set_env_var("BB_FRAME_GEN", "off");
+        std::printf("UWP feature budget: frame generation %s turned off (%.1f MiB per generated "
+                    "frame at %s, over the 50 MiB this port allows by default); "
+                    "heavy_features_optin=1 in bbport.ini keeps it\n",
+                    frame_gen, frame_gen_mib, output);
+    }
+    // Item 16's other two evaluations, printed where a run can be read: the frame cap and its
+    // frames-in-flight cost, and the caches on disk. Neither changes behaviour on its own - a 30 fps
+    // cap is the player's `fps_cap=`. The texture cache is measured by the per-minute memory line's
+    // `textures N (M MiB)`; there is no texture-downscale switch in this tree, so that measurement
+    // is an A/B of `scene_res=` / the preset, not of a flag that would have to be invented first.
+    const char* fps_cap = value("fps_cap");
+    std::printf("UWP feature budget: fps_cap=%s (each frame in flight holds a %0.1f MiB scene target "
+                "plus the presenter's images; a 30 cap halves the frames the GPU may queue)\n",
+                fps_cap ? fps_cap : "60 (default)", scene_mib);
+    std::fflush(stdout);
+}
+
+/// One watchdog step. Returns the bytes it released/// One watchdog step. Returns the bytes it released (0 for the visible steps, which free nothing
+/// directly and are measured instead by the usage line the next check prints).
+static std::uint64_t run_watchdog_step(BbWatchdog::Step step, std::uint64_t need) {
+    switch (step) {
+    case BbWatchdog::StepLadder:
+    case BbWatchdog::StepPager:
+    case BbWatchdog::StepDegrade:
+    case BbWatchdog::StepReduce:
+        return bbgpu_uwp_recovery_step(int(step), need);
+    default:
+        break;
+    }
+    return 0;
+}
+
+/// bbport: the per-category memory table (A4) and the Windows side of the picture (B6).
+///
+/// Every earlier log gave one number - `UWP memory telemetry: 5116/5120 MiB` - and the question it
+/// could not answer was *whose* bytes those were. This prints the categories side by side, and the
+/// last line is the answer to "is it us": what the app budget accounts for minus what every category
+/// we know about sums to. A large `unaccounted` means the bytes are not guest memory and not the
+/// GPU's, so no change of ours can return them; a small one means the next reclaim has a target.
+///
+/// Cheap enough for release: one page walk for the pager's totals, a handful of counter reads for
+/// the GPU, and five `MemoryManager` fields, once per heartbeat (5 s, 1 s near the limit).
+static void log_memory_table(uint64_t presents) {
+    BbSwapStats swap{};
+    runtime_memory_swap_stats(&swap);
+    BbGpuMemoryCats gpu{};
+    const bool have_gpu = bbgpu_uwp_memory_cats(&gpu) != 0;
+
+    // B6's Windows side: the paging counters, which say whether the console is thrashing (hard
+    // faults climbing, peak working set far above the current one) while our own numbers look calm.
+    // Resolved through the loader rather than linked: psapi/kernel32's process-memory query is not
+    // in the UWP API partition, but on a debug-launched build it is present, and the console's own
+    // hardware test is the run that needs the numbers. When it is missing the line says so.
+    PROCESS_MEMORY_COUNTERS_EX paging{};
+    paging.cb = sizeof(paging);
+    bool have_paging = false;
+    if (HMODULE kernel = GetModuleHandleW(L"kernel32.dll")) {
+        using QueryFn = BOOL(WINAPI*)(HANDLE, PROCESS_MEMORY_COUNTERS*, DWORD);
+        if (const auto query =
+                reinterpret_cast<QueryFn>(reinterpret_cast<void*>(GetProcAddress(
+                    kernel, "K32GetProcessMemoryInfo")))) {
+            have_paging =
+                query(GetCurrentProcess(), reinterpret_cast<PROCESS_MEMORY_COUNTERS*>(&paging),
+                      sizeof(paging)) != FALSE;
+        }
+    }
+
+    const uint64_t limit = bb_uwp_app_memory_limit();
+    const uint64_t usage = bb_uwp_app_memory_usage();
+    const uint64_t resident = runtime_memory_resident_bytes();
+    const uint64_t pinned = runtime_memory_pinned_bytes();
+
+    std::printf("UWP memory table:");
+    std::printf(" app=%llu/%llu MiB", static_cast<unsigned long long>(usage >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(limit >> 20));
+    std::printf(" guest resident=%llu MiB (pinned %llu MiB)",
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(resident >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(pinned >> 20));
+    // `parked` is the guest memory the file is holding, `used` what that cost on disk, and the two
+    // together are the A3 measurement: `.819` parked 1,149 MiB in 483 MiB, so 666 MiB that would
+    // otherwise have been resident stayed out of RAM.
+    const uint64_t parked = swap.pages * 16384;
+    std::printf("\n  swap: used=%llu budget=%llu payload=%llu MiB, pages=%llu (blank %llu), "
+                "blank=%llu raw=%llu compressed=%llu MiB\n",
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.disk_used >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.disk_budget >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.payload >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.pages),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.blank_pages),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.blank_bytes >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.raw_bytes >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.compressed_bytes >> 20));
+    {
+        // Where the resident guest memory actually is, and how much of it the pager may touch.
+        uint64_t parts[6] = {};
+        runtime_memory_resident_breakdown(parts, 6);
+        std::printf("  resident: private=%llu MiB (pageable %llu, not pageable %llu), section=%llu, "
+                    "views=%llu, disk-backed=%llu MiB\n",
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(parts[0] >> 20),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(parts[1] >> 20),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(parts[2] >> 20),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(parts[3] >> 20),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(parts[4] >> 20),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(parts[5] >> 20));
+    }
+    std::printf("  swap keeps out of RAM: %llu MiB of guest pages (blank %llu + compression) "
+                "in %llu MiB of file\n",
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>((parked > swap.disk_used ? (parked - swap.disk_used)
+                                                                        : 0) >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.blank_bytes >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.disk_used >> 20));
+    std::printf("  swap io: out=%llu in=%llu pages, copy-in failures=%llu, write failures=%llu, "
+                "at-budget=%llu MiB, write-failed=%llu MiB\n",
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.copy_out_pages),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.copy_in_pages),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.copy_in_failures),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.write_failures),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.atbudget_bytes >> 20),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(swap.write_failed_bytes >> 20));
+    if (have_gpu) {
+        const unsigned long long outstanding =
+            gpu.fence_submitted >= gpu.fence_completed
+                ? static_cast<unsigned long long>(gpu.fence_submitted - gpu.fence_completed)
+                : 0;
+        std::printf("  gpu: device=%llu MiB (available=%d), textures=%llu MiB in %llu images\n",
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(gpu.device_used >> 20), gpu.available,
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(gpu.texture_bytes >> 20),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(gpu.texture_count));
+        std::printf("  arena: live=%llu retired=%llu reserve-used=%llu MiB\n",
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(gpu.dense_live >> 20),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(gpu.dense_retired >> 20),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(gpu.arena_reserve_used >> 20));
+        std::printf("  fences: submitted=%llu completed=%llu outstanding=%llu\n",
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(gpu.fence_submitted),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(gpu.fence_completed), outstanding);
+    } else {
+        std::puts("  gpu: not available");
+    }
+    if (have_paging) {
+        std::printf("  os: hard faults=%lu, working set=%llu MiB, peak=%llu MiB, page file=%llu MiB, "
+                    "presents=%llu\n",
+                    paging.PageFaultCount,
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(paging.WorkingSetSize >> 20),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(paging.PeakWorkingSetSize >> 20),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(paging.PagefileUsage >> 20),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(presents));
+    } else {

+                std::condition_variable ready;
+                std::deque<Job> jobs;
+                bool pending[6]{}; // includes the running job; prevents duplicate work
+            };
+            auto queue = std::make_shared<WorkQueue>();
+            std::thread([queue] {
+                winrt::init_apartment(winrt::apartment_type::multi_threaded);
+                for (;;) {
+                    Job job{};
+                    {
+                        std::unique_lock lock{queue->mutex};
+                        queue->ready.wait_for(lock, std::chrono::milliseconds(250), [&] {
+                            return !queue->jobs.empty() || g_finished.load();
+                        });
+                        if (g_finished.load()) return;
+                        if (queue->jobs.empty()) continue;
+                        job = queue->jobs.front();
+                        queue->jobs.pop_front();
+                    }
+                    const auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
+                    std::printf("UWP watchdog: step %s started (headroom %llu MiB, "
+                                "usage %llu/%llu MiB, presents %llu, stuck %llu ms)\n",
+                                BbWatchdog::StepName(job.step),
+                                static_cast<unsigned long long>(job.headroom >> 20),
+                                static_cast<unsigned long long>(job.usage >> 20),
+                                static_cast<unsigned long long>(job.limit >> 20),
+                                static_cast<unsigned long long>(job.presents),
+                                static_cast<unsigned long long>(job.stuck_ms));
+                    std::fflush(stdout);
+                    const std::uint64_t freed = run_watchdog_step(job.step, job.need);
+                    const auto elapsed = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(
+                        std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - start).count();
+                    std::printf("UWP watchdog: step %s freed %llu MiB in %lld ms%s\n",
+                                BbWatchdog::StepName(job.step),
+                                static_cast<unsigned long long>(freed >> 20),
+                                static_cast<long long>(elapsed),
+                                job.step == BbWatchdog::StepReduce
+                                    ? " (settings requested; actual target changes require another frame)" : "");
+                    std::fflush(stdout);
+                    {
+                        std::scoped_lock lock{queue->mutex};
+                        queue->pending[int(job.step)] = false;
+                    }
+                }
+            }).detach();
+
+            BbWatchdog::Step highest_scheduled = BbWatchdog::StepNone;
+            std::uint64_t last_step_ms = 0, last_check_ms = 0, last_presents = 0;
+            std::uint64_t stuck_since_ms = 0, last_limit = 0;
+            while (!g_finished.load()) {
+                // With fast checks on, sample usage every 250 ms even outside the 600 MiB band;
+                // the rest of the check is throttled to one second while safely outside it. This
+                // detects a sudden crossing without sleeping through the start of a burst.
+                Sleep(thresholds.fast_enabled ? 250 : 1000);
+                if (g_finished.load()) break;
+                const auto now_ms = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(
+                    std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(
+                        std::chrono::steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch()).count());
+                const std::uint64_t limit = bb_uwp_app_memory_limit();
+                const std::uint64_t usage = bb_uwp_app_memory_usage();
+                const std::uint64_t headroom = limit == 0 ? ~std::uint64_t{0} :
+                    (usage < limit ? limit - usage : 0);
+                if (last_check_ms && now_ms - last_check_ms < BbWatchdog::TickMs(headroom, thresholds))
+                    continue;
+                last_check_ms = now_ms;
+                const std::uint64_t presents = bbgpu_uwp_present_count();
+                const bool visible = g_app_visible.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
+                if (!visible || presents != last_presents || presents == 0) stuck_since_ms = 0;
+                else if (!stuck_since_ms) stuck_since_ms = now_ms;
+                const std::uint64_t stuck_ms = stuck_since_ms ? now_ms - stuck_since_ms : 0;
+                last_presents = presents;
+                BbWatchdog::Step step = BbWatchdog::Decide(headroom, stuck_ms, thresholds);
+                if (last_limit && limit != last_limit) {
+                    std::printf("UWP watchdog: AppMemoryUsageLimit changed %llu -> %llu MiB\n",
+                                static_cast<unsigned long long>(last_limit >> 20),
+                                static_cast<unsigned long long>(limit >> 20));
+                    last_step_ms = 0;
+                    if (headroom <= thresholds.ladder_bytes && step == BbWatchdog::StepNone)
+                        step = BbWatchdog::StepLadder;
+                }
+                last_limit = limit;
+                // Exit is handled on the monitor, not queued behind a possibly stuck recovery rung.
+                if (step == BbWatchdog::StepExit) {
+                    if (g_watchdog_ran_exit.exchange(true)) continue;
+                    std::printf("UWP watchdog: presents stuck for %llu s at %llu/%llu MiB (level=%u): "
+                                "dumping state, flushing saves and exiting cleanly\n",
+                                static_cast<unsigned long long>(stuck_ms / 1000),
+                                static_cast<unsigned long long>(usage >> 20),
+                                static_cast<unsigned long long>(limit >> 20),
+                                unsigned(winrt::Windows::System::MemoryManager::AppMemoryUsageLevel()));
+                    std::fflush(stdout);
+                    bb_uwp_breadcrumb("watchdog: exiting after a stall at the memory limit");
+                    // The pager-state snapshot and breadcrumbs do not take the pager's commit
+                    // lock. Other reports and fsync can block behind the very stall we are exiting,
+                    // so attempt those on a worker with a deadline and never claim a timed-out save
+                    // flush succeeded. The app still exits if the driver or a file lock is stuck.
+                    runtime_memory_pager_state();
+                    bb_uwp_breadcrumb_dump("watchdog exit");
+                    try {
+                        auto done = std::make_shared<std::promise<void>>();
+                        auto result = done->get_future();
+                        std::thread([done] {
+                            const int flushed = runtime_files_flush();
+                            std::printf("UWP watchdog: flushed %d open save file(s)\n", flushed);
+                            std::fflush(stdout);
+                            runtime_memory_report();
+                            runtime_file_report();
+                            runtime_savedata_report();
+                            runtime_wait_report();
+                            runtime_sample_threads();
+                            bbgpu_thread_op_dump();
+                            std::fflush(stdout);
+                            done->set_value();
+                        }).detach();
+                        if (result.wait_for(std::chrono::seconds(5)) != std::future_status::ready)
+                            std::puts("UWP watchdog: dump/save flush timed out; save flush NOT confirmed");
+                    } catch (...) {
+                        std::puts("UWP watchdog: could not start dump/save worker; save flush NOT confirmed");
+                    }
+                    std::fflush(stdout);
+                    close_app("watchdog: presents stuck at the app memory limit");
+                }
+                if (!BbWatchdog::ShouldRun(step, highest_scheduled, now_ms, last_step_ms, thresholds))
+                    continue;
+                BbWatchdog::Step steps[4]{};
+                const unsigned count = BbWatchdog::NextSteps(step, highest_scheduled, steps, 4);
+                const std::uint64_t need = headroom == ~std::uint64_t{0} ? (std::uint64_t{32} << 20) :
+                    std::max<std::uint64_t>(headroom < thresholds.ladder_bytes
+                        ? thresholds.ladder_bytes - headroom : 0, std::uint64_t{32} << 20);
+                for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
+                    const auto current = steps[i];
+                    std::scoped_lock lock{queue->mutex};
+                    if (queue->pending[int(current)] || queue->jobs.size() >= 4) continue;
+                    queue->pending[int(current)] = true;
+                    queue->jobs.push_back({current, need, headroom, usage, limit, presents, stuck_ms});
+                    std::printf("UWP watchdog: step %s queued\n", BbWatchdog::StepName(current));
+                    std::fflush(stdout);
+                    if (current > highest_scheduled) highest_scheduled = current;
+                    last_step_ms = now_ms;
+                    queue->ready.notify_one();
+                }
+            }
+            queue->ready.notify_one();
+        }).detach();
+
