diff --git a/xbox/platform/storage_report.cpp b/xbox/platform/storage_report.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..7ee2f42
--- /dev/null
+++ b/xbox/platform/storage_report.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,370 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+// bbport: the OS half of the storage report (storage_report.h holds the testable half).
+//
+// Every volume is probed the same way: GetDiskFreeSpaceExW for the numbers, then a 64 KiB file that
+// is written, flushed and deleted. The probe is what makes the answer real - a UWP app is allowed to
+// read most volumes and write almost none of them, and "24 GB free on D:" is worse than useless if
+// the swap file cannot live there. The probe file is opened with FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE so a
+// crash cannot leave litter on a player's drive.
+
+#include "storage_report.h"
+
+#include <algorithm>
+#include <chrono>
+#include <cstddef>
+#include <cstdio>
+#include <cstring>
+#include <string>
+#include <vector>
+
+#ifndef WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
+#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
+#endif
+#include <windows.h>
+#include <fileapifromapp.h>
+#include <memoryapi.h>
+#include <winioctl.h>
+
+namespace BbStorage {
+namespace {
+
+constexpr std::uint64_t kProbeBytes = 64 * 1024;
+
+/// The LocalState path Report() was called with, for LocalStateFreeBytes().
+std::string g_local_dir;
+
+/// The app's own volume letter from a root path like `C:\Users\...\LocalState`.
+char LetterOf(const std::string& path) {
+    if (path.size() >= 2 && path[1] == ':') {
+        char letter = path[0];
+        if (letter >= 'a' && letter <= 'z') letter = char(letter - 'a' + 'A');
+        return letter;
+    }
+    return 0;
+}
+
+std::wstring Wide(const std::string& text) {
+    if (text.empty()) return {};
+    const int length = MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, 0, text.c_str(), (int)text.size(), nullptr, 0);
+    if (length <= 0) return {};
+    std::wstring wide((size_t)length, L'\0');
+    MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, 0, text.c_str(), (int)text.size(), wide.data(), length);
+    return wide;
+}
+
+bool ProbeWritable(const std::wstring& root) {
+    // Never truncate a pre-existing file, even on a drive the app can write.
+    const std::wstring path = root + L"bbport-probe-" + std::to_wstring(GetCurrentProcessId()) +
+                              L"-" + std::to_wstring(GetTickCount64()) + L".tmp";
+    CREATEFILE2_EXTENDED_PARAMETERS params{};
+    params.dwSize = sizeof(params);
+    params.dwFileAttributes = FILE_ATTRIBUTE_TEMPORARY;
+    params.dwFileFlags = FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE;
+    const HANDLE file = CreateFile2FromAppW(path.c_str(), GENERIC_WRITE, 0, CREATE_NEW, &params);
+    if (file == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
+        return false;
+    }
+    std::vector<char> block(kProbeBytes, 0x5a);
+    DWORD written = 0;
+    const bool ok = WriteFile(file, block.data(), (DWORD)block.size(), &written, nullptr) != FALSE &&
+                    written == block.size();
+    CloseHandle(file);
+    return ok;
+}
+
+// DRIVE_FIXED describes the medium, not the transport: many USB HDDs report DRIVE_FIXED. Query
+// the actual device bus as well; when the sandbox denies this query, err on the side of never using
+// USB rather than guessing from a letter. This may conservatively exclude D: on some consoles.
+VolumeBus QueryVolumeBus(char letter) {
+    std::wstring device = L"\\\\.\\";
+    device.push_back(static_cast<wchar_t>(letter));
+    device += L":";
+    CREATEFILE2_EXTENDED_PARAMETERS params{};
+    params.dwSize = sizeof(params);
+    HANDLE handle = CreateFile2FromAppW(device.c_str(), 0, FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE,
+                                        OPEN_EXISTING, &params);
+    if (handle == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) return VolumeBus::Unknown;
+    STORAGE_PROPERTY_QUERY query{};
+    query.PropertyId = StorageDeviceProperty;
+    query.QueryType = PropertyStandardQuery;
+    alignas(STORAGE_DEVICE_DESCRIPTOR) unsigned char data[1024]{};
+    DWORD returned = 0;
+    const BOOL ok = DeviceIoControl(handle, IOCTL_STORAGE_QUERY_PROPERTY, &query, sizeof(query),
+                                    data, sizeof(data), &returned, nullptr);
+    CloseHandle(handle);
+    if (!ok || returned < offsetof(STORAGE_DEVICE_DESCRIPTOR, BusType) + sizeof(STORAGE_BUS_TYPE))
+        return VolumeBus::Unknown;
+    const auto* descriptor = reinterpret_cast<const STORAGE_DEVICE_DESCRIPTOR*>(data);
+    if (descriptor->RemovableMedia || descriptor->BusType == BusTypeUsb ||
+        descriptor->BusType == BusTypeSd || descriptor->BusType == BusTypeMmc)
+        return VolumeBus::UsbOrRemovable;
+    // Virtual, file-backed, network and unknown buses can hide the underlying transport. Exclude
+    // those rather than reporting that a USB-backed virtual disk is safe.
+    switch (descriptor->BusType) {
+    case BusTypeScsi: case BusTypeAtapi: case BusTypeAta: case BusTypeRAID:
+    case BusTypeSas: case BusTypeSata: case BusTypeNvme:
+        return VolumeBus::NonUsb;
+    default:
+        return VolumeBus::Unknown;
+    }
+}
+
+std::vector<Volume> QueryVolumes(char local_letter) {
+    std::vector<Volume> volumes;
+    for (char letter = 'C'; letter <= 'Z'; ++letter) {
+        std::wstring root;
+        root.push_back((wchar_t)letter);
+        root += L":\\";
+        ULARGE_INTEGER free_bytes{}, total_bytes{};
+        if (!GetDiskFreeSpaceExW(root.c_str(), &free_bytes, &total_bytes, nullptr)) {
+            continue;  // no such volume, or not visible to this app
+        }
+        if (total_bytes.QuadPart == 0) continue;
+        Volume volume;
+        volume.letter = letter;
+        volume.total = total_bytes.QuadPart;
+        volume.free = free_bytes.QuadPart;
+        volume.writable = ProbeWritable(root);
+        switch (GetDriveTypeW(root.c_str())) {
+        case DRIVE_FIXED: volume.kind = VolumeKind::Fixed; break;
+        case DRIVE_REMOVABLE: volume.kind = VolumeKind::Removable; break;
+        case DRIVE_UNKNOWN: case DRIVE_NO_ROOT_DIR: volume.kind = VolumeKind::Unknown; break;
+        default: volume.kind = VolumeKind::Other; break;
+        }
+        volume.bus = volume.kind == VolumeKind::Removable ? VolumeBus::UsbOrRemovable :
+                     volume.kind == VolumeKind::Fixed ? QueryVolumeBus(letter) : VolumeBus::Unknown;
+        volumes.push_back(volume);
+        if (volumes.size() >= 16) break;
+    }
+    (void)local_letter;
+    return volumes;
+}
+
+} // namespace
+
+static const char* KindName(VolumeKind kind) {
+    switch (kind) {
+    case VolumeKind::Fixed: return "fixed";
+    case VolumeKind::Removable: return "removable";
+    case VolumeKind::Other: return "other (not eligible)";
+    default: return "unknown (not eligible)";
+    }
+}
+
+static const char* BusName(VolumeBus bus) {
+    switch (bus) {
+    case VolumeBus::NonUsb: return "verified non-USB";
+    case VolumeBus::UsbOrRemovable: return "USB/removable";
+    default: return "unknown (not eligible)";
+    }
+}
+
+// Parent directory with a trailing separator, or empty for a relative/UNC path. Requiring an
+// absolute drive path makes removable-device validation unambiguous and avoids clobbering an
+// unrelated file through a relative path.
+static std::string SwapParent(const std::string& path) {
+    if (path.size() < 4 || !LetterOf(path) || (path[2] != '\\' && path[2] != '/')) return {};
+    const auto at = path.find_last_of("\\/");
+    if (at == std::string::npos || at + 1 >= path.size()) return {};
+    return path.substr(0, at + 1);
+}
+
+static std::string UniqueSwapPath(const std::string& parent) {
+    return parent + "bloodborne-swap-" + std::to_string(GetCurrentProcessId()) + "-" +
+           std::to_string(GetTickCount64()) + ".bin";
+}
+
+SwapChoice ChooseSwap(const std::string& local_dir, const std::string& requested_path,
+                      const char* requested_source, bool auto_select, std::uint64_t reserve) {
+    const char local_letter = LetterOf(local_dir);
+    const std::string local_parent = local_dir + (local_dir.empty() || local_dir.back() == '\\' ? "" : "\\");
+    const auto volumes = QueryVolumes(local_letter);
+    auto free_of = [&](char letter) -> std::uint64_t {
+        for (const auto& volume : volumes) if (volume.letter == letter) return volume.free;
+        ULARGE_INTEGER available{};
+        const auto wide = Wide(local_parent);
+        return letter == local_letter && !wide.empty() &&
+                       GetDiskFreeSpaceExW(wide.c_str(), &available, nullptr, nullptr)
+                   ? available.QuadPart : 0;
+    };
+    if (!requested_path.empty()) {
+        const auto parent = SwapParent(requested_path);
+        const char letter = LetterOf(requested_path);
+        bool eligible = letter == local_letter && letter != 0;
+        if (!eligible) {
+            for (const auto& v : volumes) {
+                if (v.letter == letter && v.kind == VolumeKind::Fixed &&
+                    v.bus == VolumeBus::NonUsb) eligible = true;
+            }
+        }
+        const auto wide_path = Wide(requested_path);
+        WIN32_FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DATA attr{};
+        const bool exists = !wide_path.empty() &&
+            GetFileAttributesExFromAppW(wide_path.c_str(), GetFileExInfoStandard, &attr);
+        const DWORD attr_error = exists ? ERROR_SUCCESS : GetLastError();
+        const bool definitely_missing = !exists &&
+            (attr_error == ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND || attr_error == ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND);
+        if (!parent.empty() && eligible && definitely_missing && ProbeWritable(Wide(parent))) {
+            return {requested_path, requested_source ? requested_source : "explicit", letter,
+                    free_of(letter), letter == local_letter};
+        }
+        std::printf("UWP swap: requested path rejected (relative, removable/unknown, existing, or "
+                    "not writable); no existing file will be overwritten: %s\n", requested_path.c_str());
+    }
+    if (auto_select) {
+        if (const Volume* best = BestSwapVolume(volumes, local_letter, reserve)) {
+            const std::string parent = std::string(1, best->letter) + ":\\";
+            return {UniqueSwapPath(parent), "automatic", best->letter, best->free, false};
+        }
+        std::puts("UWP swap: no writable, non-removable alternative with space above the reserve; "
+                  "falling back to LocalState");
+    }
+    return {UniqueSwapPath(local_parent), auto_select ? "LocalState fallback" : "LocalState (auto off)",
+            local_letter, free_of(local_letter), true};
+}
+
+void TestSwapSpeed(const SwapChoice& choice, std::uint64_t reserve, bool enabled) {
+    constexpr std::uint64_t total = std::uint64_t{64} << 20;
+    constexpr DWORD block_size = 1024 * 1024;
+    if (!enabled) {
+        std::puts("UWP swap speed: 64 MiB test disabled (swap_speed_test=0)");
+        return;
+    }
+    if (choice.path.empty() || choice.free <= reserve || choice.free - reserve < total) {
+        std::puts("UWP swap speed: 64 MiB test skipped; not enough free space above reserve");
+        return;
+    }
+    const std::string parent = SwapParent(choice.path);
+    if (parent.empty()) {
+        std::puts("UWP swap speed: invalid path; test skipped");
+        return;
+    }
+    const std::wstring path = Wide(parent + "bbport-speed-" + std::to_string(GetCurrentProcessId()) +
+                                   "-" + std::to_string(GetTickCount64()) + ".tmp");
+    CREATEFILE2_EXTENDED_PARAMETERS params{};
+    params.dwSize = sizeof(params);
+    params.dwFileAttributes = FILE_ATTRIBUTE_TEMPORARY;
+    params.dwFileFlags = FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE | FILE_FLAG_WRITE_THROUGH |
+                         FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING | FILE_FLAG_SEQUENTIAL_SCAN;
+    HANDLE file = CreateFile2FromAppW(path.c_str(), GENERIC_WRITE | GENERIC_READ, 0, CREATE_NEW, &params);
+    if (file == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
+        std::printf("UWP swap speed: 64 MiB test could not create temporary file (error %lu)\n", GetLastError());
+        return;
+    }
+    auto* block = static_cast<unsigned char*>(
+        VirtualAllocFromApp(nullptr, block_size, MEM_RESERVE | MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE));
+    if (!block) {
+        std::printf("UWP swap speed: aligned 1 MiB buffer unavailable (error %lu)\n", GetLastError());
+        CloseHandle(file);
+        return;
+    }
+    // Incompressible-ish test data, not a sparse file of zeros. VirtualAlloc is page aligned for
+    // unbuffered I/O and every transfer size and offset is a multiple of 1 MiB.
+    std::uint32_t state = 0x12345678;
+    for (DWORD i = 0; i < block_size; ++i) {
+        state ^= state << 13; state ^= state >> 17; state ^= state << 5;
+        block[i] = static_cast<unsigned char>(state);
+    }
+    const auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
+    bool ok = true;
+    DWORD done = 0;
+    for (unsigned i = 0; i < 64 && ok; ++i)
+        ok = WriteFile(file, block, block_size, &done, nullptr) && done == block_size;
+    if (ok) ok = FlushFileBuffers(file) != FALSE;
+    const auto written = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
+    LARGE_INTEGER zero{};
+    if (ok) ok = SetFilePointerEx(file, zero, nullptr, FILE_BEGIN) != FALSE;
+    for (unsigned i = 0; i < 64 && ok; ++i)
+        ok = ReadFile(file, block, block_size, &done, nullptr) && done == block_size;
+    const auto read = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
+    const DWORD error = ok ? ERROR_SUCCESS : GetLastError();
+    if (ok) {
+        const double write_s = std::chrono::duration<double>(written - start).count();
+        const double read_s = std::chrono::duration<double>(read - written).count();
+        std::printf("UWP swap speed: 64 MiB %c: unbuffered write %.1f MiB/s (%.0f ms), "
+                    "read %.1f MiB/s (%.0f ms)\n", choice.letter,
+                    write_s > 0 ? 64.0 / write_s : 0, write_s * 1000,
+                    read_s > 0 ? 64.0 / read_s : 0, read_s * 1000);
+    } else {
+        std::printf("UWP swap speed: 64 MiB test incomplete (error %lu)\n", error);
+    }
+    CloseHandle(file);
+    VirtualFree(block, 0, MEM_RELEASE);
+    std::fflush(stdout);
+}
+
+int Report(const char* local_dir) {
+    const std::string local = local_dir ? local_dir : "";
+    g_local_dir = local;
+    const char local_letter = LetterOf(local);
+
+    std::printf("UWP storage: LocalState is on %c: (%s)\n", local_letter ? local_letter : '?',
+                local.c_str());
+    const std::vector<Volume> volumes = QueryVolumes(local_letter);
+    if (volumes.empty()) {
+        std::puts("UWP storage: no volume answered GetDiskFreeSpaceEx; storage warnings unavailable");
+        return 0;
+    }
+    std::uint64_t local_free = 0, local_total = 0;
+    for (const Volume& volume : volumes) {
+        std::printf("UWP storage: %c: total=%s free=%s%s%s type=%s bus=%s\n", volume.letter,
+                    FormatBytes(volume.total).c_str(), FormatBytes(volume.free).c_str(),
+                    volume.letter == local_letter ? " [LocalState]" : "",
+                    volume.writable ? " writable" : " read-only to this app", KindName(volume.kind), BusName(volume.bus));
+        if (volume.letter == local_letter) {
+            local_free = volume.free;
+            local_total = volume.total;
+        }
+    }
+
+    // Where the space went. The swap file is the one this port creates, and it is the one a player
+    // can delete; the dump and the saves are not ours to move.
+    if (!local.empty()) {
+        FolderSize total;
+        const auto folders = WalkFolders(std::filesystem::path(local), total);
+        for (const auto& folder : folders) {
+            std::printf("UWP storage: LocalState\\%s = %s in %llu file(s)%s\n", folder.name.c_str(),
+                        FormatBytes(folder.bytes).c_str(),
+                        static_cast<unsigned long long>(folder.files),
+                        folder.truncated ? " (walk capped: a lower bound)" : "");
+        }
+        std::printf("UWP storage: LocalState total = %s in %llu file(s) of %s on the volume\n",
+                    FormatBytes(total.bytes).c_str(),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(total.files),
+                    FormatBytes(local_total).c_str());
+    }
+
+    if (const Volume* best = BestSwapVolume(volumes, local_letter, std::uint64_t{384} << 20)) {
+        std::printf("UWP storage: largest eligible fixed volume other than LocalState is %c: "
+                    "with %s free (swap path printed in the run header)\n",
+                    best->letter, FormatBytes(best->free).c_str());
+    } else {
+        std::puts("UWP storage: no other writable fixed volume confirmed; removable and unknown "
+                  "volumes are excluded from automatic swap");
+    }
+
+    if (LowStorage(local_free)) {
+        std::printf("UWP STORAGE WARNING: %s free on %c:, below the %s this port wants for the swap "
+                    "for the game's own writes. The chosen swap volume is reported separately.\n",
+                    FormatBytes(local_free).c_str(), local_letter ? local_letter : '?',
+                    FormatBytes(kLowStorageBytes).c_str());
+        return 1;
+    }
+    return 0;
+}
+
+std::uint64_t LocalStateFreeBytes() {
+    // The volume is derived from the path Report() was given, not re-queried: the app has exactly
+    // one LocalState, and asking WinRT again every second would be a package lookup per heartbeat.
+    if (g_local_dir.empty()) return 0;
+    const char letter = LetterOf(g_local_dir);
+    if (!letter) return 0;
+    std::wstring root;
+    root.push_back((wchar_t)letter);
+    root += L":\\";
+    ULARGE_INTEGER free_bytes{}, total_bytes{};
+    if (!GetDiskFreeSpaceExW(root.c_str(), &free_bytes, &total_bytes, nullptr)) return 0;
+    return free_bytes.QuadPart;
+}
+
+} // namespace BbStorage
diff --git a/xbox/platform/storage_report.h b/xbox/platform/storage_report.h
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..1af7068
--- /dev/null
+++ b/xbox/platform/storage_report.h
@@ -0,0 +1,184 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+// bbport: what the console's storage actually looks like, and what LocalState is spending it on.
+//
+// `.819` ended the way it did because the swap file's volume had 867 MiB free while the console had
+// 30 GB elsewhere: the pager was capped to 483 MiB, the volume filled, 6,828 writes were refused and
+// the app died at 5,116/5,120 MiB with 1,171 MiB of pageable memory still resident. Nothing in the
+// log said any of that - the cap line reported the number it chose, not the one next to it.
+//
+// So this reports every volume the app can see (total, free, and whether the app may write there -
+// measured by creating a file, not guessed from the drive letter), and the size of each top-level
+// folder in LocalState, which is where the swap file, the pipeline cache, the prepared dump and the
+// game's own saves share one volume. It also answers "is there a better volume for the swap file"
+// with a name and a number rather than a suggestion.
+//
+// The pure parts (formatting, the verdict, the folder walk) are inline and free of Win32 so they are
+// testable off-console; storage_report.cpp is the part that calls the OS.
+#pragma once
+
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <cstdio>
+#include <filesystem>
+#include <string>
+#include <vector>
+
+namespace BbStorage {
+
+enum class VolumeKind { Unknown, Fixed, Removable, Other };
+// A fixed drive can still be an external USB hard disk; media type alone does not prove the bus.
+enum class VolumeBus { Unknown, NonUsb, UsbOrRemovable };
+
+struct Volume {
+    char letter = 0;          ///< 'Q', 'D', ...
+    std::uint64_t total = 0;  ///< bytes, 0 when the query failed
+    std::uint64_t free = 0;
+    bool writable = false;    ///< a 64 KiB probe file was created and removed here
+    VolumeKind kind = VolumeKind::Unknown; ///< unknown is NOT considered safe for automatic swap
+    VolumeBus bus = VolumeBus::Unknown;   ///< unknown/USB must not be chosen automatically
+};
+
+struct SwapChoice {
+    std::string path;
+    std::string source;  ///< environment, ini, automatic, or LocalState fallback
+    char letter = 0;
+    std::uint64_t free = 0;
+    bool local = true;
+};
+
+struct FolderSize {
+    std::string name;
+    std::uint64_t bytes = 0;
+    std::uint64_t files = 0;
+    bool truncated = false;   ///< the walk hit its entry cap (size is then a lower bound)
+};
+
+/// Below this much free space on the volume that holds LocalState, the run is warned about before it
+/// starts rather than at the point where the pager is capped to it.
+inline constexpr std::uint64_t kLowStorageBytes = std::uint64_t{1024} << 20;  // 1 GiB
+
+/// Human-readable size, for the log and the warning. One decimal below a GiB, none above.
+inline std::string FormatBytes(std::uint64_t bytes) {
+    char text[32];
+    if (bytes >= (std::uint64_t{1} << 30)) {
+        std::snprintf(text, sizeof(text), "%.1f GiB", double(bytes) / double(std::uint64_t{1} << 30));
+    } else if (bytes >= (std::uint64_t{1} << 20)) {
+        std::snprintf(text, sizeof(text), "%llu MiB",
+                      static_cast<unsigned long long>(bytes >> 20));
+    } else {
+        std::snprintf(text, sizeof(text), "%llu KiB",
+                      static_cast<unsigned long long>(bytes >> 10));
+    }
+    return text;
+}
+
+/// The verdict for one volume: is this run about to be limited by storage?
+inline bool LowStorage(std::uint64_t free_bytes) {
+    return free_bytes < kLowStorageBytes;
+}
+
+/// The volume with the most free space that the app may write to, or nullptr. `skip` is the letter
+/// of the volume to ignore (the app volume itself, when the caller wants an alternative, or the USB
+/// drive holding the dump - writing the swap file there would be both slow and rude).
+inline const Volume* BestWritable(const std::vector<Volume>& volumes, char skip) {
+    const Volume* best = nullptr;
+    for (const Volume& volume : volumes) {
+        if (!volume.writable || volume.letter == skip) continue;
+        if (!best || volume.free > best->free) best = &volume;
+    }
+    return best;
+}
+
+/// Automatic swap placement: only an independently probed writable FIXED volume may beat
+/// LocalState. DRIVE_FIXED alone does not rule out a USB HDD: require a confirmed non-USB bus too;
+/// unknown/removable/remote devices are rejected.
+/// D wins a tie, otherwise the one with most free bytes wins. Below the reserve it is unusable.
+inline const Volume* BestSwapVolume(const std::vector<Volume>& volumes, char local,
+                                     std::uint64_t reserve) {
+    const Volume* best = nullptr;
+    for (const Volume& volume : volumes) {
+        if (!volume.writable || volume.letter == local || volume.kind != VolumeKind::Fixed ||
+            volume.bus != VolumeBus::NonUsb || volume.free <= reserve) continue;
+        if (!best || volume.free > best->free ||
+            (volume.free == best->free && volume.letter == 'D' && best->letter != 'D')) {
+            best = &volume;
+        }
+    }
+    return best;
+}
+
+/// Select a location (including strict removable-drive and existing-file checks). The caller applies
+/// env/ini precedence and provides the maximum free-space reserve. No file is overwritten.
+SwapChoice ChooseSwap(const std::string& local_dir, const std::string& requested_path,
+                      const char* requested_source, bool auto_select, std::uint64_t reserve);
+
+/// An opt-in 64 MiB temporary-file throughput test on the selected volume. Logs actual write/read
+/// timings or why it could not safely run. The file uses CREATE_NEW + DELETE_ON_CLOSE.
+void TestSwapSpeed(const SwapChoice& choice, std::uint64_t reserve, bool enabled);
+
+/// Size of every immediate child of `root`, files counted through the whole subtree.
+/// `cap` bounds the number of entries examined, and a folder that hits it is marked `truncated` so a
+/// huge tree cannot turn a startup diagnostic into a startup delay. Missing folders are skipped.
+inline std::vector<FolderSize> WalkFolders(const std::filesystem::path& root, FolderSize& root_total,
+                                           std::uint64_t cap = 200000) {
+    std::vector<FolderSize> out;
+    root_total = FolderSize{};
+    root_total.name = "LocalState";
+    std::error_code ec;
+    if (!std::filesystem::exists(root, ec)) {
+        return out;
+    }
+    std::vector<std::filesystem::path> children;
+    for (std::filesystem::directory_iterator it{root, ec}, end; !ec && it != end; it.increment(ec)) {
+        children.push_back(it->path());
+    }
+    std::uint64_t budget = cap;
+    for (const auto& child : children) {
+        FolderSize entry;
+        entry.name = child.filename().string();
+        if (std::filesystem::is_directory(child, ec)) {
+            for (std::filesystem::recursive_directory_iterator it{child, ec}, end;
+                 !ec && it != end; it.increment(ec)) {
+                if (budget == 0) {
+                    entry.truncated = true;
+                    break;
+                }
+                --budget;
+                std::error_code size_ec;
+                if (it->is_regular_file(size_ec)) {
+                    entry.bytes += std::filesystem::file_size(it->path(), size_ec);
+                    ++entry.files;
+                }
+            }
+            ec.clear();
+        } else {
+            std::error_code size_ec;
+            entry.bytes = std::filesystem::file_size(child, size_ec);
+            entry.files = entry.bytes ? 1 : 0;
+        }
+        root_total.bytes += entry.bytes;
+        root_total.files += entry.files;
+        root_total.truncated = root_total.truncated || entry.truncated;
+        out.push_back(std::move(entry));
+    }
+    return out;
+}
+
+/// One line per volume, one per folder, and the recommendation. `local_dir` is the UTF-8 LocalState
+/// path. Returns 1 when storage is low (the caller shows the warning), 0 otherwise.
+int Report(const char* local_dir);
+
+/// Free bytes on the volume that holds LocalState. Cached for a second: the heartbeat asks every
+/// sample and the answer cannot change faster than a write can fill it.
+std::uint64_t LocalStateFreeBytes();
+
+/// The text of the visible warning. Inline, so the test can hold its wording without linking the
+/// OS half: it is what the player is asked to act on, and "low storage" alone would not say what to
+/// free or why the game cares.
+inline std::string WarningText() {
+    return std::string("Low storage: the volume holding the game's data has less than ") +
+           FormatBytes(kLowStorageBytes) +
+           " free. Saves and caches also need that space even if swap is on another volume. "
+           "Free space on that volume (old logs, captures, other games) before playing.";
+}
+
+} // namespace BbStorage
diff --git a/xbox/platform/swap_codec.h b/xbox/platform/swap_codec.h
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..06fbfb8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/xbox/platform/swap_codec.h
@@ -0,0 +1,233 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+//
+// bbport: the page codec for the UWP swap file.
+//
+// Why this exists: the console accepted every page we wrote until `disk pages=1171 MiB` and then
+// answered ERROR_DISK_FULL (.908, docs/hardware-test-23) - with 767 MiB of guest memory still
+// pageable and the app limit 780 MiB away. The device is simply almost full, and 1.17 GiB of swap
+// is all the room this port will ever get on it. Guest private pages compress well (a heap of
+// pointers, float data, unused buffers and zeroed blocks), so storing each page compressed is the
+// only remaining way to raise how much guest memory can live on that 1.17 GiB.
+//
+// Format: LZ4 block, one page at a time, no frame. The caller writes a 2-byte little-endian length
+// in front of the payload and reads it back; a stored length equal to the page size means the page
+// was written raw (the codec did not shrink it). Compressed payloads are always smaller than the
+// page, so a corrupt length is detectable by the caller's bound check.
+//
+// Both functions are plain C with no Windows dependency: xbox/tests/swap_codec_test.cpp round-trips
+// random, zero, text-like and page-like data through them in CI, and the runtime verifies every
+// page with uwp_swap_hash on the way back in, so a codec bug shows up as a failed read rather than
+// as silently corrupted guest memory.
+
+#pragma once
+
+#include <stddef.h>
+#include <stdint.h>
+#include <string.h>
+
+#define UWP_LZ_HASH_BITS 14
+#define UWP_LZ_MIN_MATCH 4
+#define UWP_LZ_LAST_LITERALS 8
+#define UWP_LZ_MAX_OFFSET 65535
+#define UWP_LZ_MIN_LENGTH 13
+
+static uint32_t uwp_lz_read32(const unsigned char *p) {
+    uint32_t v;
+    memcpy(&v, p, sizeof(v));
+    return v;
+}
+
+static uint32_t uwp_lz_hash(uint32_t sequence) {
+    return (sequence * UINT32_C(2654435761)) >> (32 - UWP_LZ_HASH_BITS);
+}
+
+// Returns the compressed size, or 0 when the page does not compress into `capacity` bytes (the
+// caller then stores it raw). `capacity` must be at least the source size for the 0 case to be
+// meaningful; the runtime passes the page size.
+static size_t uwp_lz_compress(const unsigned char *source, size_t size, unsigned char *dest,
+                              size_t capacity, void *scratch) {
+    // `scratch` is UWP_LZ_HASH_BITS worth of int32 offsets; the caller owns it so this function is
+    // reentrant and allocates nothing.
+    int32_t *table = (int32_t *)scratch;
+    memset(table, 0xFF, sizeof(int32_t) << UWP_LZ_HASH_BITS);
+    size_t ip = 0;
+    size_t anchor = 0;
+    size_t op = 0;
+    if (size < UWP_LZ_MIN_LENGTH) {
+        return 0;
+    }
+    const size_t limit = size - UWP_LZ_LAST_LITERALS;
+    while (ip < limit) {
+        const uint32_t sequence = uwp_lz_read32(source + ip);
+        const uint32_t hash = uwp_lz_hash(sequence);
+        const int32_t reference = table[hash];
+        table[hash] = (int32_t)ip;
+        if (reference < 0 || (size_t)(ip - (size_t)reference) > UWP_LZ_MAX_OFFSET ||
+            uwp_lz_read32(source + (size_t)reference) != sequence) {
+            ++ip;
+            continue;
+        }
+        const size_t start = (size_t)reference;
+        size_t match = UWP_LZ_MIN_MATCH;
+        // A match never reaches the end of the block: the last UWP_LZ_LAST_LITERALS bytes stay
+        // literals, which is what makes the final sequence a literals-only one (and therefore what
+        // lets the decoder finish exactly at the last byte of the page).
+        const size_t match_limit = size - UWP_LZ_LAST_LITERALS;
+        while (ip + match < match_limit && source[start + match] == source[ip + match]) {
+            ++match;
+        }
+        const size_t literals = ip - anchor;
+        const size_t match_code = match - UWP_LZ_MIN_MATCH;
+        // token + literal extensions + literals + 2-byte offset + match extensions. The match
+        // length itself is never stored as a byte, only its extension bytes past the nibble.
+        size_t need = 1 + literals + 2;
+        if (literals >= 15) {
+            need += (literals - 15) / 255 + 1;
+        }
+        if (match_code >= 15) {
+            need += (match_code - 15) / 255 + 1;
+        }
+        if (op + need > capacity) {
+            return 0;
+        }
+        size_t token_at = op++;
+        const size_t literal_header = literals >= 15 ? 15 : literals;
+        unsigned char token = (unsigned char)(literal_header << 4);
+        if (literals >= 15) {
+            size_t rest = literals - 15;
+            while (rest >= 255) {
+                dest[op++] = 255;
+                rest -= 255;
+            }
+            dest[op++] = (unsigned char)rest;
+        }
+        memcpy(dest + op, source + anchor, literals);
+        op += literals;
+        const size_t offset = ip - start;
+        dest[op++] = (unsigned char)(offset & 0xFF);
+        dest[op++] = (unsigned char)(offset >> 8);
+        const size_t match_header = match_code >= 15 ? 15 : match_code;
+        token |= (unsigned char)match_header;
+        dest[token_at] = token;
+        if (match_code >= 15) {
+            size_t rest = match_code - 15;
+            while (rest >= 255) {
+                dest[op++] = 255;
+                rest -= 255;
+            }
+            dest[op++] = (unsigned char)rest;
+        }
+        ip += match;
+        anchor = ip;
+        if (ip >= limit) {
+            break;
+        }
+        // Index the position just behind the match, as LZ4 does: it is the one most likely to be
+        // useful for the next sequence and costs nothing.
+        if (ip >= 2) {
+            table[uwp_lz_hash(uwp_lz_read32(source + ip - 2))] = (int32_t)(ip - 2);
+        }
+    }
+    const size_t literals = size - anchor;
+    size_t need = 1 + literals;
+    if (literals >= 15) {
+        need += (literals - 15) / 255 + 1;
+    }
+    if (op + need > capacity) {
+        return 0;
+    }
+    const size_t token_at = op++;
+    const size_t literal_header = literals >= 15 ? 15 : literals;
+    dest[token_at] = (unsigned char)(literal_header << 4);
+    if (literals >= 15) {
+        size_t rest = literals - 15;
+        while (rest >= 255) {
+            dest[op++] = 255;
+            rest -= 255;
+        }
+        dest[op++] = (unsigned char)rest;
+    }
+    memcpy(dest + op, source + anchor, literals);
+    op += literals;
+    return op;
+}
+
+// One page as the swap file stores it: a 2-byte little-endian length header, then either an LZ4
+// block or the page verbatim.
+//
+// bbport: the rule this enforces is the one the read path depends on. A stored length equal to the
+// page size means "raw", so a *compressed* block of exactly that size is indistinguishable from a
+// raw one - and reading it back as raw hands the guest 16 KiB of LZ4 bytes. That is not a corner
+// case: `uwp_lz_compress` returns exactly `size` for a nearly-incompressible page (measured on the
+// host: 235 of 400,000 page-shaped pages, about 1 in 1,700), and the `.437` console run stopped on
+// `UWP promoted page integrity at 000000104D3B8000` after 65,475 stored pages because of it
+// (docs/hardware-test-26). Anything that does not come out strictly smaller is stored raw here, so
+// the ambiguity cannot reach the file.
+//
+// Returns the bytes written to `dest`; `capacity` must be at least `size` + 2 and `size` must fit
+// in the 16-bit header (both hold for a 16 KiB page). *raw is set to 1 for the raw fallback.
+static size_t uwp_swap_encode_page(const unsigned char *source, size_t size, unsigned char *dest,
+                                   size_t capacity, void *scratch, int *raw) {
+    size_t length = size;
+    int stored_raw = 1;
+    if (size <= UINT16_MAX && capacity >= size + 2) {
+        const size_t packed = uwp_lz_compress(source, size, dest + 2, capacity - 2, scratch);
+        if (packed != 0 && packed < size) {
+            length = packed;
+            stored_raw = 0;
+        }
+    }
+    if (stored_raw) memcpy(dest + 2, source, size);
+    dest[0] = (unsigned char)(length & 0xFF);
+    dest[1] = (unsigned char)((length >> 8) & 0xFF);
+    if (raw) *raw = stored_raw;
+    return length + 2;
+}
+
+// Returns the number of bytes written to `dest` (exactly `capacity` on success) or 0 on malformed
+// input - a length overrun, a back-reference before the start of the block, or a short block.
+static size_t uwp_lz_decompress(const unsigned char *source, size_t size, unsigned char *dest,
+                                size_t capacity) {
+    size_t ip = 0;
+    size_t op = 0;
+    while (ip < size) {
+        const unsigned char token = source[ip++];
+        size_t literals = token >> 4;
+        if (literals == 15) {
+            unsigned char extra;
+            do {
+                if (ip >= size) return 0;
+                extra = source[ip++];
+                literals += extra;
+            } while (extra == 255);
+        }
+        if (literals > size - ip || literals > capacity - op) return 0;
+        memcpy(dest + op, source + ip, literals);
+        ip += literals;
+        op += literals;
+        if (ip == size) {
+            break; // the last sequence carries literals only
+        }
+        if (size - ip < 2) return 0;
+        const size_t offset = (size_t)source[ip] | ((size_t)source[ip + 1] << 8);
+        ip += 2;
+        if (offset == 0 || offset > op) return 0;
+        size_t match = (size_t)(token & 0x0F);
+        if (match == 15) {
+            unsigned char extra;
+            do {
+                if (ip >= size) return 0;
+                extra = source[ip++];
+                match += extra;
+            } while (extra == 255);
+        }
+        match += UWP_LZ_MIN_MATCH;
+        if (match > capacity - op) return 0;
+        const unsigned char *from = dest + op - offset;
+        for (size_t i = 0; i < match; ++i) {
+            dest[op + i] = from[i];
+        }
+        op += match;
+    }
+    return op == capacity ? op : 0;
+}
diff --git a/xbox/platform/swap_pool_accounting.h b/xbox/platform/swap_pool_accounting.h
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cc169de
--- /dev/null
+++ b/xbox/platform/swap_pool_accounting.h
@@ -0,0 +1,32 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+// Portable accounting for the 4 KiB committed pages in the UWP compressed swap pool.
+// The caller serializes access and supplies a zero-initialized bitset of ceil(page_count / 8) bytes.
+#pragma once
+#include <stddef.h>
+#include <stdint.h>
+
+#define BB_POOL_PAGE_SIZE UINT64_C(4096)
+
+// Mark a page-aligned range committed or decommitted. Return bytes whose state actually changed.
+// In particular, recommitting an already committed page after a failed decommit is NOT new usage.
+static inline uint64_t bb_pool_mark_pages(unsigned char *map, uint64_t offset, uint64_t length,
+                                          int committed) {
+    uint64_t changed = 0;
+    const uint64_t first = offset / BB_POOL_PAGE_SIZE;
+    const uint64_t count = length / BB_POOL_PAGE_SIZE;
+    for (uint64_t i = first; i < first + count; ++i) {
+        const unsigned char mask = (unsigned char)(1u << (i & 7u));
+        unsigned char *const cell = &map[i >> 3];
+        const int old = (*cell & mask) != 0;
+        if (old != (committed != 0)) {
+            if (committed) *cell |= mask;
+            else *cell &= (unsigned char)~mask;
+            changed += BB_POOL_PAGE_SIZE;
+        }
+    }
+    return changed;
+}
+
+static inline uint64_t bb_pool_net_saved(uint64_t guest_bytes, uint64_t committed_bytes) {
+    return guest_bytes > committed_bytes ? guest_bytes - committed_bytes : 0;
+}
diff --git a/xbox/platform/watchdog_policy.h b/xbox/platform/watchdog_policy.h
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..f07c8fa
--- /dev/null
+++ b/xbox/platform/watchdog_policy.h
@@ -0,0 +1,223 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+// BUILD 3, item 15: the recovery watchdog's rules, as plain arithmetic.
+//
+// The watchdog is the answer to a shape both `0717` and `819` had: the app sat at its limit for
+// seconds, the collector ran, the pager ran, and nothing was logged between "we are at the limit"
+// and the allocation failure - so the run could not say which step was reached or what each one
+// bought. The rules live here (no threads, no Win32, no Vulkan) so they can be tested on the build
+// machine: xbox/tests/watchdog_policy_test.cpp.
+//
+// Everything is in bytes and milliseconds. The step *order* is the part that has to be right: a
+// smaller headroom must never run a cheaper step, and a stall that is already at the exit threshold
+// must not degrade the resolution first and then find out there is nothing left to try.
+#pragma once
+
+#include <cstdint>
+
+namespace BbWatchdog {
+
+/// What the watchdog does when a threshold is crossed. Numbered by escalation so a caller can log
+/// the step and a test can assert the order; `StepNone` is "nothing to do".
+enum Step : int {
+    StepNone = 0,
+    /// (a) within `ladder_bytes` of the limit: release retired arenas, trim staging, emergency
+    /// reclaim of images. The cheap steps: nothing the player can see changes.
+    StepLadder = 1,
+    /// (b) within `pager_bytes`: force a pager sweep (including the compressed pool). Costs
+    /// page-out time on the guest's threads, so it is only reached once (a) was not enough.
+    StepPager = 2,
+    /// (c) within `degrade_bytes`, or presents stuck for `stuck_degrade_ms`: switch optional
+    /// features off at run time (upscaler, frame generation, optional buffers) and lower the
+    /// internal resolution. Visible, so it is only taken once (b) has been tried.
+    StepDegrade = 3,
+    /// (d) BUILD 4 (item 3): the step for a run whose features are *already* off. `.813` logged
+    /// "degrade freed 0 MiB" at 83 MiB of headroom and then exited: the feature switch was a no-op
+    /// because A5 had them off from the start, so there was nothing between "degrade" and "exit".
+    /// This one changes what the renderer allocates - the lowest scene preset and the smallest
+    /// output, which is what the host targets are sized from - so it frees MiB rather than flags.
+    StepReduce = 4,
+    /// (e) presents stuck for `stuck_exit_ms` while at the limit: dump state, flush saves and exit
+    /// cleanly with a reason, instead of being killed by the console mid-save.
+    StepExit = 5,
+};
+
+/// Thresholds, in the units the console reports. Defaults are the plan's numbers; every one can be
+/// overridden from `bbport.ini` (item 15 asks for that explicitly).
+struct Thresholds {
+    bool enabled = true;
+    bool fast_enabled = true;
+    bool reduce_enabled = true;
+    std::uint64_t ladder_bytes = std::uint64_t{400} << 20;
+    std::uint64_t pager_bytes = std::uint64_t{250} << 20;
+    std::uint64_t degrade_bytes = std::uint64_t{150} << 20;
+    std::uint64_t stuck_degrade_ms = 3000;
+    std::uint64_t stuck_exit_ms = 10000;
+    /// BUILD 4 (item 3): the stronger-than-degrade threshold. Between `degrade_bytes` and
+    /// `reduce_bytes` the run degrades; at or below `reduce_bytes` it also takes step (d). 83 MiB of
+    /// headroom is where `.813` gave up, so 96 MiB is the number that would have caught it.
+    std::uint64_t reduce_bytes = std::uint64_t{96} << 20;
+    /// BUILD 4 (item 3): a check every 250 ms while the run is within this distance of the limit,
+    /// because a 1 s tick missed a burst that moved 527 MiB in under 2 s.
+    std::uint64_t fast_tick_bytes = std::uint64_t{600} << 20;
+    /// Minimum time between two steps. Each step costs milliseconds-to-seconds on the guest's
+    /// threads; running one per second while the app hovers at a threshold is how a watchdog
+    /// becomes the stall it was meant to survive.
+    std::uint64_t cooldown_ms = 2000;
+};
+
+/// `headroom` is `limit - usage` (0 when the limit is unknown, which disables the byte thresholds:
+/// a console that does not report a limit must not be degraded on arithmetic).
+/// `stuck_ms` is how long the present counter has been unchanged while the app is visible, 0 when it
+/// is moving or the app is in the background.
+[[nodiscard]] inline Step Decide(std::uint64_t headroom, std::uint64_t stuck_ms,
+                                 const Thresholds& thresholds) {
+    if (!thresholds.enabled) {
+        return StepNone;
+    }
+    // The exit is decided first, and it needs both halves: a 10 s stall *and* no headroom. A 10 s
+    // stall with memory to spare is a bug the stall report should still be able to catch, and
+    // exiting would take the log's evidence with it; a run that is at its ceiling and has stopped
+    // presenting is the one that will be killed mid-save if nothing does it cleanly.
+    if (stuck_ms >= thresholds.stuck_exit_ms && headroom <= thresholds.degrade_bytes) {
+        return StepExit;
+    }
+    if (thresholds.reduce_enabled && headroom <= thresholds.reduce_bytes) {
+        // The stronger step. A caller that has not degraded yet runs Degrade first in the same tick
+        // (see NextSteps*), so going straight from 400 MiB to 90 between two ticks still turns the
+        // features off before it lowers the preset.
+        return StepReduce;
+    }
+    if (headroom <= thresholds.degrade_bytes || stuck_ms >= thresholds.stuck_degrade_ms) {
+        return StepDegrade;
+    }
+    if (headroom <= thresholds.pager_bytes) {
+        return StepPager;
+    }
+    if (headroom <= thresholds.ladder_bytes) {
+        return StepLadder;
+    }
+    return StepNone;
+}
+
+/// True when `now_ms - last_step_ms` has reached the cooldown. `last_step_ms == 0` (never stepped)
+/// always passes: the first crossing is not delayed.
+[[nodiscard]] inline bool CooldownElapsed(std::uint64_t now_ms, std::uint64_t last_step_ms,
+                                         const Thresholds& thresholds) {
+    if (last_step_ms == 0) {
+        return true;
+    }
+    if (now_ms < last_step_ms) {
+        return true; // the clock went backwards (a wrap or a re-init): do not stall the watchdog
+    }
+    return now_ms - last_step_ms >= thresholds.cooldown_ms;
+}
+
+/// Steps that are worth repeating every cooldown while the condition holds: (a) and (b) find more
+/// each time memory becomes available. (c) and (d) do not - the features are already off, and the
+/// exit happens once - so they run only when they are a new, higher step than the last one.
+[[nodiscard]] inline bool Repeatable(Step step) {
+    return step == StepLadder || step == StepPager;
+}
+
+/// List every crossed recovery rung in ascending order. An abrupt drop from 600 to 90 MiB must
+/// not silently skip the release and pager. Repeating a cheap rung returns just that rung; the
+/// caller prevents duplicate queued/running work. Exit is handled immediately by the monitor.
+[[nodiscard]] inline unsigned NextSteps(Step decided, Step highest_scheduled, Step* out,
+                                         unsigned capacity) {
+    if (!capacity || decided == StepNone) return 0;
+    if (decided == StepExit) { out[0] = StepExit; return 1; }
+    if (decided <= highest_scheduled) {
+        out[0] = decided;
+        return 1;
+    }
+    unsigned n = 0;
+    const int first = highest_scheduled < StepLadder ? int(StepLadder) : int(highest_scheduled) + 1;
+    for (int rung = first; rung <= int(decided) && n < capacity; ++rung) out[n++] = Step(rung);
+    return n;
+}
+
+/// BUILD 4 (item 3): the tick interval that applies now. 250 ms near the limit, 1 s otherwise.
+[[nodiscard]] inline std::uint64_t TickMs(std::uint64_t headroom, const Thresholds& thresholds) {
+    return thresholds.fast_enabled && headroom <= thresholds.fast_tick_bytes ? 250 : 1000;
+}
+
+/// Whether this step should run now, given the last one that ran.
+///
+/// (a) and (b) are gated by the cooldown and repeat: each run may find memory the previous one
+/// could not. (c) and (d) are one-shot escalations: the features are already off, and the exit
+/// happens once. An escalation above the last step is *not* held back by the cooldown - waiting
+/// before the exit step is how a watchdog would spend the exit threshold on a resolution change.
+[[nodiscard]] inline bool ShouldRun(Step step, Step last_step, std::uint64_t now_ms,
+                                    std::uint64_t last_step_ms, const Thresholds& thresholds) {
+    if (step == StepNone) {
+        return false;
+    }
+    if (step > last_step) return true; // never delay an escalation behind a cooldown
+    if (!Repeatable(step)) return false;
+    return CooldownElapsed(now_ms, last_step_ms, thresholds);
+}
+
+/// `key=value` -> bytes, for `*_mb` ini settings. Returns `fallback` for anything unparseable, and
+/// clamps to [min_bytes, max_bytes] so a typo cannot disable a step or make it fire immediately.
+[[nodiscard]] inline std::uint64_t ParseMiB(const char* text, std::uint64_t fallback,
+                                            std::uint64_t min_bytes, std::uint64_t max_bytes) {
+    if (text == nullptr || text[0] == '\0') {
+        return fallback;
+    }
+    std::uint64_t value = 0;
+    bool any = false;
+    for (const char* p = text; *p != '\0'; ++p) {
+        if (*p < '0' || *p > '9') {
+            break;
+        }
+        value = value * 10 + std::uint64_t(*p - '0');
+        any = true;
+    }
+    if (!any) {
+        return fallback;
+    }
+    const std::uint64_t bytes = value << 20;
+    if (bytes < min_bytes) {
+        return min_bytes;
+    }
+    return bytes > max_bytes ? max_bytes : bytes;
+}
+
+/// `key=value` -> milliseconds, same rules.
+[[nodiscard]] inline std::uint64_t ParseMs(const char* text, std::uint64_t fallback,
+                                           std::uint64_t min_ms, std::uint64_t max_ms) {
+    if (text == nullptr || text[0] == '\0') {
+        return fallback;
+    }
+    std::uint64_t value = 0;
+    bool any = false;
+    for (const char* p = text; *p != '\0'; ++p) {
+        if (*p < '0' || *p > '9') {
+            break;
+        }
+        value = value * 10 + std::uint64_t(*p - '0');
+        any = true;
+    }
+    if (!any) {
+        return fallback;
+    }
+    if (value < min_ms) {
+        return min_ms;
+    }
+    return value > max_ms ? max_ms : value;
+}
+
+/// The step's name, for the log line each step prints.
+[[nodiscard]] inline const char* StepName(Step step) {
+    switch (step) {
+    case StepLadder: return "release (arenas, staging, images)";
+    case StepPager: return "pager sweep";
+    case StepDegrade: return "degrade (features off, resolution down)";
+    case StepReduce: return "reduce (lowest scene preset, smallest output)";
+    case StepExit: return "exit";
+    case StepNone: break;
+    }
+    return "none";
+}
+
+} // namespace BbWatchdog

diff --git a/xbox/scripts/crash-rvas.txt b/xbox/scripts/crash-rvas.txt
index b2d12a2..1a9fedf 100644
--- a/xbox/scripts/crash-rvas.txt

+#   Fault: exception 0xc00000fd at bloodborne.exe+0xc52457 (thread 5104)
+# The six rsp slots below it are the frames the fault handler could see on that stack.
+0xc52457
+0x8c96c
+0x9128c
+0x8d54d
+0x8d167
+0x8cf85
