`````diff
diff --git a/xbox/tests/arena_admission_policy_test.cpp b/xbox/tests/arena_admission_policy_test.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..5d348df
--- /dev/null
+++ b/xbox/tests/arena_admission_policy_test.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,25 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+#include "arena_admission_policy.h"
+#include <cassert>
+#include <cstdio>
+#include <limits>
+
+int main() {
+    using namespace BbArenaAdmission;
+    constexpr std::uint64_t M = 1ull << 20;
+    assert(BudgetFits(4800 * M, 5120 * M, 70 * M));
+    assert(!BudgetFits(4800 * M, 5120 * M, 70 * M + 1));
+    assert(!BudgetFits(5121 * M, 5120 * M, 16 * M));
+    assert(BudgetFits(0, 0, std::numeric_limits<std::uint64_t>::max()));
+    assert(!BudgetFits(std::numeric_limits<std::uint64_t>::max() - 10,
+                       std::numeric_limits<std::uint64_t>::max(), 16 * M));
+    // The live cap counts the replacement only once; the budget check counts the entire new
+    // allocation in addition to current usage, including all not-yet-retired old arenas.
+    assert(ProjectedLive(700 * M, 300 * M, 360 * M) == 760 * M);
+    assert(CapFits(700 * M, 300 * M, 360 * M));
+    assert(!CapFits(700 * M, 300 * M, 369 * M));
+    assert(CapFits(800 * M, 0, 800 * M, 0));
+    assert(ProjectedLive(std::numeric_limits<std::uint64_t>::max(), 0, 1) ==
+           std::numeric_limits<std::uint64_t>::max());
+    std::puts("arena admission arithmetic: all checks passed");
+}
diff --git a/xbox/tests/graphics_toggles_test.cpp b/xbox/tests/graphics_toggles_test.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..57c6456
--- /dev/null
+++ b/xbox/tests/graphics_toggles_test.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,266 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+// CI test for gpu/shim/bbport_effects.h and the three places that consume it.
+//
+// The failure this guards against is not a crash: it is a toggle that exists everywhere a player can
+// see it and nowhere the port can act on it. A row in the ini table with no patch name in
+// patches/Bloodborne.xml applies nothing; a patch name one character off the XML (`perf increase)`
+// vs `perf increase`) throws "patch not found" at start and takes the whole set with it; a runtime
+// toggle nobody parses writes `bloom=50` into bbport.ini and shows Off in the menu forever.
+//
+// So this reads the shipped files - bbport_effects.h, patches/Bloodborne.xml, scripts/patches.py,
+// bbport_settings.{h,cpp}, bbport_overlay.cpp, the post-process shader and its pass - and checks that
+// they agree with the table. It is a text check on purpose: it is checking the files that ship, not a
+// copy of them, and it needs nothing but the standard library.
+//
+// Run from the repository root (the CI test step runs at the checkout root); the file lookup also
+// walks up a few levels so it can be run from xbox/tests.
+
+#include "bbport_effects.h"
+
+#include <algorithm>
+#include <cstdio>
+#include <cstring>
+#include <string>
+#include <vector>
+
+namespace {
+
+int failures = 0;
+
+void Check(bool condition, const std::string& what) {
+    if (!condition) {
+        std::printf("FAIL: %s\n", what.c_str());
+        ++failures;
+    } else {
+        std::printf("ok: %s\n", what.c_str());
+    }
+}
+
+bool ReadFile(const std::string& path, std::string& out) {
+    if (FILE* file = std::fopen(path.c_str(), "rb")) {
+        char buffer[8192];
+        size_t read = 0;
+        while ((read = std::fread(buffer, 1, sizeof(buffer), file)) > 0) {
+            out.append(buffer, read);
+        }
+        std::fclose(file);
+        return true;
+    }
+    return false;
+}
+
+/// The repository root, found by walking up from the working directory.
+std::string Root() {
+    std::string base;
+    for (int up = 0; up < 5; ++up) {
+        const std::string prefix = base.empty() ? std::string{} : base;
+        std::string probe;
+        if (ReadFile(prefix + "patches/Bloodborne.xml", probe)) {
+            // "." not "": an empty prefix is the answer for the checkout root, and an empty return
+            // has to stay the one thing that means "not found".
+            return up == 0 ? std::string(".") : prefix;
+        }
+        base += "../";
+    }
+    return std::string{};
+}
+
+std::string Read(const std::string& root, const std::string& rel) {
+    std::string text;
+    const bool ok = ReadFile(root + "/" + rel, text);
+    Check(ok, "can read " + rel);
+    return text;
+}
+
+bool Contains(const std::string& haystack, const std::string& needle) {
+    return haystack.find(needle) != std::string::npos;
+}
+
+/// The `<Metadata ... Name="...">` values of a patches file, as quoted strings.
+std::vector<std::string> PatchNames(const std::string& xml) {
+    std::vector<std::string> names;
+    size_t at = 0;
+    while ((at = xml.find("Name=\"", at)) != std::string::npos) {
+        at += 6;
+        const size_t end = xml.find('"', at);
+        if (end == std::string::npos) {
+            break;
+        }
+        names.push_back(xml.substr(at, end - at));
+        at = end;
+    }
+    return names;
+}
+
+/// The single-line `'key':('off','on'),` entries of scripts/patches.py, keyed by the ini key. The
+/// value is the entry's text, so a test can ask "does this line name this patch?".
+std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> PythonEffects(const std::string& py) {
+    std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> entries;
+    size_t at = py.find("EFFECTS={");
+    if (at == std::string::npos) {
+        return entries;
+    }
+    size_t end = py.find("\n}", at);
+    if (end == std::string::npos) {
+        end = py.size();
+    }
+    const std::string block = py.substr(at, end - at);
+    size_t line = 0;
+    while (line < block.size()) {
+        size_t eol = block.find('\n', line);
+        if (eol == std::string::npos) {
+            eol = block.size();
+        }
+        std::string text = block.substr(line, eol - line);
+        line = eol + 1;
+        if (text.find('\'') == std::string::npos) {
+            continue;
+        }
+        const size_t colon = text.find("':(");
+        if (colon == std::string::npos) {
+            continue;
+        }
+        const size_t open = text.find('\'', 0);
+        entries.emplace_back(text.substr(open + 1, colon - open - 1), text);
+    }
+    return entries;
+}
+
+bool Has(const std::vector<std::string>& list, const std::string& value) {
+    return std::find(list.begin(), list.end(), value) != list.end();
+}
+
+const char* const kNull = nullptr;
+
+std::string Str(const char* text) {
+    return text ? std::string(text) : std::string();
+}
+
+} // namespace
+
+int main() {
+    const std::string root = Root();
+    if (root.empty()) {
+        std::printf("FATAL: cannot find the repository root (run from the checkout)\n");
+        return 1;
+    }
+
+    const std::string xml = Read(root, "patches/Bloodborne.xml");
+    const std::string py = Read(root, "scripts/patches.py");
+    const std::string settings_h = Read(root, "gpu/shim/bbport_settings.h");
+    const std::string settings_cpp = Read(root, "gpu/shim/bbport_settings.cpp");
+    const std::string overlay = Read(root, "gpu/shim/bbport_overlay.cpp");
+    const std::string shader = Read(root, "gpu/shadps4/video_core/host_shaders/post_process.frag");
+    const std::string pp_h =
+        Read(root, "gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/host_passes/pp_pass.h");
+    const std::string presenter = Read(root, "gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_presenter.cpp");
+
+    const std::vector<std::string> patch_names = PatchNames(xml);
+    const auto python_effects = PythonEffects(py);
+    Check(patch_names.size() > 50, "the patches file has its Metadata names");
+    Check(!python_effects.empty(), "scripts/patches.py has an EFFECTS table");
+
+    // --- the table itself ---------------------------------------------------
+    for (int e = 0; e < BbPortEffects::EffectCount; ++e) {
+        const auto& row = BbPortEffects::Effects[e];
+        const std::string key = Str(row.key);
+        const std::string label = Str(row.label);
+        Check(!key.empty(), "effect " + std::to_string(e) + " has a key");
+        Check(!label.empty(), "effect " + key + " has a menu label");
+        Check(row.patch_off != kNull || row.patch_on != kNull || row.runtime,
+              "effect " + key + " either patches something or is marked runtime");
+        for (int other = e + 1; other < BbPortEffects::EffectCount; ++other) {
+            if (key == Str(BbPortEffects::Effects[other].key)) {
+                Check(false, "effect key '" + key + "' is used twice");
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    // --- every patch name exists in the shipped patch set --------------------
+    for (int e = 0; e < BbPortEffects::EffectCount; ++e) {
+        const auto& row = BbPortEffects::Effects[e];
+        for (const char* name : {row.patch_off, row.patch_on}) {
+            if (!name) {
+                continue;
+            }
+            Check(Has(patch_names, name),
+                  std::string("patch '") + name + "' (" + Str(row.key) + ") exists in Bloodborne.xml");
+        }
+    }
+
+    // --- and the desktop patch compiler maps the same names to the same key --
+    for (int e = 0; e < BbPortEffects::EffectCount; ++e) {
+        const auto& row = BbPortEffects::Effects[e];
+        if (!row.patch_off && !row.patch_on) {
+            continue; // runtime feature: no patch, so nothing for patches.py to map
+        }
+        const std::string key = Str(row.key);
+        const auto found = std::find_if(python_effects.begin(), python_effects.end(),
+                                        [&](const auto& entry) { return entry.first == key; });
+        Check(found != python_effects.end(), "scripts/patches.py maps '" + key + "'");
+        if (found != python_effects.end()) {
+            for (const char* name : {row.patch_off, row.patch_on}) {
+                if (name) {
+                    Check(Contains(found->second, std::string("'") + name + "'"),
+                          "scripts/patches.py maps '" + key + "' to '" + name + "'");
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    // --- runtime toggles are parsed, stored and shown ------------------------
+    for (int t = 0; t < BbPortEffects::RuntimeToggleCount; ++t) {
+        const auto& row = BbPortEffects::RuntimeToggles[t];
+        const std::string key = Str(row.key);
+        const std::string field = Str(row.field);
+        Check(!key.empty() && !field.empty(), "runtime toggle " + std::to_string(t) + " is named");
+        // Parsed: a `key ==` comparison in the ini reader on the GPU side...
+        Check(Contains(settings_cpp, "key == \"" + key + "\""),
+              "bbport_settings.cpp parses '" + key + "'");
+        // ...and stored: a member of that exact name.
+        Check(Contains(settings_h, " " + field + "{") || Contains(settings_h, " " + field + " ={"),
+              "bbport_settings.h declares '" + field + "'");
+        // Written back, so a player's change survives the next start. `Save()` writes either the
+        // value (`upscaler=%s`, `preset=%d`) or a name derived from it, so the key in a format
+        // literal is the thing to look for.
+        Check(Contains(settings_cpp, key + "=") || Contains(settings_cpp, field + ".load()"),
+              "bbport_settings.cpp saves '" + key + "'");
+        // Shown: the menu text, which is how a player reaches it at all.
+        const std::string label = Str(row.label);
+        Check(Contains(overlay, label), "the menu shows '" + label + "'");
+    }
+
+    // The community port's spelling of the motion-vector toggle stays a working alias.
+    Check(Contains(settings_cpp, BbPortEffects::LessGhostingAlias),
+          "bbport_settings.cpp accepts the 'less_ghosting' spelling");
+
+    // --- bloom is not a placebo: it reaches the shader ----------------------
+    // The table claims bloom works. These three checks are what "works" means: the pass carries the
+    // value, the presenter fills it every frame, and the shader reads it. If any one is missing the
+    // row is a checkbox that changes nothing, which is exactly what this test exists to catch.
+    Check(Contains(pp_h, "float bloom"), "the post-process push constants carry 'bloom'");
+    Check(Contains(presenter, "pp_settings.bloom"), "vk_presenter fills pp_settings.bloom");
+    Check(Contains(shader, "pp.bloom"), "post_process.frag reads pp.bloom");
+    Check(Contains(shader, "float bloom;"), "post_process.frag declares bloom in its push constants");
+    // The layout contract: the block is four 4-byte members on the host side (asserted by
+    // static_assert in pp_pass.h) and must be four 4-byte members here. A `bool` in the shader is 4
+    // bytes today, but C++ `bool` is 1, so the two sides only stay in step while they agree on the
+    // spelling - hence the check rather than a comment.
+    const size_t block_at = shader.find("layout (push_constant) uniform settings {");
+    if (block_at == std::string::npos) {
+        Check(false, "post_process.frag has a push-constant block");
+    } else {
+        const std::string block = shader.substr(block_at, shader.find('}', block_at) - block_at);
+        Check(!Contains(block, "bool "), "the push-constant block uses uint, not bool, for flags");
+        Check(Contains(block, "hdr;") && Contains(block, "srgb_input;"),
+              "the push-constant block still carries both flags");
+    }
+
+    if (failures != 0) {
+        std::printf("%d check(s) failed\n", failures);
+        return 1;
+    }
+    std::printf("all checks passed (%d effects, %d runtime toggles)\n", BbPortEffects::EffectCount,
+                BbPortEffects::RuntimeToggleCount);
+    return 0;
+}
diff --git a/xbox/tests/ini_file_test.cpp b/xbox/tests/ini_file_test.cpp
index 3540edd..e324db9 100644
--- a/xbox/tests/ini_file_test.cpp
+++ b/xbox/tests/ini_file_test.cpp
@@ -148,0 +149,58 @@ void TestClearingPatchPath() {
+
+void TestTopLevelInsert() {
+    const std::string base = "# player settings\nupscaler=off\n\n[dump]\nuse_patch=1\n";
+    bool changed = false;
+    const std::string out = BbIni::SetTopLevel(base, "skip_intro", "1", &changed);
+    Check(changed, "a new top-level key reports a change");
+    const auto values = BbIni::Parse(out);
+    CheckEqual(values.at("skip_intro"), "1", "the key reads back");
+    CheckEqual(values.at("dump.use_patch"), "1", "the section below is untouched");
+    Check(out.find("[dump]\nuse_patch=1") != std::string::npos, "section order is kept");
+    Check(out.find("upscaler=off\nskip_intro=1") != std::string::npos,
+          "the key lands at the end of the top-level block");
+}
+
+void TestTopLevelReplace() {
+    const std::string base = "skip_intro=0\n# comment\nfps_cap=60\n[dump]\nskip_intro=9\n";
+    bool changed = false;
+    const std::string out = BbIni::SetTopLevel(base, "skip_intro", "1", &changed);
+    Check(changed, "changing a top-level key reports a change");
+    Check(out.find("# comment") != std::string::npos, "comments survive");
+    const auto values = BbIni::Parse(out);
+    CheckEqual(values.at("fps_cap"), "60", "other keys survive");
+    // A key of the same name inside a section keeps its own line; the bare key is the one written.
+    Check(out.find("[dump]\nskip_intro=9") != std::string::npos,
+          "the section's own key is not rewritten");
+    CheckEqual(BbIni::Parse(out).at("dump.skip_intro"), "9",
+               "and the section still answers for it");
+}
+
+void TestTopLevelDuplicate() {
+    const std::string base = "a=1\nskip_intro=0\nb=2\nskip_intro=0\n[c]\nk=v\n";
+    bool changed = false;
+    const std::string out = BbIni::SetTopLevel(base, "skip_intro", "1", &changed);
+    Check(changed, "a duplicate key reports a change");
+    size_t count = 0;
+    for (size_t at = out.find("skip_intro="); at != std::string::npos;
+         at = out.find("skip_intro=", at + 1)) {
+        ++count;
+    }
+    Check(count == 1, "duplicates collapse to one line");
+    CheckEqual(BbIni::Parse(out).at("skip_intro"), "1", "the surviving line wins");
+    CheckEqual(BbIni::Parse(out).at("c.k"), "v", "sections survive");
+}
+
+void TestTopLevelSameValue() {
+    const std::string base = "skip_intro=1\n[dump]\npatch_path=\n";
+    bool changed = true;
+    BbIni::SetTopLevel(base, "skip_intro", "1", &changed);
+    Check(!changed, "writing the same value reports no change");
+}
+
+void TestTopLevelEmptyFile() {
+    bool changed = false;
+    const std::string out = BbIni::SetTopLevel("", "skip_intro", "1", &changed);
+    Check(changed, "an empty file gains the key");
+    CheckEqual(out, std::string("skip_intro=1\n"), "and nothing else");
+}
+
@@ -161,0 +220,5 @@ int main() {
+    TestTopLevelInsert();
+    TestTopLevelReplace();
+    TestTopLevelDuplicate();
+    TestTopLevelSameValue();
+    TestTopLevelEmptyFile();
diff --git a/xbox/tests/storage_report_test.cpp b/xbox/tests/storage_report_test.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..74227d0
--- /dev/null
+++ b/xbox/tests/storage_report_test.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,172 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+// CI test for xbox/platform/storage_report.h: the storage report's portable half.
+//
+// The console half of this feature (which volumes exist, which of them the app may write to) needs
+// the console. What can be held here is the arithmetic and the rules that decide whether a player
+// is warned: the size formatting, the low-storage verdict, "pick the biggest writable volume other
+// than the one we are on", and the folder walk that answers "what is LocalState spending the
+// volume on". The walk is the part with a trap in it - a truncated walk must say so instead of
+// reporting a number that is silently too small.
+
+#include "storage_report.h"
+
+#include <cstdio>
+#include <cstdlib>
+#include <filesystem>
+#include <fstream>
+#include <string>
+#include <vector>
+
+namespace {
+
+int failures = 0;
+
+void Check(bool condition, const std::string& what) {
+    if (!condition) {
+        std::printf("FAIL: %s\n", what.c_str());
+        ++failures;
+    } else {
+        std::printf("ok: %s\n", what.c_str());
+    }
+}
+
+void CheckEqual(const std::string& actual, const std::string& expected, const std::string& what) {
+    Check(actual == expected, what + " (got '" + actual + "', expected '" + expected + "')");
+}
+
+BbStorage::Volume Make(char letter, std::uint64_t free_bytes, bool writable) {
+    BbStorage::Volume volume;
+    volume.letter = letter;
+    volume.total = free_bytes * 4;
+    volume.free = free_bytes;
+    volume.writable = writable;
+    return volume;
+}
+
+} // namespace
+
+int main() {
+    // --- formatting -------------------------------------------------------
+    CheckEqual(BbStorage::FormatBytes(0), "0 KiB", "zero");
+    CheckEqual(BbStorage::FormatBytes(1536), "1 KiB", "kilobytes");
+    CheckEqual(BbStorage::FormatBytes(std::uint64_t{512} << 20), "512 MiB", "megabytes");
+    CheckEqual(BbStorage::FormatBytes(std::uint64_t{4} << 30), "4.0 GiB", "gigabytes");
+
+    // --- the verdict ------------------------------------------------------
+    Check(!BbStorage::LowStorage(std::uint64_t{4} << 30), "4 GiB free is not low");
+    Check(BbStorage::LowStorage(std::uint64_t{867} << 20),
+          "867 MiB free is low (the .819 volume that capped the swap file to 483 MiB)");
+    Check(!BbStorage::LowStorage(BbStorage::kLowStorageBytes), "exactly the threshold is not low");
+    Check(BbStorage::LowStorage(BbStorage::kLowStorageBytes - 1), "one byte under is low");
+
+    // --- the volume with room, and the ones that only look like it --------
+    {
+        std::vector<BbStorage::Volume> volumes = {
+            Make('Q', std::uint64_t{867} << 20, true),    // LocalState: small, writable
+            Make('D', std::uint64_t{30} << 30, false),    // the big one: read-only to the app
+            Make('E', std::uint64_t{2} << 30, true),      // the real alternative
+            Make('F', 0, true),                          // writable, no space
+        };
+        const auto* best = BbStorage::BestWritable(volumes, 'Q');
+        Check(best != nullptr && best->letter == 'E',
+              "the biggest *writable* volume wins, not the biggest volume");
+        Check(BbStorage::BestWritable(volumes, 'E') != nullptr &&
+                  BbStorage::BestWritable(volumes, 'E')->letter == 'Q',
+              "the volume being skipped is never the answer");
+        std::vector<BbStorage::Volume> readonly = {Make('Q', std::uint64_t{1} << 30, true),
+                                                   Make('D', std::uint64_t{30} << 30, false)};
+        Check(BbStorage::BestWritable(readonly, 'Q') == nullptr,
+              "a read-only volume is never recommended, however large");
+    }
+
+    // Automatic swap must never pick USB, an unknown type, or LocalState while a fixed volume
+    // with usable space exists; most free space wins and D breaks ties.
+    {
+        using namespace BbStorage;
+        auto q = Make('Q', 88ull << 20, true);
+        auto d = Make('D', 76ull << 30, true); d.kind = VolumeKind::Fixed; d.bus = VolumeBus::NonUsb;
+        auto e = Make('E', 283ull << 30, true); e.kind = VolumeKind::Removable; e.bus = VolumeBus::UsbOrRemovable;
+        auto f = Make('F', 90ull << 30, true); f.kind = VolumeKind::Unknown;
+        std::vector<Volume> volumes{q, d, e, f};
+        const Volume* best = BestSwapVolume(volumes, 'Q', 384ull << 20);
+        Check(best && best->letter == 'D', "verified D beats larger removable E and unknown F");
+        volumes[2].kind = VolumeKind::Fixed; // USB HDDs can report DRIVE_FIXED
+        Check(BestSwapVolume(volumes, 'Q', 384ull << 20)->letter == 'D',
+              "a fixed-media USB disk is still excluded");
+        volumes[3].kind = VolumeKind::Fixed;
+        volumes[3].bus = VolumeBus::NonUsb;
+        best = BestSwapVolume(volumes, 'Q', 384ull << 20);
+        Check(best && best->letter == 'F', "the largest eligible fixed drive wins");
+        volumes[3].free = d.free;
+        best = BestSwapVolume(volumes, 'Q', 384ull << 20);
+        Check(best && best->letter == 'D', "D wins a tie");
+        volumes[1].writable = false; volumes[3].writable = false;
+        Check(BestSwapVolume(volumes, 'Q', 0) == nullptr,
+              "no eligible alternative means LocalState fallback");
+        volumes[1].writable = true; volumes[1].free = 384ull << 20;
+        Check(BestSwapVolume(volumes, 'Q', 384ull << 20) == nullptr,
+              "a fixed drive at its reserve is unusable");
+    }
+
+    // --- the folder walk --------------------------------------------------
+    {
+        std::error_code ec;
+        const auto root = std::filesystem::temp_directory_path(ec) / "bbport_storage_walk_test";
+        std::filesystem::remove_all(root, ec);
+        std::filesystem::create_directories(root / "Prepared" / "nested", ec);
+        std::filesystem::create_directories(root / "Logs", ec);
+        auto write = [](const std::filesystem::path& path, size_t bytes) {
+            std::ofstream out(path, std::ios::binary);
+            std::string block(bytes, 'x');
+            out.write(block.data(), (std::streamsize)block.size());
+        };
+        write(root / "Prepared" / "patches.bin", 4000);
+        write(root / "Prepared" / "nested" / "eboot.bin", 6000);
+        write(root / "Logs" / "loader.log.txt", 1000);
+        write(root / "bbport.ini", 500);
+
+        BbStorage::FolderSize total;
+        const auto folders = BbStorage::WalkFolders(root, total);
+        Check(folders.size() == 3, "three entries: two folders and one loose file");
+        std::uint64_t prepared = 0, logs = 0, ini = 0;
+        for (const auto& folder : folders) {
+            if (folder.name == "Prepared") prepared = folder.bytes;
+            if (folder.name == "Logs") logs = folder.bytes;
+            if (folder.name == "bbport.ini") ini = folder.bytes;
+        }
+        Check(prepared == 10000, "a folder's size includes its subfolders");
+        Check(logs == 1000, "a folder's size is its files");
+        Check(ini == 500, "a loose file is reported on its own line");
+        Check(total.bytes == 11500, "the total is the sum of the entries");
+        Check(!total.truncated, "a small tree is not truncated");
+
+        // A walk with a cap must say it was capped rather than return a small number as if it were
+        // the answer: that is the difference between a diagnostic and a lie.
+        BbStorage::FolderSize capped_total;
+        const auto capped = BbStorage::WalkFolders(root, capped_total, 2);
+        bool any_truncated = false;
+        for (const auto& folder : capped) any_truncated = any_truncated || folder.truncated;
+        Check(any_truncated, "a capped walk is marked truncated");
+        Check(capped_total.bytes <= total.bytes, "a capped walk never reports more than the full one");
+
+        std::filesystem::remove_all(root, ec);
+    }
+
+    // --- a missing root is not a crash ------------------------------------
+    {
+        BbStorage::FolderSize total;
+        const auto folders = BbStorage::WalkFolders(
+            std::filesystem::path{"Z:/bbport/does/not/exist"}, total);
+        Check(folders.empty() && total.bytes == 0, "a missing LocalState reports nothing");
+    }
+
+    // --- the warning text says what to do ---------------------------------
+    Check(!BbStorage::WarningText().empty(), "the warning text exists for the dialog");
+
+    if (failures != 0) {
+        std::printf("%d check(s) failed\n", failures);
+        return 1;
+    }
+    std::printf("storage report: all checks passed\n");
+    return 0;
+}
diff --git a/xbox/tests/swap_codec_test.cpp b/xbox/tests/swap_codec_test.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..0d4eae2
--- /dev/null
+++ b/xbox/tests/swap_codec_test.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,300 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+// CI test for the UWP swap page codec (xbox/platform/swap_codec.h).
+//
+// The console's swap file is written compressed because the device refused further pages at
+// 1,171 MiB (docs/hardware-test-23). A codec bug would corrupt guest memory, so this test round-
+// trips every kind of data the pager sees and checks the properties the runtime relies on:
+//   * every payload the compressor produces decompresses back to the identical page;
+//   * a page that does not compress is reported as such (0), and the caller's raw fallback is what
+//     actually stores it;
+//   * malformed input is rejected instead of overrunning the destination - the runtime turns that
+//     into a failed read, never into a silently wrong page.
+#include "swap_codec.h"
+
+#include <cstdio>
+#include <cstdlib>
+#include <random>
+#include <string>
+#include <vector>
+
+namespace {
+
+constexpr size_t kPage = 16384;
+constexpr size_t kScratchBytes = sizeof(int32_t) << UWP_LZ_HASH_BITS;
+
+int failures = 0;
+
+void Check(bool condition, const std::string& what) {
+    if (!condition) {
+        std::printf("FAIL: %s\n", what.c_str());
+        ++failures;
+    } else {
+        std::printf("ok: %s\n", what.c_str());
+    }
+}
+
+struct Codec {
+    std::vector<int32_t> scratch = std::vector<int32_t>(kScratchBytes / sizeof(int32_t));
+    std::vector<unsigned char> compressed = std::vector<unsigned char>(kPage * 2);
+    std::vector<unsigned char> restored = std::vector<unsigned char>(kPage);
+
+    // 1 when the page had to be stored raw (compressor refused), 0 when it fit, -1 on mismatch.
+    int RoundTrip(const std::vector<unsigned char>& page, const char* what) {
+        // The runtime passes the page size as the capacity, so a page that cannot shrink is
+        // refused (0) and stored raw instead.
+        const size_t packed = uwp_lz_compress(page.data(), page.size(), compressed.data(),
+                                              page.size(), scratch.data());
+        if (packed == 0) {
+            return 1;
+        }
+        if (packed >= page.size()) {
+            std::printf("FAIL: %s compressed to %zu of %zu bytes\n", what, packed, page.size());
+            ++failures;
+            return -1;
+        }
+        const size_t back = uwp_lz_decompress(compressed.data(), packed, restored.data(),
+                                              page.size());
+        if (back != page.size() || memcmp(restored.data(), page.data(), page.size()) != 0) {
+            std::printf("FAIL: %s did not round-trip (%zu bytes in, %zu out)\n", what, packed,
+                        back);
+            ++failures;
+            return -1;
+        }
+        return 0;
+    }
+};
+
+} // namespace
+
+int main() {
+    Codec codec;
+    std::mt19937_64 random{0x5eed5eed};
+
+    // 1. All zero: the pager elides these entirely, but the codec must handle them too.
+    {
+        std::vector<unsigned char> page(kPage, 0);
+        const int result = codec.RoundTrip(page, "an all-zero page");
+        Check(result == 0, "an all-zero page compresses and round-trips");
+        const size_t packed = uwp_lz_compress(page.data(), page.size(), codec.compressed.data(),
+                                              page.size(), codec.scratch.data());
+        Check(packed != 0 && packed < 128, "an all-zero page compresses to a handful of bytes");
+    }
+
+    // 2. Random data is incompressible: the codec must say so rather than emit something bigger.
+    {
+        std::vector<unsigned char> page(kPage);
+        for (auto& byte : page) {
+            byte = static_cast<unsigned char>(random());
+        }
+        const size_t packed = uwp_lz_compress(page.data(), page.size(), codec.compressed.data(),
+                                              page.size(), codec.scratch.data());
+        Check(packed == 0, "random data is refused rather than stored larger");
+        // And the raw fallback the runtime uses keeps it intact.
+        codec.compressed.assign(page.begin(), page.end());
+        Check(memcmp(codec.compressed.data(), page.data(), kPage) == 0,
+              "the raw fallback stores the page unchanged");
+    }
+
+    // 3. Page-shaped data: half pointers/ids, half zeros - what a guest heap page looks like.
+    {
+        std::vector<unsigned char> page(kPage);
+        for (size_t i = 0; i < kPage; i += 8) {
+            const uint64_t value = (i / 8) % 3 == 0 ? 0 : (random() & 0x0000'0FFF'FFFF'FFFF);
+            memcpy(page.data() + i, &value, sizeof(value));
+        }
+        const int result = codec.RoundTrip(page, "a heap-like page");
+        Check(result == 0, "a heap-like page compresses and round-trips");
+        const size_t packed = uwp_lz_compress(page.data(), page.size(), codec.compressed.data(),
+                                              page.size(), codec.scratch.data());
+        Check(packed != 0 && packed < kPage, "a heap-like page compresses to less than its size");
+    }
+
+    // 4. Text-like data with long runs and repeats.
+    {
+        std::vector<unsigned char> page(kPage);
+        const char* line = "UWP swap: pageable private=1209 pinned=0 MiB; page-out passes=437\n";
+        size_t at = 0;
+        while (at + strlen(line) <= kPage) {
+            memcpy(page.data() + at, line, strlen(line));
+            at += strlen(line);
+        }
+        while (at < kPage) {
+            page[at++] = 0;
+        }
+        const int result = codec.RoundTrip(page, "a text-like page");
+        Check(result == 0, "a text-like page compresses and round-trips");
+    }
+
+    // 5. Every length the compressor has to encode specially: tiny pages, and pages whose match
+    //    length crosses the 15 and 255 extension boundaries.
+    {
+        for (size_t size : {size_t{13}, size_t{14}, size_t{15}, size_t{16}, size_t{19}, size_t{20},
+                            size_t{31}, size_t{32}, size_t{270}, size_t{271}, size_t{300}}) {
+            std::vector<unsigned char> page(size, 0);
+            const size_t packed = uwp_lz_compress(page.data(), page.size(), codec.compressed.data(),
+                                                  page.size(), codec.scratch.data());
+            const bool ok = packed == 0 ? false : uwp_lz_decompress(codec.compressed.data(), packed,
+                                                                   codec.restored.data(),
+                                                                   page.size()) == page.size();
+            Check(ok, "a page of " + std::to_string(size) + " zero bytes round-trips");
+        }
+    }
+
+    // 6. A long run followed by noise: matches of several hundred bytes.
+    {
+        std::vector<unsigned char> page(kPage, 0xAB);
+        for (size_t i = kPage / 2; i < kPage; ++i) {
+            page[i] = static_cast<unsigned char>(random());
+        }
+        Check(codec.RoundTrip(page, "a long run followed by noise") == 0,
+              "a long run followed by noise round-trips");
+    }
+
+    // 7. Fifty random pages of varying character, to catch an off-by-one that a fixed shape hides.
+    {
+        int ok = 0;
+        for (int n = 0; n < 50; ++n) {
+            std::vector<unsigned char> page(kPage);
+            const unsigned kind = n % 5;
+            for (size_t i = 0; i < kPage; ++i) {
+                switch (kind) {
+                case 0:
+                    page[i] = static_cast<unsigned char>(random());
+                    break;
+                case 1:
+                    page[i] = static_cast<unsigned char>(i & 0xFF);
+                    break;
+                case 2:
+                    page[i] = static_cast<unsigned char>((i / 64) & 0x7);
+                    break;
+                case 3:
+                    page[i] = (i % 977) < 700 ? 0 : static_cast<unsigned char>(random());
+                    break;
+                default:
+                    page[i] = static_cast<unsigned char>(n);
+                    break;
+                }
+            }
+            // 0 = stored compressed, 1 = refused and stored raw by the caller; -1 is a failure.
+            if (codec.RoundTrip(page, "a varied page") >= 0) {
+                ++ok;
+            }
+        }
+        Check(ok == 50, "fifty varied pages all round-trip or are refused");
+    }
+
+    // 8. Malformed input must be rejected, not written past the end of the destination.
+    {
+        std::vector<unsigned char> restore(kPage, 0xCC);
+        // Literal length that runs past the block.
+        const unsigned char overrun[] = {0xF0, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x01};
+        Check(uwp_lz_decompress(overrun, sizeof(overrun), restore.data(), restore.size()) == 0,
+              "a literal run past the end of the block is rejected");
+        // Back-reference before the start of the block.
+        const unsigned char backref[] = {0x00, 0x01, 0x00};
+        Check(uwp_lz_decompress(backref, sizeof(backref), restore.data(), restore.size()) == 0,
+              "a back-reference before the start is rejected");
+        // A block that ends without filling the page.
+        const unsigned char short_block[] = {0x40, 'a', 'b', 'c', 'd'};
+        Check(uwp_lz_decompress(short_block, sizeof(short_block), restore.data(), restore.size()) ==
+                  0,
+              "a short block is rejected");
+        Check(restore[0] == 0xCC || restore[0] == 'a',
+              "the rejected input never wrote past the destination");
+    }
+
+    // 9. The raw marker is a length equal to the page size, so a *compressed* block of exactly that
+    //    size is indistinguishable from a raw one on the way back in. This is not hypothetical: the
+    //    `.437` console run stopped on `UWP promoted page integrity at 000000104D3B8000` after
+    //    65,475 stored pages, and the host search below lands on such a page within a few attempts
+    //    (docs/hardware-test-26). The runtime must store it raw, and the reader must get the page
+    //    back unchanged.
+    {
+        std::vector<unsigned char> page(kPage);
+        std::mt19937_64 hazard{0xb100d};
+        bool found = false;
+        for (int attempt = 0; attempt < 4000 && !found; ++attempt) {
+            for (auto& byte : page) {
+                byte = static_cast<unsigned char>(hazard());
+            }
+            const int copies = 14 + static_cast<int>(hazard() % 6);
+            for (int c = 0; c < copies; ++c) {
+                const size_t dst = (hazard() % (kPage - 16)) & ~size_t{7};
+                const size_t from = (hazard() % (kPage - 16)) & ~size_t{7};
+                memcpy(page.data() + dst, page.data() + from, 8);
+            }
+            const size_t packed = uwp_lz_compress(page.data(), kPage, codec.compressed.data() + 2,
+                                                  kPage, codec.scratch.data());
+            if (packed != kPage) {
+                continue;
+            }
+            found = true;
+            // The compressor really did produce a block the size of the page.
+            Check(true, "a nearly-incompressible page compresses to exactly the page size");
+            int raw = 0;
+            const size_t total = uwp_swap_encode_page(page.data(), kPage, codec.compressed.data(),
+                                                      kPage + 2, codec.scratch.data(), &raw);
+            const size_t stored = static_cast<size_t>(codec.compressed[0]) |
+                                  (static_cast<size_t>(codec.compressed[1]) << 8);
+            Check(raw == 1, "a block that is not smaller than the page is stored raw");
+            Check(total == kPage + 2 && stored == kPage,
+                  "the stored record carries the raw marker, not the compressed size");
+            // The runtime's read rule, applied to what was stored.
+            memset(codec.restored.data(), 0xCC, kPage);
+            if (stored == kPage) {
+                memcpy(codec.restored.data(), codec.compressed.data() + 2, kPage);
+            } else {
+                uwp_lz_decompress(codec.compressed.data() + 2, stored, codec.restored.data(),
+                                  kPage);
+            }
+            Check(memcmp(codec.restored.data(), page.data(), kPage) == 0,
+                  "the page comes back unchanged through the stored record");
+        }
+        Check(found, "the host search finds a page that compresses to exactly the page size");
+    }
+
+    // 10. The whole stored format, not just the codec: encode a page the way the pager does, then
+    //     read it back the way the pager does. Every shape, and no page may come back different.
+    {
+        std::mt19937_64 shapes{0x5a1ad};
+        size_t bad = 0;
+        for (int i = 0; i < 2000; ++i) {
+            std::vector<unsigned char> page(kPage);
+            const unsigned kind = static_cast<unsigned>(shapes() % 5);
+            for (size_t at = 0; at < kPage; ++at) {
+                switch (kind) {
+                case 0: page[at] = static_cast<unsigned char>(shapes()); break;
+                case 1: page[at] = 0; break;
+                case 2: page[at] = static_cast<unsigned char>((at / 64) & 0xFF); break;
+                case 3: page[at] = static_cast<unsigned char>(shapes() % 4); break;
+                default: page[at] = static_cast<unsigned char>((at % 13) ? 0 : shapes()); break;
+                }
+            }
+            int raw = 0;
+            const size_t total = uwp_swap_encode_page(page.data(), kPage, codec.compressed.data(),
+                                                      kPage + 2, codec.scratch.data(), &raw);
+            const size_t stored = static_cast<size_t>(codec.compressed[0]) |
+                                  (static_cast<size_t>(codec.compressed[1]) << 8);
+            if (total != stored + 2 || stored == 0 || stored > kPage) {
+                ++bad;
+                continue;
+            }
+            if (stored == kPage) {
+                memcpy(codec.restored.data(), codec.compressed.data() + 2, kPage);
+            } else if (uwp_lz_decompress(codec.compressed.data() + 2, stored, codec.restored.data(),
+                                         kPage) != kPage) {
+                ++bad;
+                continue;
+            }
+            if (memcmp(codec.restored.data(), page.data(), kPage) != 0) ++bad;
+        }
+        Check(bad == 0, "2000 stored records read back byte-identical");
+    }
+
+    if (failures != 0) {
+        std::printf("swap codec: %d check(s) failed\n", failures);
+        return 1;
+    }
+    std::printf("swap codec: all checks passed\n");
+    return 0;
+}
diff --git a/xbox/tests/swap_pool_accounting_test.cpp b/xbox/tests/swap_pool_accounting_test.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..5d6dda9
--- /dev/null
+++ b/xbox/tests/swap_pool_accounting_test.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,20 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+#include "swap_pool_accounting.h"
+#include <cassert>
+#include <cstdio>
+
+int main() {
+    unsigned char map[2]{};
+    const uint64_t p = BB_POOL_PAGE_SIZE;
+    assert(bb_pool_mark_pages(map, 2 * p, 3 * p, 1) == 3 * p);
+    // A failed decommit leaves the bits set; reuse cannot count the same physical pages twice.
+    assert(bb_pool_mark_pages(map, 2 * p, 3 * p, 1) == 0);
+    assert(bb_pool_mark_pages(map, 3 * p, 2 * p, 0) == 2 * p);
+    assert(bb_pool_mark_pages(map, 4 * p, 3 * p, 1) == 3 * p);
+    assert(bb_pool_mark_pages(map, 0, 16 * p, 0) == 4 * p);
+    assert(bb_pool_mark_pages(map, 0, 16 * p, 0) == 0);
+    assert(bb_pool_mark_pages(map, 7 * p, 3 * p, 1) == 3 * p); // crosses a bitmap byte
+    assert(bb_pool_net_saved(16 * p, 6 * p) == 10 * p);
+    assert(bb_pool_net_saved(3 * p, 6 * p) == 0);
+    std::puts("swap pool accounting: all checks passed");
+}
diff --git a/xbox/tests/swap_pool_windows_test.cpp b/xbox/tests/swap_pool_windows_test.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..8a1a674
--- /dev/null
+++ b/xbox/tests/swap_pool_windows_test.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,46 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+// Exercise the Windows decommit API the compressed pool uses. This is not an Xbox hardware test.
+#include <cstdio>
+#include <cstdlib>
+#ifdef _WIN32
+#ifndef _WIN32_WINNT
+#define _WIN32_WINNT 0x0A00
+#endif
+#include <windows.h>
+#include <memoryapi.h>
+// The standalone clang-cl test is not linked through the UWP target; this import lives in the
+// same WindowsApp library used by the real package rather than the desktop kernel32 import set.
+#pragma comment(lib, "WindowsApp.lib")
+
+static void Require(bool ok, const char* message) {
+    if (!ok) {
+        std::fprintf(stderr, "FAIL: %s (Win32 error %lu)\n", message, GetLastError());
+        std::exit(1);
+    }
+}
+int main() {
+    constexpr SIZE_T page = 4096, reservation = 65536;
+    auto* base = static_cast<unsigned char*>(
+        VirtualAllocFromApp(nullptr, reservation, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_NOACCESS));
+    Require(base != nullptr, "reserve");
+    Require(VirtualAllocFromApp(base, 2 * page, MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE) == base, "commit");
+    base[0] = 0x42;
+    base[page] = 0x73;
+    Require(VirtualFree(base, page, MEM_DECOMMIT) != 0, "VirtualFree MEM_DECOMMIT");
+    MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION info{};
+    Require(VirtualQuery(base, &info, sizeof(info)) != 0 && info.State == MEM_RESERVE,
+            "decommitted page remains reserved");
+    Require(VirtualQuery(base + page, &info, sizeof(info)) != 0 && info.State == MEM_COMMIT &&
+                base[page] == 0x73,
+            "neighbouring live blob remains committed and unchanged");
+    Require(VirtualAllocFromApp(base, page, MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE) == base,
+            "recommit freed page");
+    Require(base[0] == 0 && base[page] == 0x73, "recommitted page is zero; neighbour survived");
+    Require(VirtualFree(base, 0, MEM_RELEASE) != 0, "release reservation");
+    std::puts("Windows swap-pool decommit: all checks passed");
+}
+#else
+int main() {
+    std::puts("Windows swap-pool decommit: skipped on non-Windows host");
+}
+#endif
diff --git a/xbox/tests/texture_cache_policy_test.cpp b/xbox/tests/texture_cache_policy_test.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..b2e7d58
--- /dev/null
+++ b/xbox/tests/texture_cache_policy_test.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,395 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+// CI test for the texture cache's eviction policy (video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache_policy.h)
+// and the uid rule that makes a stored ImageId safe to re-check.
+//
+// The crash this pins down: on the console the collector freed an image that the rasterizer, the
+// presenter or the upscaler still held. Common::SlotId is a bare index without a generation, so the
+// next lookup either trips slot_vector.h ValidateIndex ("invalid or freed slot index") or reads
+// whichever image reused the slot. Two rules keep that from happening:
+//   1. an image that something refers to (bound / render target / scene proxy / video-out) is never
+//      freed by the collector, and it does not consume a deletion either;
+//   2. a stored id is only used again when the image's uid still matches, so a reused slot is
+//      detected rather than silently misread.
+#include "texture_cache_policy.h"
+
+#include <algorithm>
+#include <cstdio>
+#include <cstdlib>
+#include <string>
+#include <vector>
+
+namespace {
+
+int failures = 0;
+
+void Check(bool condition, const std::string& what) {
+    if (!condition) {
+        std::printf("FAIL: %s\n", what.c_str());
+        ++failures;
+    } else {
+        std::printf("ok: %s\n", what.c_str());
+    }
+}
+
+// A stand-in for the two facts the policy depends on: the pin flags and the uid of the image that
+// currently occupies a slot.
+struct FakeSlot {
+    bool allocated = false;
+    unsigned long long uid = 0;
+    bool bound = false, target = false, scene_proxy = false, vo_surface = false;
+    bool collected = false; ///< the draw being recorded already resolved this id
+    bool external = false;
+
+    BbGpu::ImagePinState Pin() const {
+        BbGpu::ImagePinState pin;
+        pin.bound = bound;
+        pin.target = target;
+        pin.scene_proxy = scene_proxy;
+        pin.vo_surface = vo_surface;
+        pin.collected = collected;
+        pin.external = external;
+        return pin;
+    }
+};
+
+// Mirrors TextureCache::IsImageCollected over the rasterizer's held set.
+bool Collected(const std::vector<int>& held, int id) {
+    return std::find(held.begin(), held.end(), id) != held.end();
+}
+
+// Mirrors TextureCache::TryGetImage(id, uid): uid 0 is a liveness check, otherwise the uid must
+// still match the image in that slot.
+bool StillOurs(const FakeSlot& slot, unsigned long long uid) {
+    if (!slot.allocated) {
+        return false;
+    }
+    return uid == 0 || slot.uid == uid;
+}
+
+void TestUnpinnedImageCanGo() {
+    FakeSlot slot;
+    slot.allocated = true;
+    slot.uid = 7;
+    Check(BbGpu::GcMayFreeImage(slot.Pin(), true), "an unbound, unused image is evictable");
+    Check(!BbGpu::GcMayFreeImage(slot.Pin(), false), "the age/pressure rules still have to select it");
+}
+
+void TestEachPinFlagHoldsTheImage() {
+    // One flag at a time: each on its own must stop the collector. These are exactly the checks
+    // ReclaimMemoryFor applies, which the GC pass was missing.
+    const char* names[] = {"bound", "render target", "scene proxy", "video-out surface",
+                           "collected by the draw", "stored external id/uid"};
+    for (int i = 0; i < 6; ++i) {
+        FakeSlot slot;
+        slot.allocated = true;
+        slot.uid = 11;
+        switch (i) {
+        case 0: slot.bound = true; break;
+        case 1: slot.target = true; break;
+        case 2: slot.scene_proxy = true; break;
+        case 3: slot.vo_surface = true; break;
+        case 4: slot.collected = true; break;
+        case 5: slot.external = true; break;
+        }
+        Check(BbGpu::ImagePinned(slot.Pin()), std::string("a live ") + names[i] + " pins the image");
+        Check(!BbGpu::GcMayFreeImage(slot.Pin(), true),
+              std::string("the collector keeps a ") + names[i]);
+    }
+}
+
+void TestExperimentalDiscard() {
+    BbGpu::ImagePinState pin;
+    using BbGpu::GcMayExperimentDrop;
+    Check(GcMayExperimentDrop(pin, true, true, true, true, true),
+          "opt-in critical stale tiled candidate can be considered");
+    Check(!GcMayExperimentDrop(pin, false, true, true, true, true), "experiment is opt-in");
+    Check(!GcMayExperimentDrop(pin, true, false, true, true, true), "not under critical pressure");
+    Check(!GcMayExperimentDrop(pin, true, true, false, true, true), "not tiled");
+    Check(!GcMayExperimentDrop(pin, true, true, true, false, true), "not GPU-written");
+    Check(!GcMayExperimentDrop(pin, true, true, true, true, false), "not old enough");
+    pin.external = true;
+    Check(!GcMayExperimentDrop(pin, true, true, true, true, true), "external id/uid stays pinned");
+    pin.external = false; pin.collected = true;
+    Check(!GcMayExperimentDrop(pin, true, true, true, true, true), "collected id stays pinned");
+}
+
+void TestCollectedIdsAreHeld() {
+    // The rasterizer resolves an id in pass 1 and binds it in pass 2; between the two the image has
+    // no binding flag set, so only the held set stops the collector from freeing it.
+    std::vector<int> held{4, 9};
+    Check(Collected(held, 4) && Collected(held, 9), "both ids the draw resolved are held");
+    Check(!Collected(held, 5), "an id the draw did not resolve is not held");
+    FakeSlot slot;
+    slot.allocated = true;
+    slot.collected = true;
+    Check(!BbGpu::GcMayFreeImage(slot.Pin(), true),
+          "the collector keeps an id the current draw resolved");
+    held.clear();
+    slot.collected = Collected(held, 4);
+    Check(BbGpu::GcMayFreeImage(slot.Pin(), true),
+          "after ResetBindings cleared the held set the image is evictable again");
+}
+
+void TestPinCombinations() {
+    FakeSlot slot;
+    slot.allocated = true;
+    Check(!BbGpu::ImagePinned(slot.Pin()), "nothing pinned when no flag is set");
+    slot.bound = slot.target = true;
+    Check(BbGpu::ImagePinned(slot.Pin()), "several flags still mean pinned");
+    slot.bound = slot.target = false;
+    slot.scene_proxy = true;
+    Check(BbGpu::ImagePinned(slot.Pin()), "a scene proxy alone is enough");
+}
+
+void TestPinnedImageDoesNotConsumeDeletions() {
+    // The collector must keep iterating past a pinned candidate (clean_up returns false), otherwise a
+    // queue of pinned entries would stall the pass: that regression left a 6 GB card over its
+    // critical mark with 0 evictions until ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory.
+    FakeSlot pinned;
+    pinned.allocated = true;
+    pinned.target = true;
+    FakeSlot freeable;
+    freeable.allocated = true;
+
+    unsigned deletions = 0;
+    for (const FakeSlot* slot : {&pinned, &pinned, &freeable}) {
+        if (!BbGpu::GcMayFreeImage(slot->Pin(), true)) {
+            continue; // kept, and no deletion is spent
+        }
+        ++deletions;
+    }
+    Check(deletions == 1, "only the freeable image counts against the deletion budget");
+}
+
+void TestStoredIdDetectsReusedSlot() {
+    // The upscaler stores scene_color together with the uid it had at the time. A slot reused by a
+    // different image must not be mistaken for the original.
+    FakeSlot slot;
+    slot.allocated = true;
+    slot.uid = 100;
+    const unsigned long long stored_uid = slot.uid;
+    Check(StillOurs(slot, stored_uid), "the same image is recognised");
+
+    slot.uid = 101; // a new image took the slot
+    Check(!StillOurs(slot, stored_uid), "a reused slot is rejected by the uid");
+
+    slot.allocated = false; // the slot was freed outright
+    Check(!StillOurs(slot, stored_uid), "a freed slot is rejected");
+    Check(!StillOurs(slot, 0), "a freed slot is rejected by the liveness check too");
+}
+
+void TestLivenessOnlyCheck() {
+    // Ids owned by another component (CameraMotion::Depth, a draw's parameters) have no uid here:
+    // uid 0 asks only whether the slot still exists.
+    FakeSlot slot;
+    slot.allocated = true;
+    slot.uid = 42;
+    Check(StillOurs(slot, 0), "a live slot passes the liveness check whatever its uid");
+    slot.allocated = false;
+    Check(!StillOurs(slot, 0), "a freed slot fails the liveness check");
+}
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// BUILD 2 (items 8-11): the classification that answers "why did the pass free nothing", the
+// write-back budget, the back-off and the hysteresis.
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+BbGpu::GcCandidateState CleanCandidate() {
+    return BbGpu::GcCandidateState{};
+}
+
+void TestClassificationOrder() {
+    const BbGpu::GcPassLimits limits;
+    // Nothing wrong: the candidate may go.
+    Check(BbGpu::GcClassifyCandidate(BbGpu::ImagePinState{}, CleanCandidate(), limits, false) ==
+              BbGpu::GcBlock::none,
+          "an unused, unwritten image is classified as freeable");
+
+    // A pin outranks every other reason: whatever else is wrong, the answer is "something holds it".
+    FakeSlot pinned;
+    pinned.bound = true;
+    BbGpu::GcCandidateState written_tiled = CleanCandidate();
+    written_tiled.gpu_written = written_tiled.tiled = true;
+    Check(BbGpu::GcClassifyCandidate(pinned.Pin(), written_tiled, limits, false) ==
+              BbGpu::GcBlock::pinned,
+          "a bound image is reported as pinned before any write-back rule");
+
+    // GPU-written and tiled: its contents exist only in VRAM and no host copy can reproduce the
+    // guest's tiling, so it stays. This is the column that explains `.717`.
+    Check(BbGpu::GcClassifyCandidate(BbGpu::ImagePinState{}, written_tiled, limits, false) ==
+              BbGpu::GcBlock::gpu_written_tiled,
+          "a GPU-written tiled image is retained");
+    // BB_GC_DROP_OLD=1 is the opt-in that lets it go unwritten, and it must not be needed for a
+    // linear image.
+    Check(BbGpu::GcClassifyCandidate(BbGpu::ImagePinState{}, written_tiled, limits, true) ==
+              BbGpu::GcBlock::none,
+          "with BB_GC_DROP_OLD the old tiled image may be dropped");
+}
+
+void TestUnsupportedLayout() {
+    BbGpu::GcPassLimits limits;
+    BbGpu::GcCandidateState candidate = CleanCandidate();
+    candidate.gpu_written = true;
+    candidate.layout_supported = false;
+    Check(BbGpu::GcClassifyCandidate(BbGpu::ImagePinState{}, candidate, limits, false) ==
+              BbGpu::GcBlock::unsupported_layout,
+          "an image the write-back path cannot express is kept, never half-written");
+    // eFMann PR #18: dropping it instead of writing it back is the same loss as dropping a tiled
+    // target, so the drop switch must not bypass the layout check on a linear image.
+    Check(BbGpu::GcClassifyCandidate(BbGpu::ImagePinState{}, candidate, limits, true) ==
+              BbGpu::GcBlock::unsupported_layout,
+          "BB_GC_DROP_OLD does not override an unsupported layout");
+}
+
+void TestWritebackBudgetAndPressureGate() {
+    BbGpu::GcPassLimits limits;
+    BbGpu::GcCandidateState candidate = CleanCandidate();
+    candidate.gpu_written = true;
+
+    // Below the pressure mark a write-back costs a GPU finish for no reason: the image is kept and
+    // counted in its own column, not silently treated as a budget failure.
+    candidate.writeback_allowed = false;
+    Check(BbGpu::GcClassifyCandidate(BbGpu::ImagePinState{}, candidate, limits, false) ==
+              BbGpu::GcBlock::not_pressured,
+          "below the pressure mark a GPU-written image is not copied out");
+    // The pressure gate is checked before the budget: an exhausted budget must not change the answer.
+    candidate.writebacks_done = limits.writebacks + 10;
+    Check(BbGpu::GcClassifyCandidate(BbGpu::ImagePinState{}, candidate, limits, false) ==
+              BbGpu::GcBlock::not_pressured,
+          "the pressure gate is reported even with the budget spent");
+
+    candidate.writeback_allowed = true;
+    candidate.writebacks_done = 0;
+    Check(BbGpu::GcClassifyCandidate(BbGpu::ImagePinState{}, candidate, limits, false) ==
+              BbGpu::GcBlock::none,
+          "under pressure with budget left the image may be written back and freed");
+    candidate.writebacks_done = limits.writebacks - 1;
+    Check(BbGpu::GcClassifyCandidate(BbGpu::ImagePinState{}, candidate, limits, false) ==
+              BbGpu::GcBlock::none,
+          "the last write-back of the budget is still allowed");
+    candidate.writebacks_done = limits.writebacks;
+    Check(BbGpu::GcClassifyCandidate(BbGpu::ImagePinState{}, candidate, limits, false) ==
+              BbGpu::GcBlock::writeback_budget,
+          "a pass never spends more than its four write-backs");
+    // A caller that has spent four write-backs and a positive count must compare, not guess.
+    limits.writebacks = 0;
+    Check(BbGpu::GcClassifyCandidate(BbGpu::ImagePinState{}, CleanCandidate(), limits, false) ==
+              BbGpu::GcBlock::none,
+          "a write-back budget of zero does not block an image nobody has to copy out");
+}
+
+void TestBackOff() {
+    const BbGpu::GcPassLimits limits; // 32 MiB useful, 64 MiB growth
+    const unsigned long long mib = 1ull << 20;
+    Check(BbGpu::GcShouldBackOff(0, 0, limits), "a pass that freed nothing with no growth is skipped");
+    Check(BbGpu::GcShouldBackOff(31 * mib, 63 * mib, limits),
+          "just under both marks still backs off");
+    Check(!BbGpu::GcShouldBackOff(32 * mib, 0, limits),
+          "a pass that freed 32 MiB is worth running again");
+    Check(!BbGpu::GcShouldBackOff(0, 64 * mib, limits),
+          "using 64 MiB more since the last pass earns a new walk");
+    Check(!BbGpu::GcShouldBackOff(200 * mib, 0, limits), "a large reclaim is not backed off");
+}
+
+void TestHysteresis() {
+    const unsigned long long trigger = 2048ull << 20;   // 2 GiB mark
+    const unsigned long long hysteresis = 128ull << 20; // 128 MiB gap
+    const unsigned long long mib = 1ull << 20;
+
+    Check(BbGpu::GcHysteresisActive(trigger, trigger, hysteresis, false),
+          "reaching the trigger starts the collector");
+    Check(!BbGpu::GcHysteresisActive(trigger - 1 * mib, trigger, hysteresis, false),
+          "below the trigger an idle collector stays idle");
+
+    // Once running it keeps going past the trigger, all the way down to trigger - hysteresis.
+    Check(BbGpu::GcHysteresisActive(trigger - 1 * mib, trigger, hysteresis, true),
+          "the collector does not stop the instant it touches the trigger");
+    Check(BbGpu::GcHysteresisActive(trigger - 127 * mib, trigger, hysteresis, true),
+          "one MiB above the target is still collecting");
+    Check(!BbGpu::GcHysteresisActive(trigger - hysteresis, trigger, hysteresis, true),
+          "reaching the target stops the collector");
+    Check(!BbGpu::GcHysteresisActive(trigger - 200 * mib, trigger, hysteresis, true),
+          "well below the target it stays stopped");
+    // The gap is what stops a run sitting on the mark from evicting and re-uploading every pass.
+    Check(!BbGpu::GcHysteresisActive(trigger - 64 * mib, trigger, hysteresis, false),
+          "half-way up the hysteresis band does not restart it");
+    // A trigger below the hysteresis (a very low limit) must not underflow.
+    Check(!BbGpu::GcHysteresisActive(0, 64 * mib, 128 * mib, true),
+          "a trigger smaller than the hysteresis does not wrap around");
+}
+
+void TestPassAccounting() {
+    // Every examined candidate ends in exactly one column, so the report line adds up: a pass that
+    // freed nothing can be read off the blocked columns. This is the check that `.717`'s log lacked.
+    BbGpu::GcPassLimits limits;
+    struct Case {
+        BbGpu::ImagePinState pin;
+        BbGpu::GcCandidateState candidate;
+    };
+    std::vector<Case> cases(10);
+    cases[0].pin.target = true;                                  // pinned
+    cases[1].candidate.gpu_written = cases[1].candidate.tiled = true; // tiled, retained
+    cases[2] = cases[1];                                          // tiled, retained
+    cases[3].candidate.gpu_written = true;                         // freeable
+    cases[4].candidate.gpu_written = true;
+    cases[4].candidate.layout_supported = false;                   // unsupported layout
+    cases[5].candidate.gpu_written = true;
+    cases[5].candidate.writeback_allowed = false;                  // not pressured
+    for (int i = 6; i < 10; ++i) {
+        cases[i].candidate.gpu_written = true;                     // written back until the budget ends
+    }
+    unsigned long long freed = 0, pinned = 0, tiled = 0, budget = 0, none_pressure = 0, layout = 0;
+    unsigned writebacks = 0;
+    for (const Case& c : cases) {
+        switch (BbGpu::GcClassifyCandidate(c.pin, BbGpu::GcCandidateState{c.candidate}, limits,
+                                          false)) {
+        case BbGpu::GcBlock::pinned: ++pinned; break;
+        case BbGpu::GcBlock::gpu_written_tiled: ++tiled; break;
+        case BbGpu::GcBlock::unsupported_layout: ++layout; break;
+        case BbGpu::GcBlock::not_pressured: ++none_pressure; break;
+        case BbGpu::GcBlock::writeback_budget: ++budget; break;
+        case BbGpu::GcBlock::none:
+            // The pass may spend one write-back; when the budget is gone the same image is blocked.
+            if (writebacks < limits.writebacks) {
+                ++writebacks;
+                ++freed;
+            } else {
+                ++budget;
+            }
+            break;
+        case BbGpu::GcBlock::recent: break;
+        }
+    }
+    Check(freed == 4, "four candidates were freed, each by one write-back");
+    Check(pinned == 1 && tiled == 2 && layout == 1 && none_pressure == 1,
+          "each blocked candidate lands in its own column");
+    Check(budget == 1, "the candidate past the write-back budget is reported as such");
+    Check(freed + pinned + tiled + budget + none_pressure + layout == cases.size(),
+          "examined equals freed plus every blocked column");
+}
+
+} // namespace
+
+int main() {
+    TestUnpinnedImageCanGo();
+    TestEachPinFlagHoldsTheImage();
+    TestExperimentalDiscard();
+    TestCollectedIdsAreHeld();
+    TestPinCombinations();
+    TestPinnedImageDoesNotConsumeDeletions();
+    TestStoredIdDetectsReusedSlot();
+    TestLivenessOnlyCheck();
+    // Build 2: why a selected candidate is kept, the write-back budget, back-off and hysteresis.
+    TestClassificationOrder();
+    TestUnsupportedLayout();
+    TestWritebackBudgetAndPressureGate();
+    TestBackOff();
+    TestHysteresis();
+    TestPassAccounting();
+    if (failures != 0) {
+        std::printf("%d check(s) failed\n", failures);
+        return EXIT_FAILURE;
+    }
+    std::printf("texture cache policy: all checks passed\n");
+    return EXIT_SUCCESS;
+}
diff --git a/xbox/tests/watchdog_policy_test.cpp b/xbox/tests/watchdog_policy_test.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..e443375
--- /dev/null
+++ b/xbox/tests/watchdog_policy_test.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,186 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+// CI test for the recovery watchdog's rules (xbox/platform/watchdog_policy.h).
+//
+// The watchdog is what a run at the app's memory limit relies on, and its failure modes are quiet:
+// a threshold parsed a factor of 1024 wrong, a step that repeats every second and becomes the stall
+// it was meant to survive, a cooldown that delays the exit step behind a resolution change, or an
+// order that runs the pager before the cheap release. None of those crash, so none of them is caught
+// anywhere else.
+#include "watchdog_policy.h"
+
+#include <cstdio>
+#include <cstdlib>
+#include <string>
+
+namespace {
+
+int failures = 0;
+constexpr unsigned long long MiB = 1ull << 20;
+
+void Check(bool condition, const std::string& what) {
+    if (!condition) {
+        std::printf("FAIL: %s\n", what.c_str());
+        ++failures;
+    } else {
+        std::printf("ok: %s\n", what.c_str());
+    }
+}
+
+void TestThresholdsAreBytes() {
+    // The plan's numbers: 400 / 250 / 150 MiB and a 1 s check with a ~2 s cooldown per step.
+    const BbWatchdog::Thresholds defaults;
+    Check(defaults.ladder_bytes == 400 * MiB, "the ladder threshold is 400 MiB");
+    Check(defaults.pager_bytes == 250 * MiB, "the pager threshold is 250 MiB");
+    Check(defaults.degrade_bytes == 150 * MiB, "the degrade threshold is 150 MiB");
+    Check(defaults.stuck_degrade_ms == 3000, "presents stuck 3 s degrades");
+    Check(defaults.stuck_exit_ms == 10000, "presents stuck 10 s exits");
+    Check(defaults.cooldown_ms == 2000, "each step is at least 2 s apart");
+}
+
+void TestStepOrder() {
+    const BbWatchdog::Thresholds t;
+    // Plenty of room: nothing runs. A watchdog that reclaims while the app is calm is a stutter.
+    Check(BbWatchdog::Decide(2000 * MiB, 0, t) == BbWatchdog::StepNone,
+          "2,000 MiB of headroom: no step");
+    Check(BbWatchdog::Decide(400 * MiB + 1, 0, t) == BbWatchdog::StepNone,
+          "just above the ladder threshold: no step");
+    Check(BbWatchdog::Decide(400 * MiB, 0, t) == BbWatchdog::StepLadder,
+          "at the ladder threshold: the cheap release runs");
+    Check(BbWatchdog::Decide(150 * MiB + 1, 0, t) == BbWatchdog::StepPager,
+          "between pager and degrade: the pager sweeps, not the release");
+    Check(BbWatchdog::Decide(150 * MiB, 0, t) == BbWatchdog::StepDegrade,
+          "at the degrade threshold: features go off");
+    Check(BbWatchdog::Decide(1 * MiB, 0, t) == BbWatchdog::StepReduce,
+          "at the limit with presents moving: reduce, never exit on arithmetic alone");
+    Check(BbWatchdog::Decide(0, 0, t) == BbWatchdog::StepReduce,
+          "a limit of zero headroom is not an exit");
+
+    // A stall escalates on its own, whatever the headroom says.
+    Check(BbWatchdog::Decide(2000 * MiB, 3000, t) == BbWatchdog::StepDegrade,
+          "presents stuck 3 s degrades even with memory to spare");
+    Check(BbWatchdog::Decide(2000 * MiB, 10000, t) == BbWatchdog::StepDegrade,
+          "a 10 s stall with memory to spare degrades but does not exit");
+    Check(BbWatchdog::Decide(100 * MiB, 10000, t) == BbWatchdog::StepExit,
+          "the exit outranks the degrade at the limit");
+    Check(BbWatchdog::Decide(100 * MiB, 2999, t) == BbWatchdog::StepDegrade,
+          "one millisecond short of the stall threshold does not exit");
+}
+
+void TestFastTickAndSkippedRungs() {
+    using namespace BbWatchdog;
+    Thresholds t;
+    Check(TickMs(600 * MiB, t) == 250 && TickMs(600 * MiB + 1, t) == 1000,
+          "250 ms inside 600 MiB, 1 s outside");
+    t.fast_enabled = false;
+    Check(TickMs(1, t) == 1000, "fast tick has an independent off switch");
+    Check(Decide(96 * MiB, 3000, t) == StepReduce,
+          "a stall cannot mask the stronger low-memory step");
+    t.reduce_enabled = false;
+    Check(Decide(1 * MiB, 0, t) == StepDegrade, "reduce has an independent off switch");
+    Step steps[4]{};
+    Check(NextSteps(StepReduce, StepNone, steps, 4) == 4 &&
+          steps[0] == StepLadder && steps[1] == StepPager &&
+          steps[2] == StepDegrade && steps[3] == StepReduce,
+          "a rapid burst queues all four steps in order");
+    Check(NextSteps(StepReduce, StepPager, steps, 4) == 2 &&
+          steps[0] == StepDegrade && steps[1] == StepReduce,
+          "already scheduled steps are not scheduled again");
+    Check(NextSteps(StepReduce, StepNone, steps, 2) == 2 &&
+          steps[0] == StepLadder && steps[1] == StepPager,
+          "a small queue returns a bounded prefix for the next tick");
+    Check(ShouldRun(StepPager, StepLadder, 10001, 10000, t),
+          "escalation from release to pager bypasses cooldown");
+}
+
+void TestDisabledAndUnknownLimit() {
+    BbWatchdog::Thresholds t;
+    t.enabled = false;
+    Check(BbWatchdog::Decide(0, 60000, t) == BbWatchdog::StepNone,
+          "watchdog=0 disables every step, including the exit");
+    // An unknown limit is represented by UINT64_MAX headroom by the caller.
+    BbWatchdog::Thresholds live;
+    Check(BbWatchdog::Decide(~0ull, 0, live) == BbWatchdog::StepNone,
+          "an unknown limit does not trigger memory thresholds");
+}
+
+void TestCooldown() {
+    const BbWatchdog::Thresholds t;
+    Check(BbWatchdog::CooldownElapsed(5000, 0, t), "the first step is never delayed");
+    Check(!BbWatchdog::CooldownElapsed(6000, 5000, t), "1 s after a step is inside the 2 s cooldown");
+    Check(BbWatchdog::CooldownElapsed(7000, 5000, t), "2 s after a step the next one may run");
+    Check(BbWatchdog::CooldownElapsed(10, 5000, t), "a clock that went backwards does not stall it");
+}
+
+void TestShouldRun() {
+    const BbWatchdog::Thresholds t;
+    using namespace BbWatchdog;
+    // Nothing to do.
+    Check(!ShouldRun(StepNone, StepNone, 10000, 0, t), "no step runs for 'none'");
+    // The release repeats, once per cooldown: each run may find arenas that were in flight before.
+    Check(ShouldRun(StepLadder, StepLadder, 10000, 0, t), "the release runs the first time");
+    Check(!ShouldRun(StepLadder, StepLadder, 11000, 10000, t), "it does not repeat inside the cooldown");
+    Check(ShouldRun(StepLadder, StepLadder, 12000, 10000, t), "it repeats after the cooldown");
+    // The pager likewise.
+    Check(ShouldRun(StepPager, StepPager, 30000, 20000, t), "the pager sweep repeats after the cooldown");
+    // Escalation is not delayed: a run that is about to be killed must not wait for a cooldown.
+    Check(ShouldRun(StepDegrade, StepLadder, 10001, 10000, t),
+          "degrade follows the release immediately");
+    Check(ShouldRun(StepExit, StepDegrade, 10001, 10000, t),
+          "the exit follows the degrade immediately");
+    // One-shot: the features are already off, and the exit happens once.
+    Check(!ShouldRun(StepDegrade, StepDegrade, 100000, 0, t), "degrade does not repeat");
+    Check(!ShouldRun(StepExit, StepExit, 100000, 0, t), "the exit does not repeat");
+    // And a lower one-shot step never re-runs over a higher one.
+    Check(!ShouldRun(StepDegrade, StepExit, 100000, 0, t), "a lower one-shot step never re-runs");
+}
+
+void TestParsing() {
+    using namespace BbWatchdog;
+    // `bbport.ini` spellings, and the typos a player makes.
+    Check(ParseMiB("400", 1, 64 * MiB, 4096 * MiB) == 400 * MiB, "400 -> 400 MiB");
+    Check(ParseMiB("  400", 1, 64 * MiB, 4096 * MiB) == 1, "a leading space is not a number: fallback");
+    Check(ParseMiB("", 7 * MiB, 64 * MiB, 4096 * MiB) == 7 * MiB, "an empty value takes the fallback");
+    Check(ParseMiB(nullptr, 7 * MiB, 64 * MiB, 4096 * MiB) == 7 * MiB, "a missing key takes the fallback");
+    Check(ParseMiB("abc", 7 * MiB, 64 * MiB, 4096 * MiB) == 7 * MiB, "a word takes the fallback");
+    Check(ParseMiB("16", 7 * MiB, 64 * MiB, 4096 * MiB) == 64 * MiB, "below the floor it clamps up");
+    Check(ParseMiB("999999", 7 * MiB, 64 * MiB, 4096 * MiB) == 4096 * MiB, "above the ceiling it clamps down");
+    Check(ParseMiB("400mb", 1, 64 * MiB, 4096 * MiB) == 400 * MiB, "a trailing unit is ignored");
+
+    Check(ParseMs("3000", 1, 200, 60000) == 3000, "3000 -> 3000 ms");
+    Check(ParseMs("10", 1, 200, 60000) == 200, "below the floor it clamps up");
+    Check(ParseMs("999999", 1, 200, 60000) == 60000, "above the ceiling it clamps down");
+    Check(ParseMs("", 2000, 200, 60000) == 2000, "an empty value takes the fallback");
+}
+
+void TestThresholdsFromIni() {
+    // The four keys item 15 asks for, read the way the watchdog reads them.
+    BbWatchdog::Thresholds t;
+    t.ladder_bytes = BbWatchdog::ParseMiB("512", t.ladder_bytes, 64 * MiB, 2048 * MiB);
+    t.pager_bytes = BbWatchdog::ParseMiB("300", t.pager_bytes, 64 * MiB, 2048 * MiB);
+    t.degrade_bytes = BbWatchdog::ParseMiB("200", t.degrade_bytes, 32 * MiB, 1024 * MiB);
+    t.cooldown_ms = BbWatchdog::ParseMs("500", t.cooldown_ms, 200, 30000);
+    Check(t.ladder_bytes == 512 * MiB && t.pager_bytes == 300 * MiB && t.degrade_bytes == 200 * MiB,
+          "the three byte thresholds come from the ini");
+    Check(t.cooldown_ms == 500, "so does the cooldown");
+    Check(BbWatchdog::Decide(180 * MiB, 0, t) == BbWatchdog::StepDegrade,
+          "with 200 MiB for degrade, 180 MiB of headroom degrades");
+}
+
+} // namespace
+
+int main() {
+    TestThresholdsAreBytes();
+    TestStepOrder();
+    TestFastTickAndSkippedRungs();
+    TestDisabledAndUnknownLimit();
+    TestCooldown();
+    TestShouldRun();
+    TestParsing();
+    TestThresholdsFromIni();
+    if (failures != 0) {
+        std::printf("%d check(s) failed\n", failures);
+        return EXIT_FAILURE;
+    }
+    std::printf("watchdog policy: all checks passed\n");
+    return EXIT_SUCCESS;
+}
`````
